paper_title: A technical review and guide to RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization
paper_abstract: RNA-fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is a powerful tool to visualize target mRNA transcripts in cultured cells, tissue sections or whole-mount preparations. As the technique has been developed over time, an ever-increasing number of divergent protocols have been published. There is now a broad selection of options available to facilitate proper tissue preparation, hybridization, and post-hybridization background removal to achieve optimal results. Here we review the technical aspects of RNA-FISH, examining the most common methods associated with different sample types including cytological preparations and whole-mounts. We discuss the application of commonly used reagents for tissue preparation, hybridization, and post-hybridization washing and provide explanations of the functional roles for each reagent. We also discuss the available probe types and necessary controls to accurately visualize gene expression. Finally, we review the most recent advances in FISH technology that facilitate both highly multiplexed experiments and signal amplification for individual targets. Taken together, this information will guide the methods development process for investigators that seek to perform FISH in organisms that lack documented or optimized protocols.
review_content: Reviewer 1: (Anonymous) Minor comments by line: Line 86 “…to label DNA the same cell types…” it seems a word is missing here This typo has been fixed and the sentence now reads “…to label DNA in the same cells from the same species.” Line 111, 127: I would have liked to see Raj 2006 cited in the introduction on the smFISH. Moreso than the later Nature Methods paper (Raj 2008, cited line 111 and 127), this 2006 first introduced the significant tile and high contrast smFISH which expanded dramatically in the years following. We have added the Raj 2006 paper to the introduction and referenced this early use of multiple singly-labeled probes. Line 156-8: A reference here could help, even if the author does not have space to elaborate more “…but we will not focus on this aspect here. However, characteristics such as the GC content, the propensity to form secondary structures, the overall length and specificity and probe quantity and quality must be considered”. The recent proliferation of purely synthetic probes in place of cloning derived probes has provided much greater control of characteristics such as GC content and the propensity to form secondary structures. E.g. Beliveau et al 2012 PNAS. A reference has been added to this point, and a follow-up point has been made with respect to the control that is given to the user with the rise of synthetic probes. 185 – I recommend broadening the time range, many modern protocols use shorter fixation for cultured cells, e.g. 10 minutes. (Chen…Zhuang 2015 ‘MERFISH’ on human cultured cells) or Skinner…Golding 2013 for e Coli. We have broadened the time range and cited the Raj Lab Turbo-FISH paper as an example of a 10 minute fixation in cultured cells. ~214 on alcohol fixation. Something could be said about “Turbo-FISH” protocol – a fast methanol based fixation. We have added a reference to the Turbo-FISH protocol in this paragraph as an example of a fast alcohol-based fixation. 229 – in discussion of ‘protection of native protein structure’ – it could be mentioned that alcohol solutions are generally denaturing and disrupt native protein structure, which can lead to loss of antigenicity for immuno FISH protocols (protein + RNA detection). The same is true of heat fix. GA fix can significantly reduce the permeability by providing to dense a crosslinking. We have included that alcohol fixatives and heat are generally not suitable for combined immunohistochemistry and FISH protocols (in respective paragraphs on alcohol fixation and fixation temperature). Line 244 – I would not recommend proteinase K treatment for Drosophila embryos. I think a more thorough search of the recent smFISH literature in Drosophila (not cited) will bear this out. See Pare…McGinnis 2009 Curr Bio, Boettiger…Levine 2009 Science, Boettiger…Levine 2013 Cell Reports, Little…Gregor Cell 2013, 2011 PLoS Bio, I could go on. Some discussion of the Pepsin treatment (in place of proteinase K) as developed more recently by the Singer lab could go well alongside the proteinase K discussion. (Bauxbaum…Singer 2014 Science). Many labs are indeed moving away from the use of pro-K with Drosophila embryos (and we now cite some of these), however, there are recent high-profile papers that still reference the use of pro-K on Drosophila (for example Trcek et al. 2017 Nature Protocols). Therefore, we have chosen not to remove the mention of pro-K with Drosophila embryos. This being said, we have added some discussion about the alternative acetone and pepsin treatments so that readers can grasp the full range of available options. As for some of the other papers that only use detergent-based methods of permeabilization, we have mentioned detergent-based methods in a later paragraph as follows: “Protease-free detergent-based methods have also been successful for permeabilization of Drosophila embryos (Boettiger & Levine, 2013).” Line 286: 50% formamide – 10 -50% might be a more accurate way to put it. For example see the high resolution smFISH protocol described by Raj et al (2006 or 2008), and built on in recent smFISH work (see work from Long Cai and Xiaowei Zhuang’s groups on highly multiplexed smFISH protocols) We agree with this point – the sentence now reads “Formamide generally composes between 10-50% of the final volume of the hybridization buffer, but this range may be exceeded under specific circumstance (Table 2).” 331 – have you validated the effect of EDTA on blocking RNases? RNase are not dependent on divalent cations the way DNases are. We have not validated this claim empirically. Thus, we have removed this claim and the associated reference from the manuscript. 364 – While I agree with the author that generally hybridizations cannot go ‘too long’, it might be instructive to discuss the ‘5 minute’ ‘TURBO-FISH’ protocol as a nice example of rapid hybridization. We agree that it is worth mentioning this example so that readers understand the range of what has been achieved, although we note that this is not feasible as a starting point. The sentences now read ”Rapid hybridization has been achieved in cultured cells in as little as five minutes with the Turbo FISH method (Shaffer et al., 2013), but this is not a prudent point of entry for new protocols, especially for whole-mount material. Generally, 12-24 hours is sufficient, regardless of the probe type (Carleton et al., 2014; Jackson, Herlitze & Hohagen, 2016; Meyer, Garzia & Tuschl, 2017; Jandura et al., 2017).” 444 – recommendations for positive controls: Probes that are expected to give signal in every cell are not so easy to distinguish from background in every cell. I think it would be good to recommend in addition or in place of these controls, to use a patterned control in a heterogenous tissue (something say that should label epithelial but not mesenchyme, or neurons but not others) or a cell cycle probe in replicative tissue or replicative cultured cells KI67, or the histones loci make good probe targets as the mRNA is long or abundant but cell cycle specific in expression). We have chosen to omit the recommendation to use poly(dT) probes as we agree that results from this control could be misleading and difficult to distinguish from background. By mentioning the use of constituently expressed genes like tubulin, we were indeed referring to a patterned control that would produce a specific staining pattern. The section has been updated to mention that if a gene like tubulin produces too much labeling, a more specific control such as a neuronal or epithelial marker should be used.
paper_title_zh: RNA荧光原位杂交技术综述与指南
paper_abstract_zh: RNA-荧光原位杂交（FISH）是一种强大的工具，用于在培养细胞、组织切片或整体制备中可视化目标mRNA转录本。随着该技术的不断发展，已发表了越来越多的不同协议。目前，已有广泛的选择方案来促进适当的组织制备、杂交和杂交后背景去除，以获得最佳结果。本文综述了RNA-FISH的技术方面，考察了与不同样本类型（包括细胞学制备和整体制备）相关的最常见方法。我们讨论了常用试剂在组织制备、杂交和杂交后洗涤中的应用，并解释了每种试剂的功能作用。我们还讨论了可用的探针类型和必要的对照，以准确可视化基因表达。最后，我们回顾了FISH技术的最新进展，这些进展促进了高度多重实验和单个目标的信号放大。综合来看，这些信息将为那些希望在缺乏文献记载或优化协议的有机体中进行FISH研究的调查人员提供方法开发指导。

considered”。纯合成探针的近期激增，取代了克隆衍生探针，提供了对GC含量和形成二级结构倾向等特性的更大控制。例如，Beliveau等人2012年《美国国家科学院院刊》。已在此点添加参考文献，并就合成探针兴起给用户带来的控制进行了后续说明。第185行 – 我建议扩大时间范围，许多现代协议对培养细胞使用更短的固定时间，例如10分钟。（Chen…Zhuang 2015年关于人类培养细胞的‘MERFISH’或Skinner…Golding 2013年关于大肠杆菌的）。我们已扩大了时间范围，并引用了Raj实验室的Turbo-FISH论文作为培养细胞中10分钟固定的例子。约第214行关于酒精固定。可以提及“Turbo-FISH”协议——一种快速的甲醇基固定。我们已在此段落中添加了对Turbo-FISH协议的引用，作为快速酒精基固定的例子。第229行 – 在讨论“保护天然蛋白质结构”时 – 可以提到酒精溶液通常是变性的，会破坏天然蛋白质结构，这可能导致免疫FISH协议（蛋白质+RNA检测）中抗原性的丧失。热固定也是如此。GA固定可以通过提供过于密集的交联显著降低渗透性。我们已包括酒精固定剂和热通常不适合联合免疫组织化学和FISH协议（在各自关于酒精固定和固定温度的段落中）。第244行 – 我不建议对果蝇胚胎进行蛋白酶K处理。我认为对近期果蝇smFISH文献（未引用）的更彻底搜索会证实这一点。参见Pare…McGinnis 2009年《当代生物学》，Boettiger…Levine 2009年《科学》，Boettiger…Levine 2013年《细胞报告》，Little…Gregor 2013年《细胞》，2011年《公共科学图书馆·生物学》，等等。关于辛格实验室最近开发的胃蛋白酶处理（代替蛋白酶K）的讨论可以与蛋白酶K讨论并列。（Bauxbaum…Singer 2014年《科学》）。许多实验室确实在远离对果蝇胚胎使用蛋白酶K（我们现在引用了其中一些），然而，仍有近期高影响力的论文引用在果蝇上使用蛋白酶K（例如Trcek等人2017年《自然协议》）。因此，我们选择不删除对果蝇胚胎使用蛋白酶K的提及。话虽如此，我们已添加了一些关于替代的丙酮和胃蛋白酶处理的讨论，以便读者能够了解所有可用的选项。至于其他仅使用去污剂基透化方法的论文，我们在后一段落中提到了去污剂基方法：“无蛋白酶的去污剂基方法也已成功用于果蝇胚胎的透化（Boettiger & Levine, 2013）。”第286行：50%甲酰胺 – 10-50%可能是一个更准确的说法。例如，参见Raj等人描述的高分辨率smFISH协议（2006或2008年），并在近期smFISH工作中建立（参见Long Cai和Xiaowei Zhuang团队关于高度多重smFISH协议的工作）。我们同意这一点 – 句子现读作“甲酰胺通常占杂交缓冲液最终体积的10-50%，但在特定情况下可能超过此范围（表2）。”第331行 – 你验证了EDTA对阻断RNA酶的效果吗？RNA酶不像DNA酶那样依赖于二价阳离子。我们未经验证此声明。因此，我们已从手稿中删除了此声明及相关参考文献。第364行 – 虽然我同意作者的观点，通常杂交不会“过长”，但讨论“5分钟”“TURBO-FISH”协议作为一个快速杂交的例子可能是有益的。我们同意提及此例是有价值的，以便读者了解已实现的范围，尽管我们注意到这不适合作为起点。句子现读作“在培养细胞中，使用Turbo FISH方法已实现仅需五分钟的快速杂交（Shaffer等人，2013年），但这对于新协议，尤其是整体材料来说，不是一个谨慎的起点。通常，12-24小时已足够，无论探针类型如何（Carleton等人，2014年；Jackson, Herlitze & Hohagen, 2016年；Meyer, Garzia & Tuschl, 2017年；Jandura等人，2017年）。”第444行 – 阳性对照的建议：预期在每个细胞中都给出信号的探针并不容易在每个细胞中与背景区分开来。我认为除了这些对照之外或代替这些对照，使用异质组织中的模式对照（例如，应该标记上皮细胞但不标记间质，或神经元但不标记其他细胞）或复制组织或复制培养细胞中的细胞周期探针KI67，或组蛋白基因座是良好的探针靶标，因为mRNA较长或丰富但表达具有细胞周期特异性）。我们选择省略使用poly(dT)探针的建议，因为我们同意此对照的结果可能具有误导性且难以与背景区分。通过提及使用如微管蛋白这样的恒定表达基因，我们确实是指一种会产生特定染色模式的模式对照。该部分已更新，提及如果像微管蛋白这样的基因产生过多标记，应使用更具体的对照，如神经元或上皮细胞标记。

paper_title: Data privacy during pandemics: A systematic literature review of COVID-19 smartphone applications
paper_abstract: Background. On January 8, 2020, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention officially announced a new virus in Wuhan, China. The first novel coronavirus (COVID-19) case was discovered on December 1, 2019, implying that the disease was spreading quietly and quickly in the community before reaching the rest of the world. To deal with the virus' wide spread, countries have deployed contact tracing mobile applications to control viral transmission. Such applications collect users' information and inform them if they were in contact with an individual diagnosed with COVID-19. However, these applications might have affected human rights by breaching users' privacy.
review_content: Reviewer 2 (Anonymous) Basic reporting - The paper is very well written and in simple words. It is thus easy to understand which is a very important characteristic of any document. Thank you for your comment. - The sections are titled as questions. While this is innovative and gets the point across, I prefer a more conventional approach to naming sections Thank you for your comment and we totally agree with your suggestion. We have changed all titles to follow the conventional approach without using any questions for naming the sections. - Each section and each point has to be discussed in much more detail. The authors superficially discuss the ideas of various works and do so in a rather heterogeneous manner with separate paragraphs dedicated to separate papers. I would look forward to a more homogeneous discussion of ideas with disparate work smoothly falling into the discussion. Agreed. We have updated the following sections in a homogenous manner and discussed ideas in a more holistic approach: Privacy protection laws for COVID-19 applications, Protection Law, Values, Issues, Entities contributing to preserving privacy of healthcare applications, and the Conclusion. Experimental design - Very little discussion is dedicated to the users’ privacy and its breach. The authors discuss laws that are prevalent around the world, “ethical” issues, and “values”. I would prefer a much more detailed analysis of the issues around privacy and its breach first in a general context and subsequently specifically with respect to the pandemic and the tracing apps. Thank you for your comment and we totally agree with it. Under the section (Issues) we have included a much more detailed analysis of the privacy and its breach, first in a general context and then with respect to the pandemic. We have also included a specific diagram for the same purpose (Figure 6) - The authors discuss the attempts made by health authorities to protect and preserve privacy. I feel this discussion is limited. The authors should also include the efforts made by governments, health authorities, world bodies, and also those made at individual levels. Agreed. As suggested, we have added a dedicated section titled (Entities contributing to preserving privacy of healthcare applications) which include efforts by governments, health authorities, and world bodies. Validity of the findings - Conclusions on various aspects of the study are not drawn. The authors talk about the issues based on the contributions of various endeavors but do not draw appropriate conclusions based on these. Thank you for your comment. We have drawn appropriate conclusions in multiple sections and improved the paper’s conclusion at the end. Additional comments - A few figures, block diagrams etc. would help the reader more effectively grasp the ideas being discussed. Agreed. We have added two diagrams and a table as follows: 1. A diagram classifying privacy issues is added to the paper (Figure 6) 2. A diagram showing the geographical locations of the contact tracing apps around the world is added (Figure 5) 3. Table 3 is added summarizing all contact tracing apps and their privacy concerns. -The authors may want to justify the content and both ends for a better appearance. Thank you for your comment. We have justified the content and both ends as requested for better appearance.
paper_title_zh: 大流行期间的数据隐私：COVID-19智能手机应用程序的系统文献综述
paper_abstract_zh: 背景。2020年1月8日，美国疾病控制与预防中心正式宣布在中国武汉发现了一种新病毒。首例新型冠状病毒（COVID-19）病例于2019年12月1日被发现，这表明该疾病在传播到全球其他地区之前，已在社区中悄然且迅速地蔓延。为应对病毒的广泛传播，各国部署了接触追踪移动应用程序以控制病毒传播。此类应用程序收集用户信息，并在用户与确诊为COVID-19的个体有过接触时通知他们。然而，这些应用程序可能因侵犯用户隐私而影响了人权。
review_content_zh:
审稿人2（匿名）

基本报告 - 论文写得非常好，语言简洁。因此，易于理解，这是任何文档都非常重要的特征。感谢您的评论。- 各节的标题以问题的形式呈现。虽然这种做法创新且能传达要点，但我更倾向于使用更传统的节标题命名方式。感谢您的评论，我们完全同意您的建议。我们已经将所有标题改为传统的命名方式，不再使用问题形式命名各节。- 每一节和每一个点都需要进行更详细的讨论。作者对各种工作的想法进行了浅显的讨论，并且以较为异质的方式，用单独的段落分别讨论不同的论文。我期待看到对各种想法进行更同质化的讨论，使不同工作自然融入讨论中。同意。我们已经以同质化的方式更新了以下各节，并以更全面的方法讨论了相关想法：COVID-19应用的隐私保护法律、保护法、价值观、问题、为医疗应用隐私保护做出贡献的实体，以及结论。

实验设计 - 对用户隐私及其泄露的讨论非常少。作者讨论了世界各地普遍存在的法律、“伦理”问题以及“价值观”。我更希望看到对隐私及其泄露问题的更详细分析，首先在一般背景下，然后具体针对疫情和追踪应用进行分析。感谢您的评论，我们完全同意。在（问题）一节中，我们已经包括了对隐私及其泄露的更详细分析，首先在一般背景下，然后针对疫情进行分析。我们还为此目的添加了具体的图表（图6）- 作者讨论了卫生部门为保护和维护隐私所做的努力。我认为这种讨论是有限的。作者还应包括政府、卫生部门、世界机构以及个人层面所做的努力。同意。按照建议，我们添加了一个专门的部分，题为（为医疗应用隐私保护做出贡献的实体），其中包括政府、卫生部门以及世界机构的努力。

研究结果的可靠性 - 对研究各个方面的结论未得出。作者基于各种努力的贡献讨论了问题，但未基于这些贡献得出适当的结论。感谢您的评论。我们在多个部分得出了适当的结论，并改进了论文最后的结论。

附加评论 - 添加一些图表、框图等将有助于读者更有效地理解所讨论的想法。同意。我们已添加了两个图表和一张表格，如下：1. 添加了一个分类隐私问题的图表（图6）2. 添加了一个显示全球接触追踪应用地理位置的图表（图5）3. 添加了总结所有接触追踪应用及其隐私问题的表格（表3）- 作者可能需要调整内容和对齐方式以获得更好的外观。感谢您的评论。我们已按照要求调整了内容和对齐方式，以获得更好的外观。

paper_title: Deep Neural Networks and Brain Alignment: Brain Encoding and Decoding (Survey)
paper_abstract: Can we obtain insights about the brain using AI models? How is the information in deep learning models related to brain recordings? Can we improve AI models with the help of brain recordings? Such questions can be tackled by studying brain recordings like functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). As a first step, the neuroscience community has contributed several large cognitive neuroscience datasets related to passive reading/listening/viewing of concept words, narratives, pictures, and movies. Encoding and decoding models using these datasets have also been proposed in the past two decades. These models serve as additional tools for basic cognitive science and neuroscience research. Encoding models aim at generating fMRI brain representations given a stimulus automatically. They have several practical applications in evaluating and diagnosing neurological conditions and thus may also help design therapies for brain damage. Decoding models solve the inverse problem of reconstructing the stimuli given the fMRI. They are useful for designing brain-machine or brain-computer interfaces. Inspired by the effectiveness of deep learning models for natural language processing, computer vision, and speech, several neural encoding and decoding models have been recently proposed. In this survey, we will first discuss popular representations of language, vision and speech stimuli, and present a summary of neuroscience datasets. Further, we will review popular deep learning based encoding and decoding architectures and note their benefits and limitations. Finally, we will conclude with a summary and discussion about future trends. Given the large amount of recently published work in the computational cognitive neuroscience (CCN) community, we believe that this survey enables an entry point for DNN researchers to diversify into CCN research.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This manuscript provides an overview over how deep neural networks are used to better understand the brain by training the DNNs to either encode various stimuli (audio, images etc.) into brain activity or, in reverse, decode such stimuli from brain activity (as measured by EEG, MEG, fMRI etc.). It provides a fairly comprehensive overview over the motivation and typical methods for such studies, and discusses a wide range of recent results.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
I found the manuscript well-written and comprehensive, if a bit longwinded at some points. I especially liked the Key Takeaways sections. Some of the results sections like "Disentangling Syntax and Semantics" may benefit from a bit more shortening, potentially moving some parts to a supplementary. I found some parts on MEG preprocessing imprecise. > Addressing these challenges requires continuous advancements in preprocessing algorithms such as fMRIPrep (Esteban et al., 2019) and MNE (Gramfort et al., 2013), MNE is a software library for MNE data analysis, not a preprocessing algorithm. Also the MEG preprocessing pipeline on page 21 should be more clearly described as *an* example, choices like a bandpass filter between 0.5 and 30 Hz can and will certainly be done differently by other researchers. Also writing "using MNE-Python (Gramfort et al.,2013) default parameters" seemed confusing to me, so do you mean there is some MNE default MEG preprocessing pipeline? If so you should like to that specific code pipeline somewhere. but seems unlikely to me that sucha pipeline would include things like temporally decimating by exactly 10x, this does not make sense as a general default for data with maybe different sampling rates etc. One thing not mentioned (or I missed) was the direction of trying to drive control biological neurons, see requested changes. Many figures look quite appealing, even if a bit diverse in visual style throughout the manuscript, but probably hard to avoid when integrating a large number of figures from the field. The top part of Figure 10 I found a little less appealing due to the distorted/strangely scaled font etc. Overall, I think the manuscript presents a valuable introduction and overview to the field of using DNNs to understand brain activity on natural stimuli.

**Requested Changes:**
Please revise the MEG preprocessing sections as described above. [Audiocite.net: A Large Spoken Read Dataset in French - 2024_Felice_audiocite.pdf](https://hal.science/hal-04533994/document) would be a dataset that I think had not been mentioned? At least for the discussion part, one thing I would like to see mentioned is the direction of trying to drive or control biological neurons using analyses of artificial deep neural networks, e.g., see [Neural population control via deep image synthesis | Science](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aav9436). I don't think this was mentioned, if I missed it, feel free to correct me. Due to the already fairly lengthy manuscript, feel free to keep this to a few sentences. If you can have a cleaner version of the top part of Figure 10, would be nice. This paper is duplicated in the references: Martin Schrimpf, Jonas Kubilius, Ha Hong, Najib J Majaj, Rishi Rajalingham, Elias B Issa, Kohitij Kar, Pouya Bashivan, Jonathan Prescott-Roy, Franziska Geiger, et al. Brain-score: Which artificial neural network for object recognition is most brain-like? BioRxiv, pp. 407007, 2018

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes
paper_title_zh: 深度神经网络与脑部对齐：脑编码与解码（综述）
paper_abstract_zh: 我们能否通过人工智能模型获得对大脑的洞察？深度学习模型中的信息与大脑记录有何关联？我们能否借助大脑记录改进人工智能模型？这些问题可以通过研究功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）等大脑记录来探讨。作为第一步，神经科学界已贡献了多个与被动阅读/聆听/观看概念词、叙事、图片和电影相关的大型认知神经科学数据集。在过去二十年中，也提出了使用这些数据集的编码和解码模型。这些模型作为基础认知科学和神经科学研究的额外工具。编码模型旨在自动生成给定刺激的fMRI大脑表征。它们在评估和诊断神经状况方面有若干实际应用，并可能有助于设计脑损伤疗法。解码模型解决的是给定fMRI重建刺激的逆问题。它们对设计脑机或脑计算机接口很有用。受深度学习模型在自然语言处理、计算机视觉和语音方面有效性的启发，最近提出了几种神经编码和解码模型。在本综述中，我们首先将讨论语言、视觉和语音刺激的流行表征，并呈现神经科学数据集的概要。进一步，我们将回顾基于深度学习的流行编码和解码架构，并指出其优点和局限性。最后，我们将总结并讨论未来趋势。鉴于计算认知神经科学（CCN）社区最近发表了大量工作，我们相信本综述为深度神经网络（DNN）研究人员进入CCN研究提供了切入点。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文概述了深度神经网络如何通过训练来更好地理解大脑，具体包括将各种刺激（音频、图像等）编码为脑活动，或反过来从脑活动（通过EEG、MEG、fMRI等测量）解码这些刺激。文章提供了关于此类研究的动机和典型方法的相当全面的概述，并讨论了广泛的最新结果。

**优点和缺点：**
我发现本文写得很好且内容全面，尽管在某些地方略显冗长。我特别喜欢“关键要点”部分。像“解析语法和语义”这样的结果部分可能需要进一步精简，可以考虑将部分内容移至补充材料。我发现关于MEG预处理的某些部分不够精确。应对这些挑战需要不断改进预处理算法，如fMRIPrep（Esteban等人，2019）和MNE（Gramfort等人，2013），但MNE是一个用于MNE数据分析的软件库，而不是预处理算法。第21页上的MEG预处理流程应更明确地描述为“一个”示例，像0.5到30 Hz的带通滤波器的选择肯定会因其他研究者的不同而有所不同。此外，“使用MNE-Python（Gramfort等人，2013）默认参数”的表述似乎有些混淆，是否意味着存在某种MNE默认的MEG预处理流程？如果是这样，应在某处引用具体的代码流程，但似乎不太可能包含诸如精确10倍时间降采样之类的内容，这对于具有不同采样率等的数据来说并不适合作为一般默认设置。未提及（或我遗漏了）的一个方向是尝试驱动或控制生物神经元，详见所请求的修改。许多图表看起来相当吸引人，尽管在整篇文章中的视觉风格略显多样，但在整合大量领域内图表时可能难以避免。图10顶部的字体扭曲/比例奇怪，我觉得不太吸引人。总体而言，我认为本文为使用DNN理解自然刺激下的脑活动提供了宝贵的介绍和概述。

**请求的修改：**
请按上述描述修订MEG预处理部分。[Audiocite.net: A Large Spoken Read Dataset in French - 2024_Felice_audiocite.pdf](https://hal.science/hal-04533994/document)似乎是一个未提及的数据集？至少在讨论部分，我希望看到提及尝试通过分析人工深度神经网络来驱动或控制生物神经元的方向，例如参见[Neural population control via deep image synthesis | Science](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aav9436)。如果未提及这一点，请纠正我，鉴于文章已经相当长，可以仅用几句话提及。如果能有图10顶部更清晰的版本，那就更好了。参考文献中重复出现了这篇文章：Martin Schrimpf, Jonas Kubilius, Ha Hong, Najib J Majaj, Rishi Rajalingham, Elias B Issa, Kohitij Kar, Pouya Bashivan, Jonathan Prescott-Roy, Franziska Geiger,等人。Brain-score: Which artificial neural network for object recognition is most brain-like? BioRxiv, pp. 407007, 2018

**声明和证据：**
是

**受众：**

paper_title: Effect of extrusion cooking on the chemical and nutritional properties of instant flours: a review
paper_abstract: Satisfying the nutritional requirements of consumers has made food industries focus on the development of safe, innocuous, easy-to-prepare products with high nutritional quality through efficient processing technologies. Extrusion cooking has emerged as a prominent technology associated with the nutritional and functional attributes of food products. This review aims to establish a theoretical framework concerning the influence of extrusion parameters on the functional and nutritional properties of precooked or instant flours, both as end-products and ingredients. It highlights the pivotal role of process parameters within the extruder, including temperature, screw speed, and raw materials moisture content, among others, and elucidates their correlation with the modifications observed in the structural composition of these materials. Such modifications subsequently induce notable changes in the ultimate characteristics of the food product. Detailed insights into these transformations are provided within the subsequent sections, emphasizing their associations with critical phenomena such as nutrient availability, starch gelatinization, protein denaturation, enhanced in vitro digestibility, reduction in the content of antinutritional factors (ANFs), and the occurrence of Maillard reactions during specific processing stages. Drawing upon insights from available literature, it is concluded that these effects represent key attributes intertwined with the nutritional properties of the end-product during the production of instant flours.
review_content:
This review presents in a comprehensive and organized way the theoretical framework concerning the influence of extrusion parameters on the functional and nutritional properties of precooked or instant flours, both as end-products and ingredients. It highlights the pivotal role of process parameters within the extruder, including temperature, screw speed, and raw materials moisture content, among others, and elucidates their correlation with the modifications observed in the structural composition of these materials.

paper_title: The characteristics and roles of antimicrobial peptides as potential treatment for antibiotic-resistant pathogens: A review
paper_abstract: The emergence of antibiotic resistant bacteria has become a significant and everincreasing threat to global public health, increasing both morbidity and mortality rates, and the financial burden on health services. Infection by drug-resistant bacteria is anticipated to contribute to the demise of almost 10 million people by the year 2050 unless a competent and effective response is devised to engage with this issue. The emergence and spread of resistance is commonly caused by the excessive or inappropriate use of antibiotics and substandard pharmaceuticals. It arises when pathogens adapt to different conditions and develop self-defence mechanisms. Currently, novel antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) have been reported to be the sole cure for some clinical cases of infectious diseases such as sepsis and skin infections, although these agents may, on occasion, require administration together with an adjunctive low-dose antibiotic. Although AMPs are a promising alternative form of anti-microbial therapy and easily applied in the medical sector, they still have limitations that should not be taken lightly. Hence, this review explores the characteristics, advantages and disadvantages of AMPs for their potential in treating antibiotic-resistant pathogens.

paper_title: Lots of movement, little progress: A review of reptile home range literature
paper_abstract: Reptiles are the most species-rich terrestrial vertebrate group with a broad diversity of life history traits. Biotelemetry is an essential methodology for reptiles as it compensates for several limitations when studying their natural history. We evaluated trends in terrestrial reptile spatial ecology studies focusing upon quantifying home ranges for the past twenty years. We assessed 290 English-language reptile home range studies published from 2000-2019 via a structured literature review investigating publications' study location, taxonomic group, methodology, reporting, and analytical techniques. Substantial biases remain in both location and taxonomic groups in the literature, with nearly half of all studies (45%) originating from the USA. Snakes were most often studied, and crocodiles were least often studied, while testudines tended to have the greatest within study sample sizes. More than half of all studies lacked critical methodological details, limiting the number of studies for inclusion in future meta-analyses (55% of studies lacked information on individual tracking durations, and 51% lacked sufficient information on the number of times researchers recorded positions). Studies continue to rely on outdated methods to quantify space-use (including Minimum Convex Polygons and Kernel Density Estimators), often failing to report subtleties on decisions that have substantial impact on home range area estimates. Moving forward researchers can select a suite of appropriate analytical techniques tailored to their research question (dynamic Brownian Bridge Movement Models for within sample interpolation, and autocorrelated Kernel Density Estimators for beyond sample extrapolation). Only 1.4% of all evaluated studies linked to available and usable telemetry data, further hindering scientific consensus. We ultimately implore herpetologists to adopt transparent reporting practices and make liberal use of open data platforms to maximize progress in the field of reptile spatial ecology.
review_content: Reviewer 2 (Anonymous) Overall summary: Well composed and detailed with sufficient justification included. The authors did very well in explaining their study parameters regarding the inclusion of articles for this meta analysis to highlight lacking data for reptile species. One suggestion for improvement is to expand upon the “Example Report” as a guideline for future studies involving telemetry of reptile species.
paper_title_zh: 大量移动，进展甚微：爬行动物家域文献综述
paper_abstract_zh: 爬行动物是物种最丰富的陆生脊椎动物类群，具有广泛的生命史特征多样性。生物遥测是研究爬行动物的重要方法，因为它弥补了在研究其自然历史时的若干局限性。我们评估了过去二十年间陆地爬行动物空间生态学研究的趋势，重点关注家域的量化。通过结构化的文献综述，我们评估了2000-2019年间发表的290篇英文爬行动物家域研究，探讨了这些出版物的研究地点、分类群、方法学、报告和分析技术。文献中在研究地点和分类群方面仍存在显著偏倚，近一半的研究（45%）来自美国。蛇类最常被研究，鳄鱼类最少被研究，而龟鳖类往往具有最大的研究内样本量。超过一半的研究缺乏关键的方法学细节，限制了未来元分析中可纳入的研究数量（55%的研究缺乏个体追踪时长的信息，51%缺乏研究者记录位置次数的充分信息）。研究继续依赖过时的空间利用量化方法（包括最小凸多边形和核密度估计），常常未能报告对家域面积估计有重大影响的决策细节。未来，研究人员可以选择一套适合其研究问题的分析技术（如动态布朗桥运动模型用于样本内插值，自相关核密度估计用于样本外推）。在所有评估的研究中，仅有1.4%链接到可用和可用的遥测数据，进一步阻碍了科学共识的形成。我们最终敦促爬行动物学家采用透明的报告实践，并充分利用开放数据平台，以最大化爬行动物空间生态学领域的进展。

paper_title: Effect of citrus-based products on urine profile: A systematic review and meta-analysis
paper_abstract: Background  . Urolithiasis is a disease with high recurrence rate, 30-50% within 5 years. The aim of the present study was to learn the effects of citrus-based products on the urine profile in healthy persons and people with urolithiasis compared to control diet and potassium citrate.  Methods.  A systematic review was performed, which included interventional, prospective observational and retrospective studies, comparing citrus-based therapy with standard diet therapy, mineral water, or potassium citrate. A literature search was conducted using PUBMED, COCHRANE, and Google Scholar with “citrus or lemonade or orange or grapefruit or lime or juice” and “urolithiasis” as search terms. For statistical analysis, a fixed-effects model was conducted when p > 0.05, and random-effects model was conducted when p < 0.05.  Results.  In total, 135 citations were found through database searching with 10 studies found to be consistent with our selection criteria. However, only 8 studies were included in quantitative analysis, due to data availability. The present study showed a higher increased in urine pH for citrus-based products (mean difference, 0.16; 95% CI 0.01-0.32) and urinary citrate (mean difference, 124.49; 95% CI 80.24-168.74) compared with a control group. However, no differences were found in urine volume, urinary calcium, urinary oxalate, and urinary uric acid. From subgroup analysis, we found that citrus-based products consistently increased urinary citrate level higher than controls in both healthy and urolithiasis populations. Furthermore, there was lower urinary calcium level among people with urolithiasis.  Conclusions.  Citrus-based products could increase urinary citrate level significantly higher than control. These results should encourage further research to explore citrus-based products as a urolithiasis treatment.
review_content:
The authors present a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis of the effect of citrus-based products on urine profile. The paper is supplemented by the PRISMA flow chart and forest plot charts to present their results.

Although their search strategy is good, they should have used other terms such as 'kidney stones', 'stones', 'ureteric stones' and 'calculi' too. They have only used the term 'Urolithiasis' which could potentially miss on other relevant studies.

As a limitation of any systematic review the authors are correct in acknowledging that their is likely to be a publication bias. Similarly, the long term effect of the use of citrate-based products in not know from this study and whether their results translate into a reduction in stone recurrences remain unknown.

A recent cochrane review on the use of citrate salts on prevention and treatment of calcium containing kidney stones in adults showed a reduction in new stone formation and stone recurrences in these patients1.

Overall the paper reads well and is a nice summary on the use of citrate based products on urine profile.
paper_title_zh: 基于柑橘类产品的尿液剖面影响：系统评价与荟萃分析
paper_abstract_zh: 背景：尿路结石是一种复发率高的疾病，5年内复发率可达30-50%。本研究旨在了解柑橘类产品对健康人和尿路结石患者尿液成分的影响，并与对照组饮食和柠檬酸钾进行比较。方法：进行了一项系统评价，包括干预性、前瞻性观察性和回顾性研究，比较了柑橘类疗法与标准饮食疗法、矿泉水或柠檬酸钾。使用PUBMED、COCHRANE和Google Scholar数据库，以“柑橘或柠檬水或橙子或葡萄柚或青柠或果汁”和“尿路结石”为检索词进行文献检索。对于统计分析，当p > 0.05时，采用固定效应模型，当p < 0.05时，采用随机效应模型。结果：通过数据库检索共找到135篇文献，发现10项研究符合我们的选择标准。然而，由于数据可用性，只有8项研究被纳入定量分析。本研究显示，与对照组相比，柑橘类产品显著提高了尿液pH（平均差异，0.16；95% CI 0.01-0.32）和尿液中柠檬酸（平均差异，124.49；95% CI 80.24-168.74）。然而，在尿液量、尿钙、尿草酸和尿尿酸方面没有发现差异。从亚组分析中，我们发现柑橘类产品在健康人和尿路结石人群中均能持续提高尿液柠檬酸水平，高于对照组。此外，尿路结石患者的尿钙水平较低。结论：柑橘类产品可以显著提高尿液柠檬酸水平，这些结果应鼓励进一步研究，探索柑橘类产品作为尿路结石治疗方法的可能性。
review_content_zh:
作者们对基于柑橘类产品的尿液成分影响进行了全面的系统综述和荟萃分析。论文辅以PRISMA流程图和森林图来展示他们的研究结果。

尽管他们的搜索策略良好，但他们本应使用其他术语，如“肾结石”、“结石”、“输尿管结石”和“结石病”，而不仅仅是“尿路结石”，这可能会遗漏其他相关研究。

作为任何系统综述的局限性，作者正确地承认可能存在发表偏差。同样，本研究并未了解基于柠檬酸盐产品的长期影响，以及其结果是否转化为结石复发的减少仍未知。

最近的一项Cochrane综述关于使用柠檬酸盐盐预防和治疗成人含钙肾结石，显示这些患者的新结石形成和结石复发减少1。

总体而言，这篇论文读起来很好，是对基于柠檬酸盐产品在尿液成分中的应用的出色总结。

paper_title: Selecting differential splicing methods: Practical considerations
paper_abstract: Alternative splicing is crucial in gene regulation, with significant implications in clinical settings and biotechnology. This review article compiles bioinformatics RNA-seq tools for investigating differential splicing; offering a detailed examination of their statistical methods, case applications, and benefits. A total of 22 tools are categorised by their statistical family (parametric, non-parametric, and probabilistic) and level of analysis (transcript, exon, and event). The central challenges in quantifying alternative splicing include correct splice site identification and accurate isoform deconvolution of transcripts. Benchmarking studies show no consensus on tool performance, revealing considerable variability across different scenarios. Tools with high citation frequency and continued developer maintenance, such as DEXSeq and rMATS, are recommended for prospective researchers. To aid in tool selection, a guide schematic is proposed based on variations in data input and the required level of analysis. Additionally, advancements in long-read RNA sequencing are expected to drive the evolution of differential splicing tools, reducing the need for isoform deconvolution and prompting further innovation.
review_content:
The article by Draper and colleagues presents a well-researched and well-organised overview of differential splicing analysis tools for short-read RNA sequencing, which will be valuable for many researchers. The practical focus is excellent, I especially like the section on developer maintenance of tooling, which is often neglected in software review articles. The decision tree in Figure 5 is also a great framework for navigating this crowded space and I’m sure will be useful to many.

Despite this, in many places the use of language is imprecise: words are missing or used incorrectly, sentences are too vague—perhaps from being over-simplified in an attempt to make the text more understandable. I also find some of the recommendations are not adequately supported by evidence. Please find some comments that I hope will be helpful, below:

Major comments
  * The method benchmarking section needs some attention. ‘Scientific accuracy’ should be replaced by just ‘accuracy’. ‘Computational power’ should be specified, presumably you mean performance characteristics such as memory usage and run time. “Lack of ground truth to set as a reference to compare to..” is unnecessary, just say a lack of ground truth splicing quantifications. Library size and sequencing depth are the same thing? Library size and positional bias are qualities of the RNA-seq data itself, not the bioinformatic pre-processing steps. Annotation quality is not a ‘pre-processing’ step - this is a feature of the organism under study. “Achieve finer control over the ground truth” could be rephrased to something more meaningful like ‘to explore the impact of increasing variability between replicates, changing replicate numbers, sequencing depth’…..etc. “The consensus drawn from these three benchmarks is that the performance of differential splicing tools exhibits considerable variability depending on the outlined factors.” This seems weak, perhaps a more nuanced conclusion can be drawn - when data is very good, deep sequencing, low variability, which tool performs best? Which tools have the lowest run times, compute requirements .etc. I don’t think it’s sufficient to simply say its complicated - please dive more into the details here. “The ongoing evolution and upkeep of tools by developers introduce a time-dependent aspect to benchmarking. Community-led maintenance efforts consistently enhance the functionality and reliability of tools over time.” I’m not sure what this means, please clarify.
  * The discussion brings in developments in long read sequencing and is quite nice - I would suggest making this a section of its own and expanding on what is already written. Alternatively, I would consider cutting it back a bit and changing the title of the article to reflect a focus on short-read sequencing data. Perhaps one point for the discussion is that whilst new methods are developing, there remains hundreds of thousands of publicly available short read RNA sequencing datasets through which novel biological insights can still be made.
  * In the section of recommendations - “For instance, if the aim is to identify known transcripts, it is advisable to opt for a parametric transcript-based tool like DEXSeq or DRIMSeq and execute a DTU study following Michael Love’s protocol.37” The citation does not support the statement - why shouldn’t researchers opt for an exon-based approach when the transcriptomic annotations are good? Also in this section, DEXSeq is recommended for DEU analysis, when rMATs is the most highly cited splicing tool and provides accurate quantifications of exon usage. “Overall, event-based methods are more suited to advanced programmers owing to their use of command-line tools over interpreters that use IDEs (Integrated development environments). For most analyses, however, a DEU or DTU-based analysis is recommended for simple interpretability and robustness.” I don’t understand, how is DEX-Seq easier to use than rMATs (for example), or MAJIQ which has extensive graphical reporting? Are you saying this because DEX-Seq is an R package so you can use RStudio? - this doesn’t seem like a particularly helpful argument - I can run rMATs or MAJIQ or any of these using a bash script in Visual Studio Code which is also an IDE…
Minor comments
  * Alternative splicing (AS) abbreviation is given several times throughout text and sometimes used, sometimes not - please be consistent.
  * “The proposed advantage of this approach is in the smaller exonic regions rather than full isoform deconvolution.” Rephrase for clarity, presumably you mean by focusing on regions unique to distinct isoforms the tool avoids the issue of assigning ambiguous reads to isoforms.
  * "A few newer methods such as DRIMSeq and DTUrtle have progressed onto non-parametric or mixed Dirichlet Multinomial Models (DMM)" ‘progression’ suggests there is some kind of hierarchy, you can just say that these models ‘use’ other distributions
  * “More complex regulatory events involve genomic features beyond exons and introns, such as alternative promoter and polyadenylation sites, which result in varying mRNA 5′ and 3′ UTR ends. However, these events are seldom included in most bioinformatics analyses, tools such as CAGER (Cap Analysis of Gene Expression) and DaPars (Dynamic Analysis of Alternative PolyAdenylation from RNA-Seq) are available for niche research” I wouldn’t say these events are more complex from a biological standpoint. The issue in analysis of alternative TSS use and APA is that short read sequencing with typical library preparation methods (e.g. random hexamer priming) won’t have good coverage of exact transcript 5’ and 3’ ends. Therefore typically library preparations with mRNA cap capture (CAGE) or 3’ end sequencing (eg. Quantseq) are used when this is the analysis goal. Also, to be a pedant, 3’UTRs and 5’UTRs are exons.
  * The discussion mentions Nextflow, and nf-core is mentioned earlier, but it might be nice to specifically mention the efforts of nf-core/rnasplice. As you know, one of the benefits of these pipelines is that everything is containerised so you don’t have to mess about installing everything. Generally speaking, one of the barriers to using tools can be installation - of the presented tools there is quite a range of levels of developer investment in making the tools easy to install. Some are in bioconda or bioconductor and have containers, others you have to contact the authors to get permission to download (MAJIQ!) - this might be related to the amount of citations that tools get. It would be nice (but not necessary) to address this too.
paper_title_zh: 选择差异剪接方法：实用考量
paper_abstract_zh: 可变剪接在基因调控中至关重要，对临床环境和生物技术具有重大意义。本文综述了用于研究差异剪接的生物信息学RNA-seq工具，详细探讨了它们的统计方法、案例应用和优势。共22种工具根据其统计家族（参数、非参数和概率）和分析水平（转录本、外显子和事件）进行分类。量化可变剪接的主要挑战包括正确识别剪接位点和准确解析转录本的异构体。基准测试研究表明，工具性能没有达成共识，不同场景下存在显著变异性。推荐高引用频率且持续维护的工具，如DEXSeq和rMATS，供未来研究者使用。为辅助工具选择，基于数据输入变化和所需分析水平，提出了一个指南图示。此外，长读长RNA测序的进步预计将推动差异剪接工具的演变，减少对异构体解析的需求，并促进进一步创新。
review_content_zh:
Draper及其同事的文章对短读RNA测序的差异剪接分析工具进行了深入研究且组织良好的概述，这对许多研究人员来说将非常有价值。其实用性焦点极佳，我特别喜欢关于开发者维护工具的部分，这在软件评论文章中通常被忽视。图5中的决策树也是一个很好的框架，用于导航这个拥挤的领域，我相信这对许多人都会很有用。

尽管如此，在许多地方，语言的使用不够精确：词汇缺失或使用不当，句子过于模糊——可能是为了使文本更易理解而过度简化所致。我还发现一些建议缺乏充分的证据支持。以下是我希望有所帮助的一些评论：

主要评论
* 方法基准测试部分需要关注。“科学准确性”应改为“准确性”。“计算能力”应具体说明，你大概是指性能特征，如内存使用和运行时间。“缺乏作为比较参考的地面真相……”是不必要的，只需说缺乏地面真相剪接定量即可。文库大小和测序深度是同一回事吗？文库大小和位置偏倚是RNA-seq数据本身的特性，而不是生物信息学预处理步骤的特性。注释质量不是“预处理”步骤——这是所研究生物体的特征。“实现对地面真相的更精细控制”可以改得更具体，如“探索增加重复间变异性、改变重复次数、测序深度”等的影响。“从这三个基准得出的共识是，差异剪接工具的性能表现出相当大的变异性，取决于所列出的因素。”这似乎有些薄弱，或许可以得出更细致的结论——当数据质量很高、测序深度大、变异性低时，哪种工具表现最佳？哪些工具的运行时间和计算要求最低？我认为仅仅说它复杂是不够的——请在此处深入探讨细节。“开发者对工具的不断演化和维护引入了基准测试的时间依赖性方面。社区主导的维护工作持续提升工具的功能和可靠性。”我不确定这是什么意思，请澄清。
* 讨论部分引入了长读测序的发展，非常不错——我建议将其作为一个独立的章节，并扩展已有内容。或者，我考虑稍微缩减这部分内容，并更改文章标题以反映对短读测序数据的关注。讨论中或许可以指出，尽管新方法正在发展，但仍有数十万公开可用的短读RNA测序数据集，通过这些数据集仍可以获得新的生物学见解。
* 在建议部分——“例如，如果目标是识别已知转录本，建议选择像DEXSeq或DRIMSeq这样的参数化转录本工具，并按照Michael Love的协议执行DTU研究。”37引用不支持该声明——为什么当转录组注释良好时，研究人员不选择基于外显子的方法？同样在这部分，DEXSeq被推荐用于DEU分析，而rMATs是最常被引用的剪接工具，并提供准确的外显子使用定量。“总体而言，基于事件的 方法更适合高级程序员，因为它们使用命令行工具而非使用IDE（集成开发环境）的解释器。然而，对于大多数分析，建议使用DEU或DTU-based分析，以简单可解释性和鲁棒性。”我不明白，DEX-Seq怎么会比rMATs（例如）或具有广泛图形报告的MAJIQ更容易使用？你是说因为DEX-Seq是R包，所以可以用RStudio吗？——这似乎不是一个特别有帮助的论点——我可以用bash脚本在Visual Studio Code中运行rMATs或MAJIQ或任何这些工具，后者也是一个IDE……

次要评论
* 文中多次给出可变剪接（AS）的缩写，有时使用，有时不使用——请保持一致。
* “这种方法的优势在于关注较小的外显子区域，而非完整的异构体解析。”请重新措辞以明确，你大概是指通过关注特定异构体独有的区域，工具避免了将模糊读数分配给异构体的问题。
* “一些较新的方法，如DRIMSeq和DTUrtle，已经发展到非参数化或混合狄利克雷多项式模型（DMM）”‘进展’暗示存在某种层级，你只需说这些模型‘使用’其他分布。
* “更复杂的调控事件涉及超出外显子和内含子的基因组特征，如可变启动子和多聚腺苷酸化位点，导致mRNA 5′和3′ UTR端变化。然而，这些事件在大多数生物信息学分析中很少被包括，工具如CAGER（基因表达帽分析）和DaPars（RNA-Seq的动态可变多聚腺苷酸化分析）可用于特定研究领域”我不会说这些事件在生物学上更复杂。分析可变TSS使用和APA的问题在于，短读测序和典型的文库制备方法（例如随机六聚体引物）不会很好地覆盖确切的转录本5’和3’端。因此，当这是分析目标时，通常使用mRNA帽捕获（CAGE）或3’端测序（例如Quantseq）的文库制备方法。此外，严格来说，3’UTR和5’UTR是外显子。
* 讨论中提到了Nextflow，前面提到了nf-core，但特别提及nf-core/rnasplice的努力可能会更好。如你所知，这些管道的一个好处是所有内容都容器化，因此你不必费心安装一切。一般来说，使用工具的一个障碍可能是安装——在所展示的工具中，开发者在使工具易于安装方面的投入程度有很大差异。有些工具在bioconda或bioconductor中，并有容器，其他工具则需要联系作者获取下载许可（MAJIQ！），这可能与工具获得的引用数量有关。如果能够 address这一点也不错（但不是必须的）。

paper_title: A Survey on Transformers in Reinforcement Learning
paper_abstract: Transformer has been considered the dominating neural architecture in NLP and CV, mostly under supervised settings. Recently, a similar surge of using Transformers has appeared in the domain of reinforcement learning (RL), but it is faced with unique design choices and challenges brought by the nature of RL. However, the evolution of Transformers in RL has not yet been well unraveled. In this paper, we seek to systematically review motivations and progress on using Transformers in RL, provide a taxonomy on existing works, discuss each sub-field, and summarize future prospects.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
Main contributions: - This survey provides a taxonomy of different applications of the transformer architectures in RL, including transformer as state encoder, as world model, or as decision maker (in the decision-transformer style). - The authors also reviewed works that apply transformer models to train generalist agents, either from scratch or by fine-tuning or prompting models. - The authors discussed future perspectives and open problems.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
Strength - This is a timely survey for an emerging and promising research area. The works mentioned in the paper are comprehensive and representative, and cover all the main areas (as far as I know) in this filed. - The authors provide a brief historical perspective on the development of model architectures in RL, and discussed challenges in applying transformer in the RL domain, e.g. the problem of non-stationary training data. This sets up an adequate context for the main discussion. Weakness (For each bullet, please see "requested changes" for details.) - There are a few inaccurate description of cited papers. - A few claims are not well supported or need rephrasing. - A few missing citations.

**Requested Changes:**
I only have a few non-critical requests: Inaccurate description of cited papers: - In section 3.2, "Emmons et al. (2021) identify that carefully choosing ... are crucial for the performance of DRL agents." That paper only discusses offline RL. - In section 5, under "Transformer Structure Tailored for Decision-making Problems": Zhou et al., 2021 is not an NLP paper. If the authors want to mention efficient transformer variants, Tay et al., 2022 (already cited) should have pointers to representative works. Questionable claims - In the introduction, "the training objective of RL agents is typically a function of the current policy, which induces nonstationarity during learning a Transformer". The non-stationary is not caused by using the policy in the training objective. It's caused by the training data being collected using an ever-changing policy. - Section 4.2, "The Transformer-based world model can help alleviate the prediction error on longer sequences." Please add citations to support this claim. A few missing citations - When discussing architectures in DRL, please consider cite IMPALA [1] - Deep Transformer Q-Networks [2] uses transformer with observation history as input, and the bellman loss is trained for multiple time-steps together. - [3] discusses applying ViT to RL Typos: - Section 4.4.2: "directly applying large language models for execution is inefficient or even feasible". feasible -> infeasible or unfeasible. Additional suggestion: - In the introduction and section 3.2, the authors discuss a few challenges of adopting transformer to RL problems. I think another possible reason is that transformer models typically need much more training data to be effective compared to models with strong inductive biases (CNN, RNN). In traditional DRL, sample efficiency is a key benchmark, which limits how much data the agent can collect to fit the model. It might be helpful to discuss this aspect as well. [1] IMPALA: Scalable Distributed Deep-RL with Importance Weighted Actor-Learner Architectures. Espeholt et al., 2018 [2] Deep transformer q-networks for partially observable reinforcement learning. Esslinger et al., 2022 [3] Stabilizing Deep Q-Learning with ConvNets and Vision Transformers under Data Augmentation. Hansen et al., 2021

**Broader Impact Concerns:**
No concerns

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes
paper_title_zh: 《强化学习中Transformer的调查》
paper_abstract_zh: Transformer被认为是自然语言处理（NLP）和计算机视觉（CV）领域的主导神经架构，主要在监督学习环境下。最近，在强化学习（RL）领域也出现了类似的Transformer应用热潮，但面临着由RL本质带来的独特设计选择和挑战。然而，Transformer在RL中的演变尚未得到充分揭示。在本文中，我们旨在系统地回顾在RL中使用Transformer的动机和进展，对现有工作进行分类，讨论每个子领域，并总结未来的前景。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
主要贡献：
- 本综述提供了Transformer架构在强化学习（RL）中不同应用的分类法，包括将Transformer作为状态编码器、世界模型或决策者（以决策-Transformer风格）。
- 作者还回顾了应用Transformer模型训练通用智能体的工作，无论是从头开始训练，还是通过微调或提示模型。
- 作者讨论了未来的前景和开放性问题。

**优点与不足：**
优点：
- 这是对一个新兴且有前景的研究领域的及时综述。文中提到的作品全面且具有代表性，涵盖了该领域的所有主要方面（据我所知）。
- 作者提供了关于RL中模型架构发展的简要历史视角，并讨论了在RL领域应用Transformer的挑战，例如非静态训练数据问题。这为主讨论设定了充分的背景。

不足（具体细节请参见“请求的更改”）：
- 对引用论文的描述有少数不准确之处。
- 一些论断缺乏充分支持或需要重新措辞。
- 缺少一些引用。

**请求的更改：**
我只有一些非关键的请求：
引用论文描述不准确：
- 在3.2节中，“Emmons等人（2021年）指出，仔细选择……对DRL智能体性能至关重要。”该论文仅讨论了离线RL。
- 在5节中，关于“为决策问题定制的Transformer结构”：Zhou等人，2021年并非NLP论文。如果作者想提及高效的Transformer变体，Tay等人，2022年（已引用）应有指向代表性作品的指针。

可疑论断：
- 在引言中，“RL智能体的训练目标通常是当前策略的函数，这在学习Transformer时引入了非静态性。”非静态性并非由在训练目标中使用策略引起，而是由使用不断变化的策略收集训练数据引起。
- 4.2节，“基于Transformer的世界模型可以帮助减轻对更长序列的预测误差。”请添加引用以支持这一论断。

缺少的引用：
- 在讨论DRL中的架构时，请考虑引用IMPALA [1]。
- 深度Transformer Q网络 [2] 使用Transformer并将观察历史作为输入，Bellman损失是针对多个时间步一起训练的。
- [3] 讨论了将ViT应用于RL。

错别字：
- 4.4.2节：“直接应用大型语言模型进行执行是低效的甚至可行的”。feasible -> infeasible或unfeasible。

额外建议：
- 在引言和3.2节中，作者讨论了将Transformer应用于RL问题的几个挑战。我认为另一个可能的原因是，与具有强归纳偏置的模型（如CNN、RNN）相比，Transformer模型通常需要更多的训练数据才能有效。在传统DRL中，样本效率是一个关键基准，这限制了智能体可以收集多少数据来拟合模型。讨论这一方面可能也有帮助。

[1] IMPALA: Scalable Distributed Deep-RL with Importance Weighted Actor-Learner Architectures. Espeholt et al., 2018
[2] Deep transformer q-networks for partially observable reinforcement learning. Esslinger et al., 2022
[3] Stabilizing Deep Q-Learning with ConvNets and Vision Transformers under Data Augmentation. Hansen et al., 2021

**更广泛的影响关切：**
无关切

**论断与证据：**
是

**受众：**
是

reasons: A few claims are not well supported or need rephrasing.
The non-stationary is not caused by using the policy in the training objective.
It's caused by the training data being collected using an ever-changing policy.
This is a timely survey for an emerging and promising research area.

paper_title: What is open peer review? A systematic review
paper_abstract:
Background : “Open peer review” (OPR), despite being a major pillar of Open Science, has neither a standardized definition nor an agreed schema of its features and implementations. The literature reflects this, with numerous overlapping and contradictory definitions. While for some the term refers to peer review where the identities of both author and reviewer are disclosed to each other, for others it signifies systems where reviewer reports are published alongside articles. For others it signifies both of these conditions, and for yet others it describes systems where not only “invited experts” are able to comment. For still others, it includes a variety of combinations of these and other novel methods. 
 Methods : Recognising the absence of a consensus view on what open peer review is, this article undertakes a systematic review of definitions of “open peer review” or “open review”, to create a corpus of 122 definitions. These definitions are systematically analysed to build a coherent typology of the various innovations in peer review signified by the term, and hence provide the precise technical definition currently lacking. 
 Results : This quantifiable data yields rich information on the range and extent of differing definitions over time and by broad subject area. Quantifying definitions in this way allows us to accurately portray exactly how ambiguously the phrase “open peer review” has been used thus far, for the literature offers 22 distinct configurations of seven traits, effectively meaning that there are 22 different definitions of OPR in the literature reviewed. 
 Conclusions : I propose a pragmatic definition of open peer review as an umbrella term for a number of overlapping ways that peer review models can be adapted in line with the aims of Open Science, including making reviewer and author identities open, publishing review reports and enabling greater participation in the peer review process.
review_content:
This is an interesting paper addressing a question that is important to journal editors and publishers as well as the wider ‘open science’ community, namely what is meant by open peer review. I have three significant concerns that need to be addressed, followed by more minor annotations and comments.


Major issues, in the order they arise in the article
 1. Would this meet most established criteria for a systematic review? Although the author completes a PRISMA checklist, he also notes firstly that he searched Web of Science, then that he added a bunch of other sources, and finally, “This set of articles was further enriched with 42 definitions from sources found through searching for the same terms in other academic databases (e.g., Google Scholar, JSTOR, disciplinary databases), Google (for blog articles) and Google Books (for books), as well as following citations in relevant bibliographies and literature reviews." This suggests that it is not really systematic (although the author is to be applauded for providing the data he worked from). There is a lack of clarity about the universe of literature that is being assessed, and of details about how it was assessed. In my view, the article is still a worthwhile undertaking, despite being non-systematic, but the title ought to reflect this.
 2. In my view the author does not pay enough attention to one important variant of open review, namely real-time review in the open, in which either invited reviewers or ‘the crowd’ comment on an article, with comments being posted as they are ready, rather than at the end of a formal process of peer review and decision-making. Conversely, the inclusion of ‘open platforms’ seems very confusing to me, as they do not have many of the criteria of openness that define the other flavours of open review that the author describes, but instead are about decoupling peer review from publication. Indeed Figure 6 makes plain that as a trait open platforms only occur twice in the 122 definitions considered. I would bet that the ‘real-time’ variant occurs far more often, and ought to be included as one of the key traits within the umbrella definition.
 3. In a paper that aims to define open peer review, it is unfortunate that the author doesn’t spend longer considering alternative definitions of peer review. Throughout the article he appears to conflate editorial selection (whether a journal accepts a manuscript) with technical review (whether the work is sound and properly reported). Thus when he talks about the “problems with peer review” he is sometimes talking about reviewers not spotting technical problems, sometimes about editors rejecting articles that don’t suit their taste, and sometimes about authors going through cycles of editorial rejection to achieve a high impact publication. Conflating these various things does not provide a sound foundation on which to build a definition of open peer review. This conflation is made worse when, for example, it is implied that the only reason for retraction is error. Thus most of the first three paragraphs of the ‘background’ section, and much of what follows about biases, incentives and wastefulness are muddled, and the references and evidence do not all support the broad claims made about ‘peer review’ (itself an ‘umbrella term’).


More minor concerns, with page numbers (PDF version) of the corresponding text
  * Abstract and later: The author needs to decide throughout the article whether he is singular (as he appears to be) or uses the royal ‘we’.
  * p7 – it is not helpful to list the seven types of openness without definitions. Even if the lengthy discussion of them follows later, I was desperate for some brief definition, in particular for the last two, and was labouring under a misapprehension about the meaning of the fourth, until much later in the article when I discovered what was meant by ‘open pre-review manuscripts’.
  * p8 – proponents of open identity review in medicine would also point out that it makes conflicts of interest much more apparent and subject to scrutiny.
  * p8 – some journals use open reports without open identities – i.e. posting reports with published articles but without identifying the reviewer (e.g. http://embor.embopress.org/about#Transparent_Process). The author writes as if open reports must always have open identities.
  * p10 – I think ‘open pre-review manuscripts’ is the wrong name for what the author is describing. At first I thought this meant the practice of posting the authors’ version of a manuscript alongside the peer review history (as is done by The BMJ, for example). But I think the author means ‘Open posting before formal review’ (which some call preprints). He might like to consider the suggestions by Neylon et al. about this issue of terminology (http://biorxiv.org/content/early/2016/12/09/092817)
  * p10 – I wonder if the author has any evidence that PubPeer has been ‘a major influence’?
  * p11 – I don’t think ‘open platforms’ is the right term either. (Although as noted above, I don’t really think this section belongs in the discussion at all, if it is to remain I would strongly recommend renaming it.) In publishing terms a platform is ‘where’ you publish articles, and the author is here discussing an aspect of how you get to the point of publication, and in particular peer review services (which as far as I can tell de facto meet only rather limited criteria of openness). I think what the author is describing is peer review options decoupled from journals (see Priem and Hemminger, Front Comput Neurosci 2012; 6: 19) and as noted I don’t understand why these have a place in a definition of open peer review.
  * p11 – Conclusion. I don’t believe the author presents a unified definition of open peer review, for all the reasons discussed above, but he does present most of the traits that together come under the umbrella term.
paper_title_zh: 什么是开放同行评审？一项系统性综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：尽管“开放同行评审”（Open Peer Review, OPR）是开放科学的重要支柱，但它既没有标准化的定义，也没有其特征和实施方式的一致性方案。文献反映了这一点，存在众多重叠且相互矛盾的定义。对一些人来说，这一术语指的是作者和评审者身份相互公开的同行评审；对另一些人来说，它指的是评审报告与文章一同发布的系统。还有一些人认为它同时包含这两种条件，而还有一些人则用它来描述不仅“受邀专家”能够发表评论的系统。还有一些人认为它包括这些和其他新方法的多种组合。

方法：鉴于对开放同行评审缺乏共识性观点，本文对“开放同行评审”或“开放评审”的定义进行了系统综述，构建了一个包含122个定义的语料库。这些定义被系统分析，以构建一个由该术语所表示的同行评审各种创新的连贯类型学，从而提供目前缺乏的精确技术定义。

结果：这些可量化的数据提供了关于不同定义的范围和程度的丰富信息，这些定义随时间和广泛学科领域而变化。以这种方式量化定义使我们能够准确描绘出“开放同行评审”这一短语迄今为止的使用是多么模糊，因为文献中提供了22种七种特征的独特组合，实际上意味着在所综述的文献中有22种不同的OPR定义。

结论：我提出一个实用定义，将开放同行评审作为一个伞式术语，涵盖多种重叠的同行评审模型适应方式，以符合开放科学的目标，包括公开评审者和作者的身份、发布评审报告以及促进更大程度的参与同行评审过程。
review_content_zh:
这是一篇有趣的论文，探讨了期刊编辑、出版商以及更广泛的“开放科学”社区都关注的重要问题，即什么是开放同行评审。我有三个需要解决的重大关切，随后是一些较小的注解和评论。

重大问题，按文章中出现的顺序排列：
1. 这是否符合大多数已建立的系统综述标准？尽管作者完成了一份PRISMA清单，但他也首先指出他搜索了Web of Science，然后添加了一堆其他来源，最后，“这组文章通过在其他学术数据库（例如Google Scholar、JSTOR、学科数据库）中搜索相同术语，Google（用于博客文章）和Google Books（用于书籍），以及跟踪相关书目和文献综述中的引用，进一步丰富了42个定义。”这表明它并不真正系统（尽管作者因提供了他所使用的数据而值得称赞）。关于所评估的文献范围及其评估细节缺乏清晰度。在我看来，尽管是非系统的，但文章仍是一项有价值的尝试，但标题应当反映这一点。
2. 在我看来，作者没有足够关注开放评审的一个重要变体，即实时公开评审，其中受邀评审者或“大众”对文章进行评论，评论一旦准备好就发布，而不是在同行评审和决策过程的最后。相反，对我来说，“开放平台”的纳入似乎非常令人困惑，因为它们并没有具备作者描述的其他开放评审类型所定义的许多开放性标准，而是关于将同行评审与出版分离。事实上，图6清楚地表明，作为特征，开放平台在所考虑的122个定义中仅出现两次。我敢打赌，“实时”变体出现的频率要高得多，应当作为伞式定义中的关键特征之一。
3. 在一篇旨在定义开放同行评审的论文中，不幸的是作者没有花更多时间考虑同行评审的替代定义。通读全文，他似乎将编辑选择（期刊是否接受手稿）与技术评审（工作是否可靠且报告得当）混为一谈。因此，当他说“同行评审的问题”时，有时是指评审者没有发现技术问题，有时是指编辑拒绝不符合他们口味的文章，有时是指作者经历多次编辑拒绝以实现高影响因子发表。混淆这些不同的事物并不能为构建开放同行评审的定义提供坚实的基础。当例如暗示撤稿的唯一原因是错误时，这种混淆变得更加严重。因此，“背景”部分的前三段大部分内容以及随后关于偏见、激励和浪费的讨论都是混乱的，参考文献和证据并不都支持对“同行评审”（本身也是一个“伞式术语”）的广泛主张。

较小的关切，附有相应文本的页码（PDF版本）：
* 摘要及之后：作者需要在全文中决定他是用单数（如他所表现的那样）还是使用“我们”的皇家用法。
* 第7页——在没有定义的情况下列出七种开放类型是没有帮助的。即使后面有长篇讨论，我也迫切需要一些简要定义，尤其是最后两个，直到文章很后面我才弄清楚“开放预评审手稿”的意思，之前一直对第四个有误解。
* 第8页——医学中开放身份评审的支持者也会指出，这使得利益冲突更加明显并受到审查。
* 第8页——一些期刊使用开放报告但不公开身份——即发布与已发表文章一起的报告但不公开评审者身份（例如http://embor.embopress.org/about#Transparent_Process）。作者写道，开放报告必须总是有公开身份。
* 第10页——我认为“开放预评审手稿”是作者所描述内容的错误名称。起初我以为这是指发布作者版本的手稿以及同行评审历史（例如The BMJ就是这样做的）。但我想作者是指“正式评审前的开放发布”（有些人称之为预印本）。他或许可以考虑Neylon等人关于这一术语问题的建议（http://biorxiv.org/content/early/2016/12/09/092817）。
* 第10页——我想知道作者是否有证据表明PubPeer是“一个主要影响”？
* 第11页——我认为“开放平台”也不是正确的术语。（尽管如上所述，如果这一部分要保留，我并不真的认为它属于讨论范畴，但我强烈建议重命名。）在出版术语中，平台是“你发布文章的地方”，而作者在这里讨论的是如何达到出版点的方面，特别是同行评审服务（据我所知，这些服务实际上只符合相当有限的开放性标准）。我认为作者所描述的是与期刊分离的同行评审选项（参见Priem和Hemminger，Front Comput Neurosci 2012; 6: 19），如前所述，我不明白为什么这些在开放同行评审的定义中有位置。
* 第11页——结论。由于上述所有原因，我不相信作者提出了一个统一的开放同行评审定义，但他确实呈现了大多数属于伞式术语的特征。

paper_title: Harmful Effects of the Microplastic Pollution on Animal Health . A Literature Review
paper_abstract: Background.The environmental pollution by microplastics is a global problem arising from the extensive production and use of plastics. Small particles of different plastics, measured less than 5 mm in diameter, are found in water, air, soil, and various living organisms around the globe. The humans constantly inhale and ingest these particles. The associated health risks raise major concerns and require dedicated evaluation.
review_content: Reviewer 3 Dear Angela, Thank you for careful evaluation of our manuscript. We corrected the manuscript according to your comments: Could you please ensure that “MP” is written in a consistent way through the text? A couple of times it is written “MPs” and it is not clear to me if it is done just by mistake or as a purpose. – “MPs” corrected to “MP”
paper_title_zh: 微塑料污染对动物健康的危害：文献综述
paper_abstract_zh: 背景。微塑料造成的环境污染是一个全球性问题，源于塑料的广泛生产和使用。直径小于5毫米的不同塑料小颗粒在全球范围内的水、空气、土壤和各种生物体中被发现。人类不断吸入和摄入这些颗粒。相关的健康风险引发了重大关切，并需要专门的评估。

paper_title: Intrinsic negative feedback as a limiting factor for the evolution of higher forms of intelligence
paper_abstract: Longstanding scientific efforts have been dedicated to answer why and how our particular intelligence is generated by our brain but not by the brain of other species. However, surprisingly little effort has been made to ask why no other species ever developed an intelligence similar to ours. Here, I explore this question based on genetic and paleontologic evidence. Contrary to the established view, this review suggests that the developmental hurdles alone are not high enough to explain the uniqueness of human intelligence (HI). As an additional explanation I propose that HI is normally not retained by natural selection, because it is, under most conditions, an intrinsically unfavourable trait. This unfavourableness, however, cannot be explained by physical constraints alone; rather, it may also be rooted in the same emotional and social complexity that is necessary for the development of HI. Thus, a major obstacle towards HI may not be solely the development of the required physical assets, but also to cope with harmful individual, social and environmental feedback intrinsically associated with this trait.
review_content:
The manuscript discusses the uniqueness of human intelligence (HI) despite its apparent evolutionary advantages. Although the theme has been tirelessly revisited by many authors, a new theory is offered, that higher intelligence is disadvantageous and kept from developing through negative feedback. The author briefly goes through the main molecular and ecological arguments for the appearance and advantages of high intelligence, showing that those are not especially uncommon or slow in evolutionary history. Therefore, none could fully justify the evolution of HI, suggesting it to be generally an unfavorable trait.

The theory is well constructed and the references support the hypothesis. Despite that, there are a few points in the manuscript that warrant attention:

Page 3 - "Brain size, structure, and complexity"
The author affirms that "In terms of genetic modifications, the development of the human brain therefore appears to be based on extending already existing features through gradual and common mechanisms, rather than being the result of a developmental quantum leap" (page 3, para 5, line 33). The example given a few lines before, of Pax6, as well as other well known genes, such as the human-specific ARHGAP11B, despite being relatively small changes, result in significant leaps in brain development. The later example of octopuses also seems to indicate a sudden change, from the moment molluscs lost their shells, which still supports the paragraph conclusion that the genetic mechanisms that allow intelligence are available to other species.

Page 5 - "Language and intelligence"
In general, this session is not clear about language being a requirement for the development of HI, a mere consequence of it, or something in between, with some contradictions. For example "It is therefore not the capacity for an articulate vocalization, but only a predisposition for it, that is essential to the evolution of HI" (page 5, para 5, line 11) and "current evidence suggests that the evolution of a HI-supporting language is not a feature strictly limited to humans or the human brain anatomy or speech production" (page 5, para 7, line 6). The conclusion is especially confusing when declaring "HI-supporting language" while the manuscript appears to state that language is not a prerequisite for HI.
About the passage:
"Let us now consider language syntax and acquisition with respect to human uniqueness. It has indeed been proposed that such properties of the human language are neither specific to language nor to humans (47,48)" (page 5, para 6, line 1). The references cited (47, 48) indicate that there may be a human-only syntax, either through universal grammar or simply an advanced form of syntax allowed by the human FLB.

Page 7 - "Conclusion and outlook"
Despite mentioning the possible negative feedback from molecular complexity, I couldn't find any examination of it in the main text. For reference: "the main barrier towards HI is not only the development of the required physical assets, but also that negative feedback from social, behavioural and molecular complexity, as well as negative environmental feedback make the development of HI increasingly unfavourable" (page 7, para 4, line 11).
I wonder if there is a link between HI and sexual selection. Although intelligence as a simple fitness indicator would be equally accessible to other animals as well, cultural and behavioral products could also have influenced mating preferences.

Finally, the text mentions the possible negative feedback of niche construction: page 7, "there might be a different type of negative feedback loop intrinsic to HI—HI might simply allow a species to become so successful in exploiting food resources that these resources become exhausted" (page 7, para 3, line 1) and again on the conclusion "we are knowingly and consciously pursuing our unsustainable development that is rapidly destroying the resources upon which we critically depend" (page 7, para 6, line 6). Despite that, HI also generates powerful positive feedback with niche construction, in which the environmental changes produced by HI favor HI itself.
paper_title_zh: 内在负反馈作为限制高阶智能演化的因素
paper_abstract_zh: 长期以来，科学界致力于解答为什么以及如何我们特定的大脑产生了智能，而其他物种的大脑却没有。然而，令人惊讶的是，几乎没有努力去探讨为什么没有其他物种发展出类似我们人类的智能。本文基于遗传学和古生物学的证据探讨了这一问题。与现有观点相反，本文认为仅凭发展障碍不足以解释人类智能（HI）的独特性。作为补充解释，我提出HI通常不会被自然选择保留，因为在大多数条件下，它本质上是一个不利的特征。然而，这种不利性不能仅通过物理限制来解释；它可能还根植于发展HI所必需的相同的情感和社会复杂性中。因此，HI的主要障碍可能不仅仅是发展所需的物理条件，还包括应对与这一特征内在相关的有害的个体、社会和环境反馈。
review_content_zh:
手稿讨论了人类智能（HI）的独特性，尽管其具有明显的进化优势。尽管许多作者不懈地重新探讨这一主题，但本文提出了一种新理论，即高智能是不利的，并通过负面反馈阻止其发展。作者简要概述了支持高智能出现和优势的主要分子和生态论点，表明这些在进化史上并不特别罕见或缓慢。因此，没有任何论点能完全解释HI的进化，暗示HI通常是一种不利特征。

该理论构建良好，参考文献支持了假设。尽管如此，手稿中仍有一些值得注意的点：

第3页 - “大脑的大小、结构和复杂性”
作者断言：“从基因修饰的角度来看，人类大脑的发展因此似乎是基于通过渐进和常见机制扩展已存在的特征，而不是发育上的量子跃迁的结果”（第3页，第5段，第33行）。几行前给出的Pax6的例子，以及其他众所周知的基因，如人类特有的ARHGAP11B，尽管变化相对较小，却导致了大脑发育的显著跃迁。后文提到的章鱼例子也似乎表明了一个突然的变化，从软体动物失去外壳的那一刻起，这仍然支持该段落的结论，即允许智能的遗传机制对其他物种也是可用的。

第5页 - “语言与智能”
总的来说，这一部分关于语言是否是HI发展的必要条件、仅仅是其结果，或介于两者之间，存在一些矛盾。例如，“因此，并非是清晰发音的能力，而只是对其的倾向，才是HI进化的关键”（第5页，第5段，第11行）以及“当前证据表明，支持HI的语言进化并非严格限于人类或人类大脑解剖结构或言语产生”（第5页，第7段，第6行）。结论尤其令人困惑，当声明“支持HI的语言”时，手稿似乎表明语言并非HI的先决条件。
关于这段话：
“现在让我们考虑语言的句法和习得与人类独特性的关系。确实有观点认为，人类语言的这些属性既非语言特有，也非人类特有”（第5页，第6段，第1行）。引用的参考文献（47, 48）表明可能存在人类独有的句法，无论是通过普遍语法还是人类FLB允许的先进句法形式。

第7页 - “结论与展望”
尽管提到了分子复杂性的可能负面反馈，我在正文主体中未能找到对此的任何考察。参考：“HI的主要障碍不仅是所需物理资产的发展，还有来自社会、行为和分子复杂性的负面反馈，以及负面环境反馈，使得HI的发展越来越不利”（第7页，第4段，第11行）。
我想知道HI与性选择之间是否存在联系。尽管智能作为简单的适应度指标对其他动物同样适用，但文化和行为产物也可能影响了择偶偏好。

最后，文本提到了生态位构建的可能负面反馈：第7页，“可能存在一种与HI内在的不同类型的负面反馈循环——HI可能仅仅使物种在利用食物资源方面如此成功，以至于这些资源被耗尽”（第7页，第3段，第1行），以及在结论中再次提到“我们有意识地追求不可持续的发展，这正在迅速摧毁我们赖以生存的关键资源”（第7页，第6段，第6行）。尽管如此，HI也在生态位构建中产生了强大的正面反馈，其中HI产生的环境变化有利于HI本身。

reasons: The theory is well constructed and the references support the hypothesis.
The references cited (47, 48) indicate that there may be a human-only syntax, either through universal grammar or simply an advanced form of syntax allowed by the human FLB.
Despite mentioning the possible negative feedback from molecular complexity, I couldn't find any examination of it in the main text.

paper_title: Uncertainty in Graph Neural Networks: A Survey
paper_abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been extensively used in various real-world applications. However, the predictive uncertainty of GNNs stemming from diverse sources such as inherent randomness in data and model training errors can lead to unstable and erroneous predictions. Therefore, identifying, quantifying, and utilizing uncertainty are essential to enhance the performance of the model for the downstream tasks as well as the reliability of the GNN predictions. This survey aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the GNNs from the perspective of uncertainty with an emphasis on its integration in graph learning. We compare and summarize existing graph uncertainty theory and methods, alongside the corresponding downstream tasks. Thereby, we bridge the gap between theory and practice, meanwhile connecting different GNN communities. Moreover, our work provides valuable insights into promising directions in this field.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This paper presents a survey on uncertainty estimation, quantification and utilisation in graph machine learning.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
On the surface level, I think that this work delivers what it promises: there is a survey of a sizeable number of publications relating to GNNs and uncertainty, these publications are reasonably organised in a structure imposed by the authors, and some avenues for future work in the area are identified. From that perspective, the effort invested by the authors could be considered worthy of a publication at TMLR. However, I also consider TMLR's criteria to place surveys in a bit of a gray area. I personally think the main utility from the surveys should come not only from an enumeration and organisation of a reference list, but also for conveying a useful opinion or argumentation that practitioners can follow when deciding which method to use. Presently, the survey does not meet this criterion in my mind. In a lot of cases, a paper is simply introduced, briefly summarised in isolation, and then the survey simply moves on to the next one. It is very rare that I see the authors' own opinions and anecdotal experiences introduced, and as a result this wouldn't necessarily be a survey that would give a lot of value beyond an organisational skeleton. Additionally, I think that there are several places where additional references and contexts could have been provided to make the story more accurate and robust (see next section for suggestions).

**Requested Changes:**
A major requested change is to introduce more of the Authors' own opinions in this survey. Try to make a clear stand about which methods should be used in which circumstances, with some levels of argumentation. Additionally, it would be useful to make a stand about whether certain papers are able to properly defend their hypothesis, or more investigation may be needed. I think it might make sense to correct this attribution to DropEdge: > Rong et al. (2019) introduce DropEdge, which randomly removes a specified number of edges from the graph by drawing independent Bernoulli random variables (with a constant rate) during each training iteration. This is not completely factually correct. Rong et al. are the first to _theoretically analyse_ edge dropout, but they are definitely not the first paper to attempt edge dropout as a regulariser. I'm not sure what's the first paper to do it, but for example, even the GAT paper (Veličković et al., ICLR'18) leverages such an operator (without theoretical motivation, of course). I also believe some sections would benefit from significantly more references being discussed. The two sections that immediately come to mind as examples are **explainability** and **robustness**. Presently, the explainability discussion in the paper doesn't go far beyond GNNExplainer. While GNNExplainer was the landmark paper in this space, there's been _a lot_ of developments since then. Papers such as GraphLIME, or GCExplainer, for example, are worth discussing. Similarly, the robustness section appears to largely neglect work on robustness certification from the folks at TUM (e.g. Simon Geisler or Aleksandar Bojchevski, et al.) which would likely also be worthy of inclusion here.

**Claims And Evidence:**
No

**Audience:**
Yes
paper_title_zh: 图神经网络中的不确定性：综述
paper_abstract_zh: 图神经网络（GNNs）已被广泛应用于各种现实世界场景中。然而，GNNs的预测不确定性源于多种因素，如数据固有的随机性和模型训练误差，可能导致预测不稳定和错误。因此，识别、量化和利用不确定性对于提升模型在下游任务中的性能以及GNN预测的可靠性至关重要。本综述旨在从不确定性的角度对GNNs进行全面概述，重点强调其在图学习中的整合。我们比较和总结了现有的图不确定性理论与方法，以及相应的下游任务。由此，我们弥合了理论与实践之间的差距，同时连接了不同的GNN社区。此外，我们的工作为该领域的有前景方向提供了宝贵的见解。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文对图机器学习中的不确定性估计、量化和利用进行了综述。

**优点与不足：**
从表面上看，我认为这项工作实现了其承诺：对大量与GNN和不确定性相关的出版物进行了综述，这些出版物被作者以合理的结构组织，并识别了该领域未来工作的若干方向。从这个角度来看，作者投入的努力可以被认为是值得在TMLR上发表的。然而，我也认为TMLR对综述的评判标准略显模糊。我个人认为，综述的主要价值不仅应来自参考列表的列举和组织，还应在于传达有用的观点或论证，以供实践者在决定使用哪种方法时参考。目前，这篇综述在我看来并未达到这一标准。在许多情况下，论文只是被简单介绍，孤立地简要总结，然后综述就继续下一篇。很少看到作者自己的观点和轶事经验被引入，因此这篇综述除了提供一个组织框架外，并不一定能提供更多价值。此外，我认为有几处可以补充更多参考文献和背景，以使论述更加准确和稳健（具体建议见下一节）。

**请求的修改：**
一个主要的修改请求是在综述中引入更多作者自己的观点。尝试明确在不同情况下应使用哪些方法，并提供一定程度的论证。此外，对某些论文是否能够有效支持其假设，或是否需要进一步研究，也应明确表态。我认为有必要更正对DropEdge的归属：> Rong等人（2019年）介绍了DropEdge，它在每次训练迭代中通过独立伯努利随机变量（具有恒定速率）随机移除指定数量的边。这并不完全符合事实。Rong等人是首次**理论分析**边丢弃的，但他们绝非首次尝试将边丢弃作为正则化的论文。我不确定第一篇这样做的论文是哪篇，但例如，即使是GAT论文（Veličković等人，ICLR'18）也使用了这样的操作（当然没有理论动机）。我还认为某些部分会因讨论更多参考文献而显著受益。立即想到的两个例子是**可解释性**和**鲁棒性**部分。目前，论文中对可解释性的讨论并未超出GNNExplainer。虽然GNNExplainer是这一领域的里程碑论文，但此后已有大量发展。例如，GraphLIME或GCExplainer等论文值得讨论。同样，鲁棒性部分似乎在很大程度上忽略了TUM团队（如Simon Geisler或Aleksandar Bojchevski等人）在鲁棒性认证方面的工作，这些工作可能也值得在此包括。

**主张与证据：**
无

**受众：**
是
