paper_title: A Comprehensive Study of Real-Time Object Detection Networks Across Multiple Domains: A Survey
paper_abstract: Deep neural network based object detectors are continuously evolving and are used in a multitude of applications, each having its own set of requirements. While safety-critical applications need high accuracy and reliability, low-latency tasks need resource and energy-efficient networks. Real-time detection networks, which are a necessity in high-impact real-world applications, are continuously proposed but they overemphasize the improvements in accuracy and speed while other capabilities such as versatility, robustness, resource, and energy efficiency are omitted. A reference benchmark for existing networks does not exist nor does a standard evaluation guideline for designing new networks, which results in ambiguous and inconsistent comparisons. We, therefore, conduct a comprehensive study on multiple real-time detection networks (anchor-based, keypoint-based, and transformer-based) on a wide range of datasets and report results on an extensive set of metrics. We also study the impact of variables such as image size, anchor dimensions, confidence thresholds, and architecture layers on the overall performance. We analyze the robustness of detection networks against distribution shift, natural corruptions, and adversarial attacks. Also, we provide the calibration analysis to gauge the reliability of the predictions. Finally, to highlight the real-world impact, we conduct two unique case studies, on autonomous driving and healthcare application. To further gauge the capability of networks in critical real-time applications, we report the performance after deploying the detection networks on edge devices. Our extensive empirical study can act as a guideline for the industrial community to make an informed choice on the existing networks. We also hope to inspire the research community towards a new direction of design and evaluation of networks that focuses on the bigger and holistic overview for a far-reaching impact.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
The paper is a very detailed survey on the study of real time Object Detection Networks. The paper details and evaluates different detection heads with different backbone, different dataset and different hardware. There is no methodological novelty but the proposed study deals with an interesting problem in many aspects with many experiments.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
Strengths: - The paper is well written and easy to follow. - The study is clear and very well detailed. The paper is very complete with a lot of evaluation with different architecture and different dataset. I think this can be of great value to the community. - The applications considered are interesting Weaknesses: - Overfitting evaluation: It would be interesting to do an overfitting study by testing the different approaches considered with several seeds to better understand the significance of the results. Since there are a lot of approaches and a lot of datasets, maybe do it with a not too expensive configuration just to get an idea of the overfitting.

**Requested Changes:**
I would like to see a study on overfitting but this is not critical as the paper is already very exhaustive.

**Broader Impact Concerns:**
Nothing special to mention .

**Rebuttal Comments:**
Response to Reviewer fya1: Thank you for your feedback. We have added an overfitting study in the revised paper. We however chose the smaller medical imaging dataset due to time constraints. We trained all 8 detectors (with one backbone-HarDNet68) on the Kvasir-SEG dataset for two more seeds and added the mean and standard deviation over the three seeds for the relevant metrics in Table 11 (changes in blue).
paper_title_zh: 跨多域实时目标检测网络综合研究：综述
paper_abstract_zh: 基于深度神经网络的物体检测器不断演进，并应用于众多领域，每个领域都有其特定的需求。虽然安全关键型应用需要高精度和高可靠性，低延迟任务则需要资源和能源高效的网络。实时检测网络是高影响力现实应用中的必要条件，尽管不断有新的网络被提出，但它们过度强调精度和速度的提升，而忽略了多功能性、鲁棒性、资源效率和能源效率等其他能力。现有网络缺乏参考基准，也没有设计新网络的标准评估指南，导致比较模糊且不一致。因此，我们对多种实时检测网络（基于锚框、关键点和变换器）在广泛数据集上进行全面研究，并报告了大量指标的结果。我们还研究了图像大小、锚框维度、置信度阈值和架构层等变量对整体性能的影响。我们分析了检测网络对分布偏移、自然干扰和对抗性攻击的鲁棒性。此外，我们提供了校准分析以评估预测的可靠性。最后，为突出现实世界的影响，我们进行了两个独特的案例研究，分别针对自动驾驶和医疗保健应用。为进一步评估网络在关键实时应用中的能力，我们报告了在边缘设备上部署检测网络后的性能。我们广泛的实证研究可作为工业界选择现有网络的指南。我们也希望激励研究社区朝着新的设计和评估网络方向迈进，关注更宏大和全面的影响。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文是对实时目标检测网络研究的非常详细的综述。文章详细描述并评估了不同检测头与不同主干网络、不同数据集和不同硬件的组合。尽管没有方法论上的创新，但所提出的研究通过大量实验从多个角度处理了一个有趣的问题。

**优点与不足：**
优点：- 文章写作质量高，易于理解。- 研究清晰且非常详细。文章非常完整，包含大量对不同架构和不同数据集的评估。我认为这对社区具有很大价值。- 所考虑的应用场景有趣。
不足：- 过拟合评估：通过使用多个种子测试所考虑的不同方法来进行过拟合研究将是有趣的，以便更好地理解结果的意义。由于方法众多且数据集丰富，或许可以采用不太昂贵的配置来进行，以初步了解过拟合情况。

**请求的修改：**
我希望看到关于过拟合的研究，但这并非关键，因为文章已经非常详尽。

**更广泛的影响关注：**
无特别提及之处。

**反驳意见：**
对评审者fya1的回应：感谢您的反馈。我们在修订稿中增加了过拟合研究。然而，由于时间限制，我们选择了较小的医学成像数据集。我们在Kvasir-SEG数据集上对全部8个检测器（使用一个主干网络-HarDNet68）进行了两个额外种子的训练，并在表11中添加了相关指标在三个种子上的均值和标准差（蓝色部分为修改内容）。

paper_title: Systematic review and meta-analysis on the effect of continuous subjective tinnitus on attention and habituation
paper_abstract: Background: Attention and habituation are two domains known to play key roles in the perception and maintenance of tinnitus. The heterogeneous nature of tinnitus and the methodologies adopted by various studies make it difficult to generalize findings. The current review aims at assessing and synthesizing evidence on the possible roles of attention and habituation in continuous subjective tinnitus.
review_content: Reviewer 2 Additional comments This revised version of the manuscript is improved over the previous. Most of the previous concerns have been addressed adequately by the authors. I refer to line (L) below. Comment 1: Two versions of the abstract are provided. One in the system and one in the actual text. Response 1: We have now updated the abstract in the system. Thank you for pointing it out. Comment 2: L75 and elsewhere. I still think it would be more appropriate to not abbreviate “don’t” and write “do not”. Response 2: Agreed. We have corrected it now. Comment 3: L79-101. I still believe that habituation needs fuller explanation. Habituation to external sound sources may be different from habituation to tinnitus. The latter may be influenced by many different factors. “sensory gating” still needs to be defined. The link between habituation and electrophysiological measures needs to be more clearly explained and a rationale why the latter is a reasonable measure of habituation is needed. Response 3: Thank you for letting us know. The points you have mentioned is valuable. We have added the necessary information in the introduction section now. Changes made: Habituation to an external sound may be different from habituation to the internal sounds like tinnitus. Since there are no standardized test to study habituation to tinnitus, measures like P50 can be used to evaluate the sensory gating thereby indirectly assessing habituation. “Sensory gating” is a phenomenon where the brain automatically analyses the incoming stream of information based on its salience to determine the weight that must be given to the stimulus. P50, is an electrophysiological measure that is used widely to evaluate the sensory gating mechanism at the thalamo-cortical level using a paired click paradigm. The redundant or the second click in the paradigm is given less importance, which is observed as reduced P50 amplitude for the redundant stimuli. Individuals having schizophrenia are reported have reduced sensory gating abilities (Shen et al., 2020). With respect to sensory gating in tinnitus population, there are only a handful of studies that have assessed sensory gating in tinnitus experimentally suggesting affected sensory gating in individuals with tinnitus (Campbell, Bean, & LaBrec, 2018; Campbell, LaBrec, Bean, Nielsen, & So, 2019) while others suggested it to be normal (Dornhoffer, Danner, Mennemeier, Blake, & Garcia-Rill, 2006). Comment 4: L85. Consider removing “&” before “habituation”. Response 4: We have removed “&” before “habituation” Comment 5: L103-110. I think that the argument that the review is essential is still not a strong argument since no actual new reasoning has been added. Response 5: We have now updated the need for the review in the introduction. We hope this makes a strong need for the review. Changes made The current review differs from the existing reviews (Cardon et al., 2020; Clarke, Henshaw, Akeroyd, Adams, & Hoare, 2020) in such a way that, we explore the effect of continuous tinnitus on attention and habituation solely instead of cognition as a whole. Assessing these two specifically in individuals with tinnitus is crucial to understand the roles these domains play, the selection and development of appropriate therapies. In addition, the existing reviews have not addressed the behavioral and electrophysiological indices of attention together nor have, they assessed attention in tinnitus by controlling confounders like hearing loss. Furthermore, existing reviews have included studies with pulsatile tinnitus making the group heterogenous. The current review aims to overcome the above by exploring the sustained effect of continuous and subjective tinnitus on attention and habituation using both behavioral and electrophysiological measures in adults. Comment 6: L110-113. I still think that the aim could be more clearly stated. It is still unclear what the study population is. I assume adults. Response 6: We have now added the study population in the aim. Changes: The current review aims to overcome the above by exploring the sustained effect of continuous and subjective tinnitus on attention and habituation using both behavioral and electrophysiological measures in adults. Comment 7: L283. Can a paradigm where the deviant stimulus occurs equal amount of times as the standard be considered to be an oddball-paradigm? Could it be an explanation as to why the largest range is seen for that study (see Figure 5)? Response 7: A ratio of 50:50 is not considered an odd ball. We have overlooked this in L283 It was an S1-S2 paradigm. This information has been corrected now. We hope this clarifies. Comment 8: L301. Add period at the end of the sentence. Response 8: We have added it now. Comment 9: L403-404. The last sentence seems to contradict what is stated on L375-380. L403-404: Therefore, the results of this review could stand as preliminary evidence for an attentional deficit in individuals with tinnitus. L375-380: Hearing loss commonly accompanies tinnitus. Eight studies either included individuals with hearing loss and/or did not test their participants’ hearing thresholds. Peripheral hearing can solely influence auditory selective attention, by increasing the time to form auditory objects or switch attention rapidly (Shinn-Cunningham & Best, 2008). Hence, hearing loss is a strong confounder and controlling hearing between the tinnitus and control groups are essential to comment on the influence of tinnitus on an individual's attentional abilities. Response 9: We have now added a statement on the effect of hearing on the results of the study. We hope this resolves the conflict aroused. Comment 10: L424-426. Please clarify what “A meta-analysis performed” refers to. Present study or a previous? Response 10: It refers to the present study. Thank you for pointing out the confusion. It has now been updated. Comment 11: L448-450. I am still not convinced that single case studies will provide much information. Response 11: In line448-450 we meant studying attention on each participant in the group will provide better information. However, the word choice used by us has created a confusion. We have now updated this and used “Studying different types of attention in each participant in the group..” Comment 12: L474. The abbreviation CNV is only mentioned in one of the tables prior to this occurrence. It would be easier for the reader to write out it here. Response 12: Yes, Agreed. It has now been corrected. Comment 13: Tables 1-4. It is unclear what order the articles in the tables are presented. Please use alphabetical order or similar. Response 13: Thank you for letting us know. We have now updated all the tables and used an alphabetical order to arrange the studies. Comment 14: Table 1. B, U, L and R need explanation. From a perceptual perspective one decimal is sufficient for assessments of loudness. Response 14: We have now given the elaboration for above short forms. Currently loudness of tinnitus is provided in dBSL. However, two studies have used Visual analogue Scale (VAS), hence we have noted the same and reported in the table. Comment 15: Table 2. From a perceptual perspective one decimal is sufficient for PTA results. I assume that PTA here stands for pure tone audiogram and not pure tone average. HFAHL needs definition (calculated from what frequencies?). Should it be “slopping” hearing loss and not “sloping”? Response 15: Thank you for pointing it out. We have now corrected sloping spelling in the table. The PTA in Table 2 stands for Pure Tone Audiometric Results. We have elaborated this in the footnotes. The average of PTA is provided in dBHL(decibel hearing level), which is usually the average of three frequency (500Hz, 1kHz and kHz). However, one study (Stevens et al 2007) has provided the HFAHL. We have elaborated the frequencies included for this average in the footnotes. Hope the information is clear now
paper_title_zh: 连续主观耳鸣对注意力和习惯化影响的系统综述和元分析
paper_abstract_zh: 背景：注意力和习惯化是已知在耳鸣感知和维持中起关键作用的两个领域。耳鸣的异质性和不同研究采用的方法论使得难以概括研究结果。本综述旨在评估和综合关于注意力和习惯化在持续性主观耳鸣中可能作用的证据。
review_content_zh:
审稿人2的补充评论

这篇修订后的手稿相较于之前的版本有所改进。作者已经充分地解决了大多数之前的关切。以下是我所指的行（L）。

评论1：提供了两个版本的摘要。一个在系统中，一个在实际文本中。

回复1：我们现在已经更新了系统中的摘要。感谢您的指出。

评论2：L75及其他地方。我仍然认为不缩写“don’t”而写成“do not”更为恰当。

回复2：同意。我们现在已经进行了更正。

评论3：L79-101。我仍然认为习惯化需要更全面的解释。对外部声源的习惯化可能与对耳鸣的习惯化不同。后者可能受到许多不同因素的影响。“感觉门控”仍需定义。习惯化与电生理测量之间的联系需要更清晰地解释，并需要说明为什么后者是衡量习惯化的合理指标。

回复3：感谢您的告知。您提到的观点很有价值。我们现在已经在引言部分添加了必要的信息。所做的更改：对外部声音的习惯化可能与对内部声音（如耳鸣）的习惯化不同。由于没有标准化测试来研究对耳鸣的习惯化，可以使用P50等测量来评估感觉门控，从而间接评估习惯化。“感觉门控”是一种现象，大脑自动分析传入的信息流，根据其显著性来确定必须给予刺激的权重。P50是一种广泛使用的电生理测量，用于通过成对点击范式评估丘脑-皮质水平的感觉门控机制。在该范式中，冗余的或第二个点击被赋予较低的重要性，表现为对冗余刺激的P50振幅降低。据报道，精神分裂症患者的感觉门控能力降低（Shen等，2020）。关于耳鸣人群的感觉门控，只有少数研究实验性地评估了耳鸣患者的感觉门控，表明耳鸣患者的感觉门控受到影响（Campbell, Bean, & LaBrec, 2018; Campbell, LaBrec, Bean, Nielsen, & So, 2019），而其他研究则认为其正常（Dornhoffer, Danner, Mennemeier, Blake, & Garcia-Rill, 2006）。

评论4：L85。考虑删除“&”之前的“习惯化”。

回复4：我们已经删除了“&”之前的“习惯化”。

评论5：L103-110。我认为关于综述是必要的论点仍然不够强，因为没有添加实际的新推理。

回复5：我们现在已经在引言中更新了综述的必要性。我们希望这能强化综述的必要性。

所做的更改：当前的综述与现有的综述（Cardon等，2020； 克拉克、亨肖、阿克罗伊德、亚当斯和霍尔（2020年）的研究方式是，我们专门探讨持续性耳鸣对注意力和习惯化的影响，而不是整体认知。在耳鸣患者中具体评估这两个方面对于理解这些领域的作用、选择和开发适当的治疗方法至关重要。此外，现有的综述并未同时涉及注意力的行为和电生理指标，也未通过控制如听力损失等混杂因素来评估耳鸣中的注意力。而且，现有综述包含了脉冲性耳鸣的研究，使得群体异质性增加。本综述旨在通过探讨持续性和主观性耳鸣对成年人的注意力和习惯化的持续影响，使用行为和电生理测量来克服上述问题。评论6：L110-113。我仍然认为研究目标可以更清晰地表述。目前仍不清楚研究对象是谁。我假设是成年人。回复6：我们现在已在目标中添加了研究对象。修改：本综述旨在通过探讨持续性和主观性耳鸣对成年人的注意力和习惯化的持续影响，使用行为和电生理测量来克服上述问题。评论7：L283。在偏差刺激与标准刺激出现次数相等的范式下，能否将其视为奇偶范式？这是否可以解释为何该研究（见图5）的范围最大？回复7：50:50的比例不被视为奇偶范式。我们在L283中忽略了这一点。它是一个S1-S2范式。这一信息现已更正。我们希望这能澄清问题。评论8：L301。在句子末尾添加句号。回复8：我们现在已添加。评论9：L403-404。最后一句似乎与L375-380中的陈述相矛盾。L403-404：因此，本综述的结果可以作为耳鸣个体存在注意力缺陷的初步证据。L375-380：听力损失通常伴随耳鸣。八项研究要么包括了有听力损失的个体，要么未测试参与者的听力阈值。外周听力可以通过增加形成听觉对象或快速切换注意力所需的时间（Shinn-Cunningham & Best, 2008）单独影响听觉选择性注意力。因此，听力损失是一个强烈的混杂因素，在耳鸣组和对照组之间控制听力对于评论耳鸣对个体注意力能力的影响至关重要。回复9：我们现在已添加关于听力对研究结果影响的声明。我们希望这能解决引起的冲突。评论10：L424-426。请澄清“进行的元分析”是指什么。当前研究还是之前的研究？回复10：它指的是当前研究。感谢您指出这一混淆。现已更新。 评论11：L448-450。我仍然不相信单一案例研究能提供太多信息。回复11：在L448-450中，我们的意思是研究小组中每个参与者的注意力将提供更好的信息。然而，我们使用的措辞造成了混淆。我们现在已经更新了这一点，使用了“研究小组中每个参与者的不同类型的注意力...”。评论12：L474。CNV这一缩写在此前的一个表格中仅提及一次。对读者来说，在这里将其完整写出会更容易理解。回复12：是的，同意。现在已经更正。评论13：表格1-4。表格中文章的呈现顺序不明确。请使用字母顺序或其他类似顺序。回复13：感谢您的提醒。我们现在已经更新了所有表格，并使用字母顺序排列研究。评论14：表格1。B、U、L和R需要解释。从感知角度来看，一个十进制数对于响度评估是足够的。回复14：我们现在已经对上述缩写进行了详细解释。目前耳鸣的响度以dBSL表示。然而，有两项研究使用了视觉模拟量表（VAS），因此我们在表格中做了相应标注。评论15：表格2。从感知角度来看，PTA结果一个十进制数就足够了。我假设这里的PTA指的是纯音听力图，而不是纯音平均值。HFAHL需要定义（从哪些频率计算得出？）。应该是“斜坡”听力损失，而不是“sloping”？回复15：感谢您的指出。我们现在已经更正了表格中的sloping拼写。表格2中的PTA代表纯音听力测试结果。我们在脚注中对此进行了详细说明。PTA的平均值以dBHL（分贝听力级）表示，通常是三个频率（500Hz、1kHz和kHz）的平均值。然而，有一项研究（Stevens等人，2007年）提供了HFAHL。我们在脚注中详细说明了计算这一平均值所包含的频率。希望现在信息已经清晰。

paper_title: Technological innovation for workload allocation in nursing care management: an integrative review
paper_abstract:
Background 
     Technology reduces the nursing workload, improve the quality care processes, patient’s safety, and avoid staff burnout. Innovative technologies are disrupting healthcare systems by improving the efficiency of processes and management. There is a discussion on the benefits, challenges, and barriers of these technologies and considering human factors of nursing management. The aim was to analyze the influence of technologies on the distribution of workload for nursing care management. 
   
   
     Methods 
     An integrative literature review was performed. Four databases were searched: Scopus, Scielo, PUBMED, and CINALH following PRISMA guidelines. Articles published from January 2016 to December 2020, published in English, Spanish and Portuguese were included. Studies were excluded when they were not original research, did not met the quality criteria or they did not answer the research questions. Quality appraisal was performed using the Crowe Critical Appraisal Tool version 1.4 (CCAT). Two reviewers independently examined the title and abstract for eligibility according to the inclusion and exclusion criteria. 
   
   
     Results 
     2818 potentially relevant articles were found, but once the inclusion and exclusion criteria in the abstracts were analyzed, 177 remained for evaluation. After following the PRISMA Guidelines, 35 studies were included in the review. Three categories were identified: Nursing workload; Information technologies and technological means for management; Technology acceptance. 
   
   
     Conclusions 
     Technology has the potential to improve care management by estimating nurse workload in ICUs and non-critical units, but scientific evidence is more detailed in the former type of services. The literature provides insights about the factors that factors and the barriers that promote the technology acceptance and usability. We did not find studies comparing technologies and no scientific evidence proving improvements in care.
review_content:
Dear authors, thank you very much for the opportunity to review this manuscript. This systematic review addresses an interesting topic on nurses' workloads. Since this is a systematic review study, the following comments are based on the PRISMA guidelines.

As general comments, a quality criterion for a systematic review is the registration of the review protocol (for example in PROSPERO). The registration number should be provided in the method and (according to PRISMA also in the abstract).

Abstract: is structured and informative.In the methods section it is possible to improve the information on the following aspects: Specify the inclusion and exclusion criteria. "Cinahl" is badly written. In the summary you duplicate the explanation of the Critical Appraisal Tool version 1.4 (CCAT) acronym. The acronyms ICUs and PRISMA are not explained.

Keywords: For proper indexing of the article once it is published, it is appropriate to use keyword descriptor terms (MesH). "Nursing Care Management" is not a MesH. ("Nursing Care" is a MesH; there are several terms that include Management that can also be used. Regarding the two terms "Personnel Staffing", "Scheduling Information Systems": there is a single descriptor that can include both "Personnel Staffing and Scheduling Information Systems".

Introduction: The introduction is very sparse; content on Technological innovation and nurses workload could be included.

Methods: It is not understood that you have established among the inclusion criteria searches until the year 2020. Three years have passed since the date of the searches and in that period new studies of interest could have been published. It is a quality criterion to update the searches when at least one year has passed since they were performed if the manuscript has not been published in that period.

Results: The results should be limited to the extraction of data from the studies without interpretation to be made in the discussion. The quality criteria of the studies should be explained in detail in the methods section. When looking at the results in Table 1, it is not possible to interpret the criterion in the last column: Excellent, some limitations...
Characteristics of the studies: in the description of the number of studies included, you must unify criteria to express them in numbers or in letters (example: four vs. 4).
The acronym ICUs is explained in results (heading: Predictors of nursing burnout and outcomes; last paragraph of this section), but the acronym has been used previously in the same paragraph. Idem EMRs acronym.

Discussion: The discussion is poor, only citing 5 studies. As I have pointed out in the previous comment, you must transfer content from the results to the discussion. The discussion should follow the structure established in the results.
paper_title_zh: 护理管理中工作量分配的技术创新：综合性回顾
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
技术可以减轻护理工作负担，提高护理质量流程，确保患者安全，并避免员工倦怠。创新技术通过提高流程和管理的效率，正在颠覆医疗保健系统。目前存在关于这些技术的益处、挑战和障碍的讨论，并考虑护理管理中的人为因素。本研究旨在分析技术对护理管理工作负担分配的影响。

方法
进行了一项综合性文献综述。检索了四个数据库：Scopus、Scielo、PUBMED和CINALH，遵循PRISMA指南。纳入了2016年1月至2020年12月期间以英语、西班牙语和葡萄牙语发表的文章。排除了非原创研究、不符合质量标准或未回答研究问题的研究。使用Crowe关键评估工具1.4版（CCAT）进行质量评估。两名评审员根据纳入和排除标准独立检查标题和摘要的资格。

结果
共发现2818篇潜在相关文章，但在分析了摘要中的纳入和排除标准后，仍有177篇待评估。遵循PRISMA指南后，共有35项研究纳入综述。确定了三个类别：护理工作负担；信息技术和管理技术手段；技术接受度。

结论
技术有潜力通过估算ICU和非重症单元的护士工作负担来改善护理管理，但科学证据在前一类服务中更为详细。文献提供了关于促进技术接受和使用因素及障碍的见解。我们未找到比较技术的相关研究，也没有科学证据证明护理质量的改善。

作为总体评论，系统综述的质量标准之一是综述方案的注册（例如在PROSPERO）。注册号应在方法部分提供，并且（根据PRISMA指南也应在摘要中提供）。

paper_title: Does evidence support the high expectations placed in precision medicine? A bibliographic review
paper_abstract:
Background : Precision medicine is the Holy Grail of interventions that are tailored to a patient’s individual characteristics. However, conventional clinical trials are designed to find differences in averages, and interpreting these differences depends on untestable assumptions. Although only an ideal, a constant effect of treatment would facilitate individual management. A direct consequence of a constant effect is that the variance of the outcome measure would be the same in the treated and control arms. We reviewed the literature to explore the similarity of these variances as a foundation for examining whether and how often precision medicine is definitively required. 
 Methods : We reviewed parallel clinical trials with numerical primary endpoints published in 2004, 2007, 2010 and 2013. We collected the baseline and final standard deviations of the main outcome measure. We assessed homoscedasticity by comparing the variance of the primary endpoint between arms through the outcome variance ratio (treated to control group). 
 Results : The review provided 208 articles with enough information to conduct the analysis. One out of five studies (n = 40, 19.2%) had statistically different variances between groups, implying a non-constant-effect. The adjusted point estimate of the mean outcome variance ratio (treated to control group) is 0.89 (95% CI 0.81 to 0.97). 
 Conclusions : The mean variance ratio is significantly lower than 1 and the lower variance was found more often in the intervention group than in the control group, suggesting it is more usual for treated patients to be stable. This observed reduction in variance might also imply that there could be a subgroup of less ill patients who derive no benefit from treatment. This would require further study as to whether the treatment effect outweighs the side effects as well as the economic costs. We have shown that there are ways to analyze the apparently unobservable constant effect.
review_content:
We enjoyed reading the paper by Cortes and colleagues as it very usefully surveys the literature for evidence that personalised effects exist, and finds little. This well-conceived study has also been well-executed but does not currently meet the same quality of reporting.

The authors also need to be careful not to overstate their case: they find the absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. Whilst, on the whole, they express this correctly, in a few places, a previous reviewer correctly challenges them on this.

Regarding the verb 'need', the first reviewer is right - it is too much to say 'If the effect randomly varies ... we need to characterize its distribution'. The authors themselves clarify, later in their reply to this reviewer, that what they mean is 'the best clinicians would like to know ...'. 'need' is a much stronger word than 'would like'. The Oxford English Dictionary defines it in terms of 'necessary', which in turn is defined as 'Indispensable, vital, essential, requisite'.

Prof White is also correct to challenge the remark on page 9 that 'the simplest interpretation ... thus rendering futile any search ...'

The problem here is that the current wording suggests futility follows from equal variances. We feel it needs some form of wording that makes it clear that the 'futile' is conditional on 'the simplest interpretation' being true and suggest '... treatment effect is constant, which, if correct, would render futile any ...'

Additional areas for clarification include:

Abstract conclusion - where the authors state ‘…outcome variance was more often smaller…’, we find the results in both the Abstract and main Results section do not fully support this conclusion. Table 1 indicates that the most common outcome by far is 'variability not changed'. The authors should re-write the Abstract in such a way that the results directly support the conclusions.

Methods - regarding the target population, it could be made more clear that 'quantitative outcomes' refers to outcomes with continuous data.

Results - the results section cites figures in the Supplementary material but the Table (Table 1) and Figure (Figure 3) included in the main paper are not discussed. It is hard to map results in the Abstract to the corresponding points in the main Results and hard to map conclusions directly to results, especially within the Abstract.

Figure 2 - the percentages in brackets are confusing. Reporting according to current reporting standards is recommended.

Discussion: on page 9 [PDF] where the authors state ‘…thus in turn also supporting evidence-based medicine’ and later on page 10 'Here, we have provided empirical insights for the rationale behind Evidence-Based Medicine.'
Both statements equate the entire philosophy and practice of evidence-based medicine/practice with 'let's use parallel group trials'. This paper deals with one element of EBM/P - that of treatment decisions and a further distillation still down to the use of parallel controlled trials to guide decision making in these circumstances. The authors should re-word these occurrences accordingly.
paper_title_zh: 精准医学的高期望是否有证据支持？文献综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：精准医学是针对患者个体特征量身定制的干预措施的“圣杯”。然而，传统的临床试验设计旨在发现平均差异，而这些差异的解释依赖于不可检验的假设。尽管只是一个理想状态，但治疗效果的恒定将有助于个体化管理。恒定效果的直接后果是，治疗组和对照组的结局测量方差相同。我们回顾了文献，探讨这些方差的相似性，作为检验精准医学是否以及多常被明确需要的基石。

方法：我们回顾了2004年、2007年、2010年和2013年发表的具有数值主要终点的平行临床试验。我们收集了主要结局指标的基线和最终标准差。通过比较治疗组与对照组主要终点之间的方差（结局方差比）来评估同方差性。

结果：回顾提供了208篇含有足够信息进行数据分析的文章。五分之一的研究（n = 40，19.2%）在组间具有统计学上不同的方差，意味着非恒定效果。调整后的平均结局方差比（治疗组与对照组）的点估计为0.89（95% CI 0.81至0.97）。

结论：平均方差比显著低于1，且干预组比对照组更常出现较低方差，这表明治疗患者的稳定性更为常见。观察到的方差减少也可能意味着存在一个病情较轻的患者亚组，他们从治疗中未获得益处。这需要进一步研究，以确定治疗效果是否超过副作用以及经济成本。我们已经证明，有方法可以分析看似不可观察的恒定效果。
review_content_zh:
我们很高兴阅读了Cortes及其同事的论文，因为它非常有用地综述了关于个性化效应存在的文献证据，并发现这类证据很少。这项构思巧妙的研究也得到了很好的执行，但目前尚未达到相同的报告质量。

作者还需要谨慎，不要夸大其词：他们发现的是证据的缺失，而不是缺失的证据。尽管总体上他们表达得正确，但在少数地方，前一位审稿人正确地对此提出了质疑。

关于动词“need”，第一位审稿人是正确的——说“如果效应随机变化……我们需要表征其分布”太过分了。作者在后来对该审稿人的回复中澄清，他们的意思是“最好的临床医生会想知道……”。“need”比“would like”要强烈得多。牛津英语词典将其定义为“必要的”，而“必要的”又被定义为“不可或缺的、至关重要的、基本的、必需的”。

White教授也正确地质疑了第9页上的评论“最简单的解释……从而使任何搜索……变得徒劳”。

这里的问题在于，当前的措辞暗示徒劳是平等方差的必然结果。我们认为需要某种形式的措辞，以明确“徒劳”是取决于“最简单的解释”为真的条件，并建议改为“……治疗效应是恒定的，如果正确，将使任何……变得徒劳”。

需要澄清的其他领域包括：

摘要结论——作者在摘要中提到“……结果方差往往更小……”，我们发现摘要和主要结果部分的结果并不完全支持这一结论。表1显示最常见的结果是“变异性未改变”。作者应重写摘要，使其结果直接支持结论。

方法——关于目标人群，可以更清楚地说明“定量结果”是指具有连续数据的结果。

结果——结果部分引用了补充材料中的图表，但未讨论主论文中的表（表1）和图（图3）。很难将摘要中的结果与主要结果部分对应的点对应起来，也很难将结论直接与结果对应，尤其是在摘要中。

图2——括号中的百分比令人困惑。建议根据当前的报告标准进行报告。

讨论：在第9页[PDF]中，作者提到“……从而反过来也支持了循证医学的证据”，并在第10页后文提到“在这里，我们为循证医学背后的理论基础提供了实证见解。”
这两句话将整个循证医学/实践的哲学和实践等同于“让我们使用平行组试验”。本文涉及EBM/P的一个要素——治疗决策，并进一步提炼到在这些情况下使用平行对照试验来指导决策。作者应相应地重新措辞这些表述。

paper_title: A Survey on Transformers in Reinforcement Learning
paper_abstract: Transformer has been considered the dominating neural architecture in NLP and CV, mostly under supervised settings. Recently, a similar surge of using Transformers has appeared in the domain of reinforcement learning (RL), but it is faced with unique design choices and challenges brought by the nature of RL. However, the evolution of Transformers in RL has not yet been well unraveled. In this paper, we seek to systematically review motivations and progress on using Transformers in RL, provide a taxonomy on existing works, discuss each sub-field, and summarize future prospects.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
Transformers have emerged as a general and powerful model for learning from high-dimensional, rich, and sequential data that has seen success across variety of domains of ML, including NLP and Computer Vision. This paper surveys the use of Transformers in Reinforcement Learning, categorizing uses of transformers into the following: 1. as one component of a more traditional RL agent system, e.g. as an observation encoder, especially when processing rich visual or hierarchical/abstract data; as a memory module that processes past states (as an alternative to other memory mechanisms such as RNNs); or as a world model; 2. as an "end-to-end" sequential decision maker, by treating RL as a sequence modeling problem, in the line of decision transformer and other approaches to hindsight RL; 3. as very large, generalist models that can solve many tasks and domains, especially when combined with pretrained models such as large language models Within these three taxonomies, the authors survey a fairly comprehensive set of recent work, including core ideas (e.g. RL as sequence modeling, generalist models), as well as additional work attempting to build and generalize such ideas. They conclude with several promising directions for future research.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
# Strengths - This area is clearly of interest to many in the TMLR audience, as transformers are increasingly the go-to modeling architecture of choice across a variety of ML domains, including RL. This paper should serve as a reasonably recent and comprehensive reference for practitioners - I largely agree with the authors' taxonomy of uses of various Transformer architectures, though I disagree with the framing (see Weaknesses) - Good survey of future directions and outstanding challenges in the field. # Weaknesses ## Framing I feel conflicted about the paper—on the one hand, Transformers have upended RL (and every other ML subfield) and so it's obviously important for people to understand how they're used in RL, and towards that end this paper does a good job at surveying the recent work and latest advancements (it may have missed a few papers, since it's hard to catch every paper that gets released in this field, but it feels reasonably comprehensive). In providing a reasonably comprehensive overview of the recent literature, this paper does a good job. On the other hand, I find the framing of the paper a bit reductive, as it simplifies and combines several distinct research advances and thrusts under the generic umbrella of "use Transformers for RL". Specifically, the authors identify three "pillars" of recent advances in RL: 1. Using Transformers to model high-dimensional, abstract sequential and/or graph-structured data as components in more "traditional" RL systems. 2. The view of reinforcement learning as sequential decision making + the hindsight information matching framework. Note that this advance is *not* inherent to Transformers, though obviously the first work pushing this view indeed used a Transformer as its modeling architecture of choice. 3. The gradual trend towards large-scale, generalist, pretrained ("foundation") models that learn to transfer and share parameters across a variety of tasks for improved performance, and the use of already successful pretrained models (such as large language models) as backbones for RL systems. Note that this advance is *also* not specific to Transformer models, though obviously the overwhelming majority of currently successful foundation models are Transformer-based. Note that of these three thrusts, all 3 involve transformers to some degree, but arguably only one of these (the first pillar) is actually specific to the Transformer architecture. The other I do believe should be included in a Transformers for RL review paper, **however** I find the paper takes a bit of a reductive framing by describing everything as Transformer-first. For example, section 4.3 is described as "using Transformers for sequential decision making", and is framed primarily as "let's use Transformers to solve a SDM problem." OTOH I believe the framing should be something like: "A recent advance in RL has been viewing RL as sequence modeling...Transformers are a particularly useful architecture for this approach because they are particularly good sequence models." Similarly, I feel like Section 4.4 is less about "Transformers for generalist agents" and more about "Transformers as (one choice) of a model architecture, towards the general trend of large-scale pretrained models and transfer learning for RL." This framing can be seen in the authors' term "TransformRL". I disagree with the authors' decision to define a new name, TransformRL, to refer to the use of Transformers in RL, given the discussion on reductiveness above, and especially given how many overloaded and confusing terms the fields of RL/ML/DL have already. In my opinion the term conflates the field (RL) with current tools that we find useful to use in the field (Transformers) and the recent central advances dominating the RL conversation, of which Transformers play varying degrees of importance (RL as sequence modeling, large-scale pretraining). It's possible Transformer hype will die down, yet these other ideas will persist, and I don't think that RL should currently be defined by the use of Transformers. Imagine, for example, if we had analogous terms like RNNNLP or CNNCV—I view them all as rather unnecessary. I think to improve the framing under my view, the paper could use a more nuanced discussion at the beginning, by saying that transformers are now a workhorse in RL because they are such expressive and capable models, but they are used for very (different) reasons stemming from orthogonal advances in RL, including (1) RL in high-dimensional spaces, (2) RL as a sequence modeling problem, and (3) the trend towards large-scale, pretrained foundation models. ## Could better summarize advantages and disadvantages *specific to Transformers* in RL I find the paper could be more detailed and nuanced when describing the reasons why one might specifically use Transformers over other models in RL, and what features of problems make Transformers a particularly good choice. Most of the sections of the paper basically show that Transformers have seen success when slotting them into basically every possible part of the RL problem: when processing observations (section 4.1.1), memory (section 4.1.2), world models (section 4.1.3). The authors catalog dozens upon dozens of apparent success stories where Transformers successfully replace existing deep architectures for RL. What should the takeaway be for the readers reading this paper? Is it that one should now use Transformers basically unilaterally, in every possible component of an RL model? The paper could emphasize *particular problems* of an RL task that make Transformers a particularly suitable solution. For example, in Section 4.1, it seems like Transformers have seen success in processing "complex information", including multi-agent representations (zambaldi et al 2018), morphological domain knowledge (kurin 2020), "sensory sequences" (tang and ha), multimodal information (team 2021), and a variety of vision settings. What is the overall recommendation or understanding from the authors, after surveying this work? Is it that one should no longer use any other more domain specific architectures such as CNNs and RNNs? Does it seem like Transformers be the go-to architecture for representation learning in RL? Are there any commonalities among domains where Transformers consistently outperform or underperform, or is more empirical work needed? I imagine that this work shows that Transformers have the most success in RL when applied the same kinds of representation learning problems as the supervised learning problems that Transformers are so good at. Assuming this is the case, the authors could more clearly illustrate this by unifying the case studies in this section, and tying it back to the general advantages of transformers as mentioned e.g. in 3rd paragraph of the intro (long dependencies, scalability). Similarly, why should one use a Transformer instead of a more traditional memory mechanism such as an RNN/LSTM in RL agents (section 4.1.2)? Should it only be for environments with extremely long-distance dependencies? How should one think about the tradeoffs of (1) increased sequence modeling capacity and (2) larger model capacity? There is some description of the relevant tradeoffs in the final paragraph, but the writing could try to better aggregate and summarize the trends in each subarea here. --- The paper also lacks nuance in describing the current outstanding challenges in using Transformers in RL. For example, end of page 1/beginning of page 2, and Section 3.2 describes "unique challenges" for Transformers in RL: 1. Sensitivity to architecture selection 2. Sensitivity to design choices (e.g. hyperparameters) 3. Large memory footprints and high latency In my view, only (3) is a challenge that is arguably somewhat unique to Transformers, especially the large-scale transformers that have seen success across vision, NLP, and RL tasks. (1) and (2) seem like general issues across the entire field of RL. ## Minor - I don't think "foundation model" is used correctly e.g. bottom of page 1, first sentence of section 4—I don't think a particular architecture can be categorized as a "foundation model" since you can still have small domain-specific transformers. Whether something is a "foundation model" is primarily determined by the model capabilities and usage intent rather than the particular architecture - I don't think Transformers are strictly sequence models, since sequence implies linear order and one can apply transformers to various richly ordered or unordered representation learning problems. However section 4.1 seems to cast Transformers as such. For example it's not clear to me that all of the uses of Transformers in section 4.1.1 are **sequence encoding** problems—e.g. the multi-entity StarCraft modeling problem is not necessarily a sequence modeling problem but rather a set representation learning problem. - End of section 4.2 "The Transformer-based world model can help alleviate the prediction error on longer sequences." Can authors elaborate? Is this an empirical finding from the Janner paper or just a general statement about improved sequence modeling capacity from transformers? - I think in every review paper it's difficult to avoid the "laundry list paragraph of several different papers" trope, but minimizing this to whatever extent possible is ideal. Section 4.3.3 sticks out as a particular "laundry list" paragraph that outlines a dozen or so advance sin Transformer architectures without really unifying or describing the main shortcomings people are trying to work around, and the main trends in this research. There are also a lot of terms that are not fully explained and digestible to the average reader (e.g. CVAE, "drop-span embedding", etc) ## Overall I don't think any of the weaknesses I described above are blockers to publication, and co-reviewers may not see as much issue with the framing as I do, and I am happy to be overriden. However in my opinion there is some additional work that would elevate this paper beyond the typical review paper in providing a more nuanced and unified view of the various new advances that have defined modern (2020+) RL research, and how precisely the Transformer architecture plays a role in all of this.

**Requested Changes:**
As I described above, I would be happy to be overriden if my co-reviewers believe the paper is fine as is, but I think to be an excellent review paper, the paper could (1) slightly change the wording to be more clear about the different roles that Transformers play across different recent advances in RL, and (2) more clearly explain the advantages and shortcomings of the Transformer architecture specifically (rather than listing challenges specific to RL as a whole), and how recent work (e.g. section 4.3.3) is trying to get around such limitations.

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes
paper_title_zh: 《强化学习中Transformer的调查》
paper_abstract_zh: Transformer已被视为自然语言处理（NLP）和计算机视觉（CV）领域的主导神经架构，主要在监督学习环境下。最近，在强化学习（RL）领域也出现了类似的Transformer应用热潮，但面临着由RL本质带来的独特设计选择和挑战。然而，Transformer在RL中的演变尚未得到充分揭示。在本文中，我们旨在系统地回顾在RL中使用Transformer的动机和进展，对现有工作进行分类，讨论每个子领域，并总结未来的前景。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
Transformer已成为一种通用且强大的模型，用于学习高维、丰富且有序的数据，并在包括自然语言处理和计算机视觉在内的多个机器学习领域取得了成功。本文综述了Transformer在强化学习中的应用，将其用途分为以下几类：1. 作为更传统RL智能体系统的一个组件，例如作为观测编码器，尤其是在处理丰富的视觉或层次/抽象数据时；作为处理过去状态的记忆模块（作为RNN等其他记忆机制的替代方案）；或作为世界模型；2. 作为“端到端”的序列决策者，通过将RL视为序列建模问题，沿决策Transformer和其他后见RL方法的思路；3. 作为非常大型的通用模型，能够解决许多任务和领域，尤其是与预训练模型（如大型语言模型）结合时。在这三种分类中，作者综述了相当全面的近期工作，包括核心思想（如RL作为序列建模、通用模型），以及试图构建和推广这些思想的额外工作。他们最后提出了几个未来研究的潜在方向。

**优点和缺点：**
# 优点 - 这一领域显然对TMLR的许多读者感兴趣，因为Transformer越来越多地成为各种ML领域（包括RL）的首选建模架构。本文应作为从业者近期且全面的参考 - 我基本同意作者对各种Transformer架构用途的分类，尽管我不同意其框架（见缺点） - 对该领域的未来方向和未解挑战进行了良好的综述。 # 缺点 ## 框架 我对这篇论文感到矛盾——一方面，Transformer颠覆了RL（以及所有其他ML子领域），因此显然重要的是让人们了解它们在RL中的使用，在这方面，本文在综述近期工作和最新进展方面做得很好（可能遗漏了几篇论文，因为很难捕捉到该领域发布的每一篇论文，但感觉相当全面）。在提供近期文献的全面概述方面，本文做得不错。另一方面，我发现论文的框架有些简化，因为它将几个不同的研究进展和推动力简化并合并到“使用Transformer进行RL”的通用伞下。具体来说，作者确定了RL近期进展的三个“支柱”：1. 使用Transformer作为组件在更“传统”的RL系统中建模高维、抽象的序列和/或图结构数据。2. 将强化学习视为序列决策+后见信息匹配框架。 请注意，这一进步并非Transformer模型所固有，尽管显然最初推动这一观点的工作确实选择了Transformer作为其建模架构。3. 逐渐向大规模、通用、预训练（“基础”）模型发展的趋势，这些模型学会在各种任务之间转移和共享参数以提高性能，以及使用已经成功的预训练模型（如大型语言模型）作为RL系统的骨干。请注意，这一进步也并非特定于Transformer模型，尽管显然目前绝大多数成功的基础模型都是基于Transformer的。请注意，在这三个主要方向中，所有三个都不同程度地涉及Transformer，但可以说只有其中一个（第一支柱）实际上是特定于Transformer架构的。其他两个我认为应该包含在关于Transformer在RL中应用的综述论文中，**然而**我发现该论文通过将一切都描述为以Transformer为先的框架，显得有些简化。例如，第4.3节被描述为“使用Transformer进行序列决策”，并且主要框架为“让我们使用Transformer来解决SDM问题”。另一方面，我认为框架应该是这样的：“RL的一个近期进展是将RL视为序列建模……Transformer是这一方法中特别有用的架构，因为它们是非常优秀的序列模型。”同样，我觉得第4.4节更少关注“Transformer用于通用智能体”，而更多关注“Transformer作为（一个选择）模型架构，朝着大规模预训练模型和RL中的迁移学习这一普遍趋势发展。”这种框架可以在作者的“TransformRL”一词中看到。鉴于上述关于简化性的讨论，尤其是考虑到RL/ML/DL领域已经有许多过载和令人困惑的术语，我不同意作者决定定义一个新名称TransformRL来指代Transformer在RL中的使用。在我看来，这一术语将领域（RL）与我们在该领域中发现的当前有用工具（Transformer）以及近期主导RL讨论的中心进展（如RL作为序列建模、大规模预训练）混淆在一起。Transformer的热潮可能会消退，但这些其他理念将持续存在，我认为RL目前不应由Transformer的使用来定义。例如，想象一下，如果我们有类似RNNNLP或CNNCV这样的类比术语——我认为它们都是不必要的。 我认为，从我的观点来看，要改进文章的框架，可以在开头进行更细致的讨论，指出变压器（Transformers）如今在强化学习（RL）中成为主力军，因为它们是表达能力强且功能强大的模型，但它们的使用出于非常不同的原因，这些原因源自RL中正交的进展，包括（1）高维空间中的RL，（2）将RL视为序列建模问题，以及（3）向大规模、预训练基础模型的趋势。## 可以更好地总结在RL中特定于Transformers的优缺点

我发现，文章在描述为何在RL中特别选择使用Transformers而非其他模型，以及哪些问题特征使Transformers成为特别好的选择时，可以更加详细和细致。文章的大部分章节基本上展示了Transformers在RL问题的几乎每个可能部分中都取得了成功：在处理观测（第4.1.1节）、记忆（第4.1.2节）、世界模型（第4.1.3节）时。作者列举了数十个明显的成功案例，其中Transformers成功取代了现有的深度架构用于RL。读者阅读这篇文章应得出的结论是什么？是否应该现在基本上单方面地在RL模型的每个可能组件中使用Transformers？文章可以强调使Transformers成为特别合适解决方案的RL任务的特定问题。

例如，在第4.1节中，Transformers在处理“复杂信息”方面似乎取得了成功，包括多智能体表示（Zambaldi等，2018）、形态学领域知识（Kurin，2020）、“感官序列”（Tang和Ha）、多模态信息（Team，2021）以及各种视觉设置。在综述了这些工作后，作者的整体建议或理解是什么？是否应该不再使用任何其他更领域特定的架构，如CNNs和RNNs？Transformers是否将成为RL中表示学习的首选架构？在Transformers始终表现优异或表现不佳的领域是否存在共性，还是需要更多的实证研究？

我想，这项工作表明，当Transformers应用于与它们在监督学习中表现如此出色的相同类型的表示学习问题时，在RL中最成功。假设情况确实如此，作者可以通过统一本节中的案例研究，并将其与引言第三段中提到的Transformers的一般优势（如长依赖关系、可扩展性）联系起来，更清晰地说明这一点。同样，为什么在RL代理中应使用Transformer而不是更传统的记忆机制，如RNN/LSTM（第4.1.2节）？是否仅适用于具有极长距离依赖的环境？ 如何思考（1）增加序列建模能力和（2）扩大模型容量之间的权衡？在最后一段中有一些相关权衡的描述，但写作可以尝试更好地汇总和总结每个子领域的趋势。--- 论文在描述当前使用Transformer在RL中的突出挑战时也缺乏细腻度。例如，第1页末尾/第2页开头，以及第3.2节描述了Transformer在RL中的“独特挑战”：1. 对架构选择的敏感性 2. 对设计选择的敏感性（例如超参数）3. 大内存占用和高延迟在我看来，只有（3）可以说是Transformer特有的挑战，尤其是那些在视觉、NLP和RL任务中取得成功的 大规模Transformer。（1）和（2）似乎是整个RL领域的普遍问题。## 小问题 - 我认为“基础模型”的使用不正确，例如第1页底部，第4节的第一句——我认为特定的架构不能被归类为“基础模型”，因为你仍然可以有小的特定领域的Transformer。是否为“基础模型”主要取决于模型能力和使用意图，而不是特定的架构。- 我认为Transformer并不严格是序列模型，因为序列暗示了线性顺序，而可以将Transformer应用于各种丰富有序或无序的表示学习问题。然而第4.1节似乎将其视为序列模型。例如，我不清楚第4.1.1节中所有Transformer的使用是否都是**序列编码**问题——例如，多实体StarCraft建模问题不一定是序列建模问题，而是集合表示学习问题。- 第4.2节末尾“基于Transformer的世界模型可以帮助减轻对更长序列的预测误差。”作者能否详细说明？这是Janner论文的实证发现还是关于Transformer改进序列建模能力的普遍说法？- 我认为在每篇综述论文中都难以避免“列举若干不同论文的段落”的套路，但尽可能减少这种写法是理想的。第4.3.3节特别突出，作为一个“列举”段落，概述了十几种Transformer架构的进展，却没有真正统一或描述人们试图克服的主要缺点，以及这一研究的主要趋势。还有一些术语没有完全解释，普通读者难以理解（例如CVAE、“drop-span embedding”等）## 总体而言，我认为上述任何弱点都不构成发表的障碍，共同评审者可能不会像我这样看待框架问题，我乐意被推翻。 然而，在我看来，还有一些额外的工作可以使这篇论文超越典型的综述论文，提供一个更为细腻和统一的视角，来审视那些定义了现代（2020+）强化学习研究的各种新进展，以及Transformer架构在其中究竟扮演了怎样的角色。

**请求的修改：**
如上所述，如果我的共同审稿人认为论文现状良好，我愿意被否决，但我认为要成为一篇优秀的综述论文，该论文可以（1）略微调整措辞，以更清晰地阐述Transformer在不同近期RL进展中所扮演的不同角色，并且（2）更清楚地解释Transformer架构的具体优势和不足（而不是列出针对RL整体的具体挑战），以及近期工作（例如第4.3.3节）是如何试图克服这些局限的。

**声明和证据：**
是

**受众：**
是

reasons: Within these three taxonomies, the authors survey a fairly comprehensive set of recent work, including core ideas (e.g. RL as sequence modeling, generalist models), as well as additional work attempting to build and generalize such ideas.

On the other hand, I find the framing of the paper a bit reductive, as it simplifies and combines several distinct research advances and thrusts under the generic umbrella of "use Transformers for RL".

I disagree with the authors' decision to define a new name, TransformRL, to refer to the use of Transformers in RL, given the discussion on reductiveness above, and especially given how many overloaded and confusing terms the fields of RL/ML/DL have already.

I find the paper could be more detailed and nuanced when describing the reasons why one might specifically use Transformers over other models in RL, and what features of problems make Transformers a particularly good choice.
The paper also lacks nuance in describing the current outstanding challenges in using Transformers in RL.
Overall I don't think any of the weaknesses I described above are blockers to publication,

However in my opinion there is some additional work that would elevate this paper beyond the typical review paper in providing a more nuanced and unified view of the various new advances that have defined modern (2020+) RL research, and how precisely the Transformer architecture plays a role in all of this.
There are also a lot of terms that are not fully explained and digestible to the average reader (e.g. CVAE, "drop-span embedding", etc)
Can authors elaborate?
Is this an empirical finding from the Janner paper or just a general statement about improved sequence modeling capacity from transformers?
I think in every review paper it's difficult to avoid the "laundry list paragraph of several different papers" trope, but minimizing this to whatever extent possible is ideal.

I don't think "foundation model" is used correctly e.g. bottom of page 1, first sentence of section 4—I don't think a particular architecture can be categorized as a "foundation model" since you can still have small domain-specific transformers.

On the other hand, I find the framing of the paper a bit reductive, as it simplifies and combines several distinct research advances and thrusts under the generic umbrella of "use Transformers for RL".

Similarly, I feel like Section 4.4 is less about "Transformers for generalist agents" and more about "Transformers as (one choice) of a model architecture, towards the general trend of large-scale pretrained models and transfer learning for RL."

Section 4.3.3 sticks out as a particular "laundry list" paragraph that outlines a dozen or so advance sin Transformer architectures without really unifying or describing the main shortcomings people are trying to work around, and the main trends in this research.

paper_title: (Semi)automated approaches to data extraction for systematic reviews and meta-analyses in social sciences: A living review protocol
paper_abstract:
Background : An abundance of rapidly accumulating scientific evidence presents novel opportunities for researchers and practitioners alike, yet such advantages are often overshadowed by resource demands associated with finding and aggregating a continually expanding body of scientific information. Across social science disciplines, the use of automation technologies for timely and accurate knowledge synthesis can enhance research translation value, better inform key policy development, and expand the current understanding of human interactions, organizations, and systems. Ongoing developments surrounding automation are highly concentrated in research for evidence-based medicine with limited evidence surrounding tools and techniques applied outside of the clinical research community. Our objective is to conduct a living systematic review of automated data extraction techniques supporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses in the social sciences. The aim of this study is to extend the automation knowledge base by synthesizing current trends in the application of extraction technologies of key data elements of interest for social scientists. 
 Methods : The proposed study is a living systematic review employing a partial replication framework based on extant literature surrounding automation of data extraction for systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Protocol development, base review, and updates follow PRISMA standards for reporting systematic reviews. This protocol is preregistered in OSF: (Semi)Automated Approaches to Data Extraction for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses in Social Sciences: A Living Review Protocol on August 14, 2022. 
 Conclusions : Anticipated outcomes of this study include: (a) generate insights supporting advancement in transferring existing reliable methods to social science research; (b) provide a foundation for protocol development leading to enhancement of comparability and benchmarking standards across disciplines; and (c) uncover exigencies that spur continued value-adding innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration for the benefit of the collective systematic review community.
review_content:
1. Authors propose to review the available-and-growing literature, technologies, and practices pertaining to conducting systematic reviews and meta-analysis by automated or semi-automated means. This review will be continuously updated via the living systematic review (LSR).
 2. The importance of this work is evident - because meta-analyses are extremely popular, useful, and necessary in many research domains, any technologies that stand to improve the conduct and quality of meta-analyses are welcome.
 3. Automated methods could apply not only to the extraction of data, but also to literature searching itself (e.g., see the Elicit AI assistant at https://elicit.org/).
 4. Authors might dive deeper on what benchmark standards might be used (overall and within domains); maybe the comparison across the technologies reviewed are relative benchmarks across a variety of dimensions (e.g., errors of omission vs. commission across JARS elements, extent of human involvement, domain-specific effectiveness).
 5. From this birds-eye view, the LSR might make summary recommendations of things such as (a) the conditions under which some tools are more useful than others; (b) how specific tools might be improved or technologies advanced more generally; (c) best reporting practices for authors (and reporting errors to avoid); (d) how humans tend to be most helpful (e.g., automation might err on the side of inclusion, for the human to winnow down).
 6. Side notes:
      + p. 4 refers to 'social research' but I think this is 'social sciences research'
      + top of Fig 2 looks like a header, but it only refers to the content of Table 1 (in other words, the reader wouldn't want to think that 'Bayesian techniques' are 'recommended for inclusion in manuscripts regardless of design')
      + Instead of the word clouds in Figs 3 and 4, I'd suggest tabling the similarities and differences, or perhaps not including them at all (e.g., the comparison wouldn't be as helpful in domains that do not conduct clinical trials)
Good luck to the authors in pursuing this LSR; I think many scholars (including myself) will find it very useful.
paper_title_zh: 社会科学中系统综述和元分析的（半）自动化数据提取方法：一项动态综述协议
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：大量迅速积累的科学证据为研究人员和从业者提供了新的机遇，然而，这些优势往往被与寻找和整合不断扩展的科学信息体相关的资源需求所掩盖。在社会科学各学科中，使用自动化技术进行及时和准确的知识合成可以增强研究转化的价值，更好地为关键政策制定提供信息，并扩展当前对人际互动、组织和系统的理解。围绕自动化的持续发展主要集中在基于证据的医学研究上，而在临床研究社区之外应用的工具和技术证据有限。我们的目标是进行一项动态系统综述，评估支持社会科学系统综述和元分析的自动化数据提取技术。本研究的目的是通过综合当前提取技术应用于社会科学关键数据元素的趋势，扩展自动化知识库。

方法：拟议的研究是一项动态系统综述，采用基于现有文献的部分复制框架，这些文献涉及系统综述和元分析的数据提取自动化。协议开发、基础综述和更新遵循PRISMA系统综述报告标准。该协议于2022年8月14日在OSF预注册：（半）自动化数据提取方法用于社会科学系统综述和元分析：一项动态综述协议。

结论：本研究的预期成果包括：（a）生成支持将现有可靠方法转移到社会科学研究的见解；（b）为协议开发提供基础，从而增强跨学科的可比性和基准标准；（c）揭示推动持续增值创新和跨学科合作以造福整个系统综述社区的迫切需求。
review_content_zh:
1. 作者提议回顾有关通过自动化或半自动化手段进行系统综述和元分析的现有且不断增长的文献、技术和实践。该综述将通过动态系统综述（LSR）持续更新。
2. 这项工作的重要性显而易见——因为元分析在许多研究领域极为流行、有用且必要，任何有望提高元分析实施和质量的技术都是受欢迎的。
3. 自动化方法不仅适用于数据提取，也适用于文献检索本身（例如，参见Elicit AI助手：https://elicit.org/）。
4. 作者可能会深入探讨可能使用的基准标准（总体和各领域内）；或许所评述技术之间的比较是跨越多个维度的相对基准（例如，JARS要素中的遗漏错误与委托错误，人类参与程度，领域特定有效性）。
5. 从鸟瞰视角来看，LSR可能会总结推荐如下事项：（a）某些工具在何种条件下比其他工具更有用；（b）特定工具如何改进或技术如何普遍提升；（c）作者的最佳报告实践（及应避免的报告错误）；（d）人类最有助于的方面（例如，自动化可能倾向于包含过多，由人类进行筛选）。
6. 旁注：
   + 第4页提到的“社会研究”，我认为应为“社会科学研究”
   + 图2顶部看似标题，但仅指表1的内容（换言之，读者不应认为“贝叶斯技术”是“无论设计如何都推荐纳入手稿”）
   + 建议用表格列出图3和图4中词云的相似之处和差异，或者或许根本不包含它们（例如，在未进行临床试验的领域，这种比较不太有帮助）

祝作者在进行此LSR的过程中好运；我认为许多学者（包括我自己）会发现它非常有用。

paper_title: Targeting KRAS mutation in gastrointestinal cancers
paper_abstract: KRAS is the most commonly mutated gene in cancer and is associated with poor prognosis. Up to 44% of gastrointestinal cancers (GI) have KRAS mutations with the highest incidence observed in pancreatic cancer. Successfully targeting a specific mutation KRAS G12C in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has challenged the dogma that KRAS is a “non-druggable” target. With the advent of several RAS inhibitors, the opportunities for targeted therapy in GI cancers appears promising. This article provides in-depth review of KRAS mutations, and recently completed and ongoing clinical trials targeting KRAS mutations in GI cancers. In addition, this article reviews potential limitations for KRAS targeting in GI cancers.
review_content:
The authors provide a comprehensive review of current-day role for KRAS inhibition in gastrointestinal cancers, including an overview of novel inhibitors, both approved and in ongoing trials. They also shed light on resistance mechanisms as well as potential efforts to overcome resistance. Please see below comments:
1- Section "Prevalence and role of KRAS mutations", line 5, G13D instead of G12D (codon 13).
2- Section "Preclinical data with KRAS inhibitors", second paragraph, please spell out TILs and PBL and use the abbreviated form in later appearances.
3- Table 2. Please update the NCT# for KRYSTAL-10 (NCT04793958) and add clinical outcomes data from KRYSTAL-1 (NCT03785249) for PDAC and biliary cancer (https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.23.00434?url_ver=Z39.88-2003&rfr_id=ori:rid:crossref.org&rfr_dat=cr_pub%20%200pubmed). Also please add data in the body of the manuscript (second paragraph under section "Clinical data with KRAS inhibitors".
4- Section "Ongoing clinical trials", modify "KRYSTAL 1" to "KRYSTAL-1" (add dash).
5- Table 3. Please add this trial with RMC-9805 https://classic.clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT06040541
and this trial with BI 1701963 https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04111458?tab=table
paper_title_zh: 靶向胃肠道癌症中的KRAS突变
paper_abstract_zh: KRAS是癌症中最常见的突变基因，与预后不良相关。高达44%的胃肠道癌症（GI）存在KRAS突变，其中胰腺癌的发病率最高。成功靶向非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）中的特定突变KRAS G12C，挑战了KRAS是“不可成药”靶点的传统观念。随着多种RAS抑制剂的问世，胃肠道癌症的靶向治疗前景看好。本文深入综述了KRAS突变，以及最近完成和正在进行的针对胃肠道癌症中KRAS突变的临床试验。此外，本文还探讨了胃肠道癌症中KRAS靶向的潜在局限性。
review_content_zh:

以及这项使用BI 1701963的试验https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04111458?tab=table

paper_title: Approaches combining methods of operational research with Business Process Model and Notation -a systematic review
paper_abstract: Background: Business process modelling is increasingly used not only by the companies' management but also by scientists dealing with process models. Process modeling is seldom done without decisionmaking nodes, which is why operational research methods are increasingly included in the process analyses.
review_content: Reviewer 1 Basic reporting >> Related Work Section needs to be deeper developed. Is there any other kind of systematic review on this topic? Answer: We have expanded the section with additional research, basic literature and current publications. >> Why are the authors talking about SOA if it is not related to this paper? Answer: Thanks for the comment, the text no longer speaks of SOA. >> There is nothing to say about Operational Research? Answer: Thank you for your comment. We have expanded the text on Operations Research in the Introduction section as well as in the Related Works and Background section. >> It seems to me that figures 1, 4, and 5 can have greater legibility, optimizing the use of the space and increasing the size of the letters in texts. Answer: We redrew and modified the images to take full advantage of the space. >> I also suggest to include a legend on figures 4 and 5 explaining the numbers in parenthesis, although they are defined in the previous page. Is helps the readers when they are analyzing the image. Answer: We have modified the labels for graphs and tables. Experimental design >> Keyword Plus by WOS - I did not find any explanation in the text about it. What does “WOS” mean? (all acronyms should be explained). Besides, there is no reference to Keyword Plus. What is the difference to the keywords assigned by the authors method? Answer: Thanks for your feedback, we've added text on Keywords Plus with a link to the appropriate Clarivate Analytics site. Validity of the findings >> The previous “Limitations” section was removed at all. A section discussing the Threats to Validity is completing missing in the paper. Answer: We have significantly expanded the section on the methodology of the systematic review, we were inspired by the PRISMA checklist. The review should now be clearer. >> The Conclusion lacks a discussion on the opportunity for future work. Therefore, does not identify unresolved questions / gaps / future directions. Answer: We have expanded and updated the Conclusion section with new findings. We have added a Discussion section, where we have summarized the discovery of gaps and the expected future development. We have further expanded the text with two publications, which we consider pioneering for the founded gaps.
paper_title_zh: 结合运筹学方法与业务流程模型和符号表示法的途径——系统综述
paper_abstract_zh: 背景：业务流程建模不仅越来越多地被公司管理层使用，也被处理流程模型的科学家所采用。流程建模很少不涉及决策节点，因此运筹学方法越来越多地被纳入流程分析中。

paper_title: Is butyrate a natural alternative to dexamethasone in the management of CoVID-19?
paper_abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (CoVID-19) caused by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 has affected more than 100 million lives. Severe CoVID-19 infection may lead to acute respiratory distress syndrome and death of the patient, and is associated with hyperinflammation and cytokine storm. The broad spectrum immunosuppressant corticosteroid, dexamethasone, is being used to manage the cytokine storm and hyperinflammation in CoVID-19 patients. However, the extensive use of corticosteroids leads to serious adverse events and disruption of the gut-lung axis. Various micronutrients and probiotic supplementations are known to aid in the reduction of hyperinflammation and restoration of gut microbiota. The attenuation of the deleterious immune response and hyperinflammation could be mediated by short chain fatty acids produced by the gut microbiota. Butyric acid, the most extensively studied short chain fatty acid, is known for its anti-inflammatory properties. Additionally, butyric acid has been shown to ameliorate hyperinflammation and reduce oxidative stress in various pathologies, including respiratory viral infections. In this review, the potential anti-inflammatory effects of butyric acid that aid in cytokine storm depletion, and its usefulness in effective management of critical illness related to CoVID-19 have been discussed.
review_content:
The authors have written a comprehensive review on the role of butyrate as a natural alternative to dexamethasone in the management of COVID-19. Various micronutrients and probiotic supplementations are known to aid in the reduction of hyperinflammation and restoration of gut microbiota. The attenuation of the deleterious immune response and hyperinflammation could be mediated by short chain fatty acids (SCFA) produced by the gut microbiota. Butyric acid is well known for its anti-inflammatory properties and ability to reduce oxidative stress and hyperinflammation in many diseases. In this review, the potential anti-inflammatory effects of butyric acid that aid in cytokine storm depletion, and its usefulness in effective management of critical illness related to COVID-19 have been discussed.

While the review is well written it seems like the title does not fully reflect the content of the review. More than 50% of the review talks about gut microbiome and probiotics and nutrients that play a role in COVID-19 pathogenesis which is not reflected in the title. Only in the second half they talk about the role of butyrate. The title needs to be revised to fully reflect the article.

There are several new publications that discuss the role of butyrate in COVID-19 pathogenesis which could be added to make this a comprehensive review like J Li et al. (2021)1; Sarkar, P et al. (2020)2; Wang L et al. (2017)3.

COVID-19 pathogenesis is exacerbated in individuals who have co-morbidities. What is the role of butyrate in co-morbidities? This has not been discussed.

Innate immune cells play a major role in the COVID-19 pathogenesis. Although the role of butyrate is described in adaptive immune response, its role in innate immunity in the context of COVID-19 pathogenesis is minimally mentioned.

Some of the molecules like PGE2, ROS-IKK pathway has not been described in Figure 1 legend.
paper_title_zh: 丁酸是否为治疗COVID-19的天然替代品？
paper_abstract_zh: 2019冠状病毒病（CoVID-19）由严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2引起，已影响超过1亿人的生活。严重的CoVID-19感染可能导致急性呼吸窘迫综合征和患者死亡，并与超炎症和细胞因子风暴相关。广谱免疫抑制剂皮质类固醇，地塞米松，正在用于管理CoVID-19患者的细胞因子风暴和超炎症。然而，皮质类固醇的广泛使用会导致严重的不良事件和肠道-肺轴的破坏。已知各种微量营养素和益生菌补充剂有助于减少超炎症和恢复肠道微生物群。肠道微生物群产生的短链脂肪酸可能介导有害免疫反应和超炎症的减弱。丁酸是研究最为广泛的短链脂肪酸，以其抗炎特性而闻名。此外，丁酸已被证明可以改善多种病理学中的超炎症并减少氧化应激，包括呼吸道病毒感染。在这篇综述中，讨论了丁酸在耗尽细胞因子风暴中的潜在抗炎作用，以及其在有效管理与CoVID-19相关的危重疾病中的有用性。
review_content_zh:
作者撰写了一篇关于丁酸作为治疗COVID-19的天然替代品——地塞米松的全面综述。已知多种微量营养素和益生菌补充剂有助于减少过度炎症和恢复肠道微生物群。由肠道微生物群产生的短链脂肪酸（SCFA）可能介导有害免疫反应和过度炎症的减弱。丁酸因其抗炎特性以及在许多疾病中减少氧化应激和过度炎症的能力而广为人知。在这篇综述中，讨论了丁酸在耗竭细胞因子风暴中的潜在抗炎作用，以及其在有效管理COVID-19相关危重症中的有用性。

尽管综述写得很好，但标题似乎并未完全反映综述的内容。综述中超过50%的内容讨论了肠道微生物群以及益生菌和营养素在COVID-19发病机制中的作用，而这些并未在标题中体现。只有在后半部分才讨论了丁酸的作用。标题需要修订以全面反映文章内容。

有几篇新发表的文献讨论了丁酸在COVID-19发病机制中的作用，可以添加进来以使这篇综述更加全面，如J Li等人（2021）1；Sarkar, P等人（2020）2；Wang L等人（2017）3。

患有共病的个体中，COVID-19的发病机制会加剧。丁酸在共病中的作用是什么？这一点尚未讨论。

固有免疫细胞在COVID-19发病机制中起着重要作用。尽管综述中描述了丁酸在适应性免疫反应中的作用，但在COVID-19发病机制背景下其对固有免疫的作用却鲜有提及。

一些分子如PGE2、ROS-IKK通路在图1的图例中未予描述。

paper_title: Micronutrients in Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes
paper_abstract: About 10 to 20% of reported pregnancies have complications like spontaneous abortion (SA), preeclampsia (PE), preterm birth (PTB), and fetal growth restriction (FGR); 60% are attributed to maternal nutritional alterations. Multiple micronutrients (MMN) are supplemented in the antenatal period, but no proper validation/guidelines are available regarding dosing/time, the need for initiation, and the duration of supplementation. Studies have reported adverse pregnancy complications related to the overuse/unwanted use of multiple micronutrient supplementations during pregnancy. Identifying the exact population requiring supplementation is necessary to prevent its abuse. This article attempts to review the impacts of micronutrient deficiency/supplementation in cases of SA, FGR, and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), preterm delivery and PE. The study used a literature search using PubMed, Google Scholar, Mendeley, and Scopus Databases using search words pregnancy, spontaneous abortion, gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), fetal growth restriction (FGR), preterm delivery, preeclampsia (PE) or “adverse pregnancy” associated with minerals, micronutrients, or supplementation. The review also considered in-house literature databases, a single-window search at Kasturba Medical College (KMC) Health sciences library, MAHE (Manipal Academy of Higher Education). The figures included in the study were created by Biorender.com. Micronutrients play multiple roles during pregnancy and fetoplacental growth stimulating growth hormone secretion, Lysyl oxidase (LOX), involved in the crosslinking between collagen and elastin in the amniotic membrane, downregulation of interleukin (IL)-1 alpha, IL-1 beta, IL-4, IL-6, Il-10, IL-12, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha and several chemokines involved in hypertension, immune-inflammatory pathways, attenuate insulin resistance, structural development of neurons and glia. Over-supplementation has led to complications such as spontaneous abortion and gestational diabetes mellitus. Since there is a lack of standardization concerning micronutrient supplementation during pregnancy, there is a need for systematic study related to the role of micronutrients during each trimester of pregnancy to optimize its supplementation and to prevent hazards associated with its abuse.
review_content:
Relevance and Description:

The article addresses a pertinent and current issue as adverse pregnancy outcomes remain a significant concern in the realm of maternal and fetal health. Micronutrient supplementation during pregnancy is a common practice, but the absence of standardized guidelines has raised concerns about potential overuse and its consequent adverse effects. Grasping the role of micronutrients during pregnancy and their connection to complications is pivotal for enhancing the well-being of both mother and fetus.

Major Points:

Clear Problem Statement: The article adeptly elucidates the issue of adverse pregnancy outcomes and their correlation with maternal nutritional adjustments. It underscores the gravity of this problem, given that approximately 10 to 20% of pregnancies are affected by complications.

Significance of Micronutrients: The article offers a comprehensive overview of the multifaceted roles played by micronutrients during pregnancy. It delves into how these micronutrients influence a variety of physiological processes, including hormone secretion, collagen and elastin crosslinking, immune responses, and neurodevelopment.

Overuse of Micronutrient Supplementation: The article correctly identifies the absence of well-defined guidelines as a major concern. It highlights that the excessive or inappropriate utilization of multiple micronutrient supplements during pregnancy has resulted in adverse outcomes, such as spontaneous abortion and gestational diabetes mellitus.

Need for Systematic Studies: The article rightly emphasizes the necessity for systematic research to optimize micronutrient supplementation during each trimester of pregnancy. Such an approach could potentially avert complications associated with both deficiency and excessive supplementation.

Minor Points:

The article could be enhanced by a more extensive discussion of specific micronutrients and their distinct impacts on pregnancy outcomes. This could provide a more nuanced comprehension of the subject matter.

While the article mentions the sources it utilized, a dedicated section detailing the methodology, encompassing the search strategy and inclusion/exclusion criteria for the considered studies, would enhance clarity.

Overall Opinion:

This article constitutes a valuable addition to the field of maternal and fetal health by addressing the critical concern of micronutrient supplementation during pregnancy and its potential consequences on adverse outcomes. The problem is elucidated effectively, and the importance of addressing it is manifest. The article furnishes a comprehensive overview of the roles of micronutrients and appropriately underscores the necessity for systematic studies and standardized guidelines.

To further enrich the article, a more in-depth exploration of individual micronutrients and a more transparent presentation of the research methodology employed for the literature search would be beneficial. In summation, this work is informative and holds promise in guiding future research and clinical practices in maternal nutrition.
paper_title_zh: 不良妊娠结局中的微量营养素
paper_abstract_zh: 约10%至20%的报道妊娠伴有并发症，如自然流产（SA）、子痫前期（PE）、早产（PTB）和胎儿生长受限（FGR）；其中60%归因于母体营养改变。产前补充多种微量营养素（MMN），但关于剂量/时间、补充的必要性及持续时间尚无适当的验证/指南。研究表明，孕期过度使用/不必要使用多种微量营养素补充剂与不良妊娠并发症相关。识别确切需要补充的人群对于防止其滥用是必要的。本文试图综述微量营养素缺乏/补充在自然流产、胎儿生长受限、妊娠期糖尿病（GDM）、早产和子痫前期（PE）病例中的影响。研究通过PubMed、Google Scholar、Mendeley和Scopus数据库进行文献检索，使用关键词妊娠、自然流产、妊娠期糖尿病（GDM）、胎儿生长受限（FGR）、早产、子痫前期（PE）或与矿物质、微量营养素或补充剂相关的“不良妊娠”。综述还考虑了内部文献数据库，以及在Kasturba医学院（KMC）健康科学图书馆、MAHE（Manipal高等教育学院）进行的单窗口搜索。研究中包含的图表由Biorender.com制作。微量营养素在孕期和胎儿胎盘生长中扮演多重角色，刺激生长激素分泌、赖氨酰氧化酶（LOX）参与羊膜中胶原和弹性蛋白的交联，下调白细胞介素（IL）-1α、IL-1β、IL-4、IL-6、IL-10、IL-12、肿瘤坏死因子（TNF）-α及多种与高血压、免疫-炎症途径相关的趋化因子，减轻胰岛素抵抗，促进神经元和胶质的结构发育。过度补充导致了如自然流产和妊娠期糖尿病等并发症。由于孕期微量营养素补充缺乏标准化，有必要对孕期各阶段微量营养素的作用进行系统性研究，以优化其补充并防止滥用相关的危害。
review_content_zh:
相关性与描述：

文章探讨了与母婴健康领域密切相关且当前仍显著的问题，即不良妊娠结局。孕期微量营养素补充是常见做法，但缺乏标准化指南引发了关于潜在过度使用及其相应不良影响的担忧。理解孕期微量营养素的作用及其与并发症的联系，对于提升母婴健康至关重要。

主要观点：

明确的问题陈述：文章巧妙地阐明了不良妊娠结局及其与母体营养调整的相关性。鉴于大约10%至20%的妊娠受并发症影响，文章强调了这一问题的严重性。

微量营养素的重要性：文章全面概述了孕期微量营养素的多方面作用。深入探讨了这些微量营养素如何影响多种生理过程，包括激素分泌、胶原蛋白和弹性蛋白交联、免疫反应以及神经发育。

微量营养素补充的过度使用：文章正确指出缺乏明确定义的指南是一个主要问题。它强调孕期过度或不当地使用多种微量营养素补充剂导致了不良后果，如自然流产和妊娠期糖尿病。

系统性研究的必要性：文章恰当地强调了进行系统性研究的必要性，以优化孕期各阶段的微量营养素补充。这种方法可能预防与营养不足和过度补充相关的并发症。

次要观点：

文章可以通过更广泛地讨论特定微量营养素及其对妊娠结局的独特影响而得到提升，这可以提供对主题更细致的理解。

尽管文章提到了所使用的资料来源，但一个专门阐述方法学的部分，包括搜索策略和所考虑研究的纳入/排除标准，将增强清晰度。

总体评价：

本文通过探讨孕期微量营养素补充及其对不良妊娠结局的潜在影响这一关键问题，为母婴健康领域做出了宝贵贡献。问题阐述有效，解决其重要性的必要性显而易见。文章全面概述了微量营养素的作用，并适当地强调了系统性研究和标准化指南的必要性。

为进一步丰富文章，更深入地探讨单个微量营养素以及更透明地呈现文献搜索所采用的研究方法将是有益的。总之，这项工作信息丰富，有望指导未来母婴营养的研究和临床实践。
