paper_title: Microservice security: a systematic literature review
paper_abstract: Microservices is an emerging paradigm for developing distributed systems. With their widespread adoption, more and more work investigated the relation between microservices and security. Alas, the literature on this subject does not form a well-defined corpus: it is spread over many venues and composed of contributions mainly addressing specific scenarios or needs. In this work, we conduct a systematic review of the field, gathering 290 relevant publications-at the time of writing, the largest curated dataset on the topic. We analyse our dataset along two lines: a) quantitatively, through publication metadata, which allows us to chart publication outlets, communities, approaches, and tackled issues; b) qualitatively, through 20 research questions used to provide an aggregated overview of the literature and to spot gaps left open. We summarise our analyses in the conclusion in the form of a call for action to address the main open challenges.
review_content: Reviewer 3 Comment 3.1 As for the search for studies, some concerns should be clarified by the authors. Firstly, why did they choose to restrict their focus to “white literature” only? It is known that industry is heavily investing on microservices, with quite many solutions (also for security) being proposed and posted in industry-driven outlets (whitepapers, blog posts, YouTube channels, etc.). I am not saying that the authors should include “grey literature” as well, but they should at least clarify why they decided to keep it out from their study. (The authors actually notice this in their conclusions, hence raising the point of why they did not consider grey literature from the beginning) Agreed. We included an explanation of why we leave the grey literature out of this review at the beginning of Section 3. For a few more details, please see our answer to Comment 2.2, since the second reviewer also highlighted this issue. Comment 3.2 In addition, I am not sure on the “repeatability” of one of the exclusion criteria, viz., “We also excluded cases in which the work tangentially mentioned the satisfaction of some security aspects, without detailing the design/development of the security technologies to accomplish them”. Whilst all other exclusion criteria are objective, this criteria seem to potentially be threaten by observer bias (as an observer may a manuscript to satisfy this conditions and hence get excluded, while another may consider the treating of security “not so tangent”, so to say). The authors should clarify how they limited/avoided possible observer biases when evaluating this criteria, e.g., in a “Threats to Validity” section. We thank the reviewer for noting that we left out the description of an important methodological aspect, thus allowing us to improve the paper. We have now written a ”Threats to Validity” subsection where we detail all the threats to our study, and we outline the steps we took to mitigate them. In particular, to limit the risk of non-repeatability, the retrieval of the papers was performed by using the search engines of the selected publishers. The first filtering of the results (Step 2, cf. Section 3) was conducted by running a script by using objective criteria such as counting the number of keywords present and the length of the paper. These automatically computed results were double-checked by at least one author to prevent problems due to the parsing of PDFs and to make sure that the language of the paper was indeed English. The second filtering (Step 3, wrt. Section 3) was performed in parallel by at least two authors, by reading the title, abstract and, if needed, the body of the paper. Decision conflicts were solved by discussion by at least two authors until a consensus was reached. 4 Moreover, to allow the reproduction of our study, we now have released the dataset containing the reason for exclusion of all the papers that were not considered in the final dataset. Comment 3.3 Finally, the authors should conclude this section by listing all selected studies (e.g., in a table). This would help keeping the authors review self-contained, hence helping readers in better understanding their results. Our original draft had indeed such a table, linked to the complete bibliography of the reviewed papers. We initially placed those items as supplemental material to stay within the recommended page limits of the journal. As already noted as a reply to comment 2.3, we are grateful to the PeerJ CS editors, who allowed us to substantially exceed the page limit and permitted us to put all the references and tables regarding the reviewed papers directly in the paper. Comment 3.4 As for the research questions, the authors state that they adopted 20 dichotomous questions with the goal of favoring precision and objectiveness. It is however not clear whether/how they ensured such precision and objectiveness. The marking of a publication as “yes” or “no” for a research question seems indeed to be subject to observer biases and errors. How did the authors avoid/limit this? This should be discussed in a “Threats to Validity” section. We have expanded the Threat to validity section clarifying that for the publication analysis, due to the binary nature and formulation of the questions, the 20 research questions were answered by the main author assigned to the publication. To detect observer bias and errors, we selected a random subset of 15 papers and had a different author answer to the research questions. The calculation of the Cohen’s kappa index over the two result sets yielded a value κ = 0.99998, giving us some confidence over the perceived precision of questions and the objectiveness of answers. Comment 3.5 The presentation of results can and must be improved, by also expanding their discussion. For instance, the authors should consider presenting the publication outlets (viz., conferences and journals) as plots, so that readers can visually observe them (rather than finding a flat list of names). Much better it would be to cluster venues according to some criteria and to show aggregated results. For instance, the authors could expand their discussion on the communities where microservices’ security is most discussed (with some graphical support). We have made integrations to the text in section 5.1 as suggested, including also diagrams for an immediate graphical representation of the data related to venues. Comment 3.6 5 Also, I am not sure on whether what the authors call “qualitative results” actually provide “qualitative” information. For instance, the distribution of types of publication is still a “quantitative” information, with which the authors partition the different contributions in the field (here the authors use the word “survey” to denote “reviews”). This type of information is typically present in systematic literature reviews, and it is usually classified as a “quantitative result”. The same holds for the other aspects discussed in Sects. 5.2.2-5. The authors state “how many” publications were marked as “yes” for the research questions pertaining to each aspect, hence providing “quantitative information” on the distribution for such aspects. To make the things more “qualitative” the authors should better enter into the details of ”what” is discussed in each publication and ”how”. Whilst the “what” can be easily shown with tables showing the authors’ classification of considered works (e.g., with rows associated with works, columns with research questions, and checkmarks placed in cells to denote that a research question is treated in a research work), the “how” requires the authors to expand their discussion by discussing how (clusters of) works discuss/tackle the research questions. To avoid any confusion, we have revised the structure of the paper calling the section as “Metadata analysis” and “Publication analysis” and propagated the changes to all the text. We have also changed the label of survey in reviews in the “types of publications” as suggested by the reviewer. Comment 3.7 As a minor comment, in Section 5.2.6 the authors state that they “were surprised to find many citations to blockchain technologies (as reported above) as well as the lack of more and more mainstream technologies like service mesh and serverless”. I am not sure on whether “service mesh” are more mainstream than “blockchains”. The authors should consider rewording this, or at least cite a reference showing the higher recognition/usage of “service mesh” if compared with “blockchains”. We agree that the comparison was not sufficiently backed by data. In this case, we decided to revise the phrase withdrawing the comparison. Comment 3.8 In their concluding remarks (Sect. 6), the authors draw some concluding remarks on the open challenges that emerged from their study. A reader however misses the links between the results presented in Sect. 5 and the open challenges/research directions listed in Sect. 6. The authors should try to make such links more explicit. For instance, they could introduce open challenges (e.g., in a “highlighting box”) in Sect. 5, immediately after the discussion highlighting the need/openness of such challenge. They could then retake/recap the open challenges (as they currently do) in Sect. 6. As anticipated as a reply to comment 1.4, we have restructured our concluding section (now named “Discussion and Future Directions”) to aggregate all the findings and the discussion on future directions. 6 For each main topic emerging as a result of our review, we highlighted what aspects are left uncovered by existing literature (see the “Insight” boxes in section 5.2). In section 6, every insight is recalled and briefly discussed to motivate the need for further research. Comment 3.9 Last, but not least, systematic literature reviews, and systematic studies in general, are known to be prone to possible threats to their validity (like those I tried to highlight in my former comments above). The authors should discuss how they mitigated/avoided possible threats to the validity of their study in a devoted section. As previously stated, we now provide a section “Threats to Validity” where we discuss how we mitigated/avoided possible threats to the validity of our study. Comment 3.10 I am not sure on whether the word “survey” used by the authors in the manuscript’s title and throughout the text is correct. Snyder’s guidelines, used by the authors to design their research, speak about “systematic literature reviews”. I would hence recommend the authors to revise their wording in “systematic literature review”, both in the title and all over the manuscript. Such wording is that most commonly associated with the type of studies like that presented by the authors in this manuscript, hence helping potential readers to better grab the type of content they would find in this manuscript. We meant review since the beginning, we sincerely apologise for a mistake slipping through right in the paper’s title. Fixed. Comment 3.11 The related work discussion should be expanded to include other relevant related reviews on “microservices & security”, e.g., that on “microservices security smells” by Ponce et al. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.13303) . Thanks for the suggestion. This paper was not yet published when we wrote the first version, we are taking advantage of the revision process to include it. Comment 3.12 The authors should cite all papers they considered in their literature review, to give credit to the authors who published such papers. The authors present selected studies and their classification in a supplemental appendix. As noticed in my above comments, such information is not supplemental, but crucial for readers to understand which papers were considered and how they were classified to answer to the authors’ research questions. The information in the appendix should hence be included in the main text of the manuscript. 7 As previously stated, thanks to the additional page concession of the editor we are now able to list all the selected papers and move the table into the main part. Please note that the table, along with additional information that could be useful for reproducibility purposes is available via Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4774894 Comment 3.13 - “Alas” -¿ “Unfortunately” or “At the same time”? - p5/28: “within the” -¿ “up to the” Fixed. References [1] Jacopo Soldani. Grey literature: A safe bridge between academy and industry? ACM SIGSOFT Softw. Eng. Notes, 44(3):11–12, 2019. 8
paper_title_zh: 微服务安全：系统文献综述
paper_abstract_zh: 微服务是开发分布式系统的一种新兴范式。随着其广泛采用，越来越多的研究探讨了微服务与安全之间的关系。然而，关于这一主题的文献并未形成一个明确定义的知识体系：它分散在多个场合，主要由针对特定场景或需求的贡献组成。在本文中，我们对该领域进行了系统综述，收集了290篇相关出版物——在撰写本文时，这是该主题上最大的精选数据集。我们沿着两条线索分析我们的数据集：a）定量分析，通过出版物元数据，这使我们能够绘制出版物渠道、社区、方法以及所解决问题的图表；b）定性分析，通过20个研究问题，用于提供文献的综合概览，并发现遗留的空白。我们在结论中总结了我们的分析，并以行动号召的形式提出了应对主要开放挑战的建议。
review_content_zh:
审稿人3 评论3.1 关于研究的检索，作者需要澄清一些问题。首先，为什么他们选择仅关注“白皮书文献”？众所周知，工业界在微服务上的投入很大，提出了许多解决方案（包括安全方面的），并在行业驱动的渠道（白皮书、博客文章、YouTube频道等）上发表。我并不是说作者也应该包括“灰色文献”，但他们至少应该澄清为什么决定将其排除在研究之外。（作者实际上在结论中提到了这一点，因此引发了为什么他们一开始没有考虑灰色文献的问题）同意。我们在第3节的开始部分包含了对为什么将灰色文献排除在本次综述之外的解释。更多细节请参见我们对评论2.2的回复，因为第二位审稿人也强调了这个问题。

评论3.2 此外，我对一个排除标准中的“可重复性”表示怀疑，即“我们也排除了那些只是附带提及某些安全方面的满足，而没有详细说明实现这些安全技术的设计/开发的案例”。尽管所有其他排除标准都是客观的，但这一标准似乎可能受到观察者偏见的影响（因为一个观察者可能会认为某篇手稿满足这些条件而被排除，而另一个观察者可能会认为对安全的处理“并不那么附带”）。作者应该澄清在评估这一标准时如何限制/避免了可能的观察者偏见，例如在“有效性威胁”部分。感谢审稿人指出我们遗漏了一个重要的方法学描述，从而使我们能够改进论文。我们现在已经撰写了一个“有效性威胁”小节，详细说明了我们研究的所有威胁，并概述了我们为减轻这些威胁所采取的步骤。特别是，为了限制不可重复的风险，论文的检索是通过使用所选出版商的搜索引擎进行的。结果的初次筛选（步骤2，参见第3节）是通过运行一个脚本来进行的，使用客观标准，如关键词数量和论文长度。这些自动计算的结果由至少一位作者进行双重检查，以防止因PDF解析问题，并确保论文的语言确实是英语。第二次筛选（步骤3，参见第3节）由至少两位作者并行进行，通过阅读论文的标题、摘要和必要时正文。决策冲突由至少两位作者讨论直至达成共识解决。此外，为了允许我们研究的再现，我们现在已经发布了包含所有未纳入最终数据集的论文排除原因的数据集。 评论3.3 最后，作者应该通过列出所有选定的研究（例如，在表格中）来结束这一部分。这将有助于使作者的综述自包含，从而帮助读者更好地理解他们的结果。我们的原始草稿确实有这样一张表格，与所评论文的完整参考文献相连。我们最初将这些内容作为补充材料，以符合期刊推荐页数限制。正如在回复评论2.3时所指出的，我们感谢PeerJ CS的编辑们，他们允许我们大幅超出页数限制，并允许我们将所有关于所评论文的参考文献和表格直接放入论文中。

评论3.4 关于研究问题，作者表示他们采用了20个二元问题，目的是提高精确性和客观性。然而，尚不清楚他们如何确保这种精确性和客观性。将出版物标记为研究问题的“是”或“否”似乎确实会受到观察者偏见和错误的影响。作者是如何避免/限制这一点的？这应该在“有效性威胁”部分进行讨论。我们已经扩展了“有效性威胁”部分，澄清了对于出版物分析，由于问题的二元性质和表述，20个研究问题由分配给出版物的第一作者回答。为了检测观察者偏见和错误，我们随机选择了15篇论文，由不同的作者回答研究问题。通过计算两组结果的Cohen's kappa指数，得到κ = 0.99998，这使我们对问题的感知精确性和答案的客观性有一定信心。

评论3.5 结果的呈现可以且必须改进，同时扩展其讨论。例如，作者应考虑以图表形式呈现出版物渠道（即会议和期刊），以便读者可以直观地观察它们（而不是找到一串平面的名称列表）。更好的做法是根据某些标准对场所进行聚类，并展示汇总结果。例如，作者可以扩展关于微服务安全讨论最多的社区的讨论（并辅以图形支持）。我们已根据建议对第5.1节中的文本进行了整合，包括图表，以便立即图形化展示与场所相关的数据。

评论3.6 此外，我不确定作者所谓的“定性结果”是否实际上提供了“定性”信息。例如，出版物类型的分布仍然是一种“定量”信息，作者用它来划分该领域的不同贡献（在这里，作者使用“survey”一词来表示“综述”）。这类信息通常出现在系统文献综述中，通常被归类为“定量结果”。 同样，对于第5.2.2-5节中讨论的其他方面也是如此。作者指出“有多少”出版物在涉及每个方面的研究问题时被标记为“是”，从而提供了关于这些方面的分布的“定量信息”。为了使内容更具“定性”，作者应更深入地探讨每篇出版物中“讨论了什么”以及“如何讨论”。虽然“什么”可以通过展示作者对所考虑作品的分类的表格来轻松展示（例如，行与作品相关联，列与研究问题相关联，并在单元格中放置复选标记以表示研究问题在研究作品中得到了处理），但“如何”则需要作者通过讨论（作品集群）如何讨论/解决研究问题来扩展他们的讨论。为了避免任何混淆，我们修订了论文的结构，将部分称为“元数据分析”和“出版物分析”，并将更改传播到所有文本中。我们还根据审稿人的建议更改了综述中“出版物类型”的调查标签。

评论3.7 作为一个小意见，在第5.2.6节中，作者表示他们“惊讶地发现许多引用区块链技术（如上所述）以及缺乏更多主流技术，如服务网格和无服务器”。我不确定“服务网格”是否比“区块链”更主流。作者应考虑重新措辞，或者至少引用一个参考文献，显示“服务网格”与“区块链”相比具有更高的认可度/使用率。我们同意这种比较没有得到充分的数据支持。在这种情况下，我们决定修订该短语，撤回比较。

评论3.8 在他们的结论性评论（第6节）中，作者对他们研究中所出现的开放性挑战进行了总结性评论。然而，读者错过了第5节中呈现的结果与第6节中列出的开放性挑战/研究方向之间的联系。作者应尝试使这些联系更加明确。例如，他们可以在第5节中（在讨论突出需要/开放性挑战之后立即）引入开放性挑战（例如，在“突出框”中），然后可以在第6节中重新回顾/总结开放性挑战（正如他们目前所做的那样）。正如在回复评论1.4时所预告的，我们重新构建了我们的结论部分（现在命名为“讨论与未来方向”），以汇总所有发现和关于未来方向的讨论。对于作为我们综述结果的每个主要主题，我们突出了现有文献未覆盖的方面（见第5.2节中的“洞察”框）。在第6节中，回顾并简要讨论了每一个洞察，以激发进一步研究的必要性。 评论3.9 最后但同样重要的是，系统文献综述以及一般性的系统研究，众所周知容易受到其有效性的潜在威胁（如我在上述评论中所尝试指出的那些）。作者应在专门的章节中讨论他们如何减轻/避免了研究有效性的潜在威胁。如前所述，我们现在提供了一个“有效性威胁”章节，讨论了我们如何减轻/避免了研究有效性的潜在威胁。

评论3.10 我不确定作者在文稿标题及全文中使用的“survey”一词是否正确。作者用于设计研究的Snyder指南中提到的是“系统文献综述”。因此，我建议作者将标题及全文中的措辞改为“系统文献综述”。这种措辞通常与作者在本文稿中呈现的研究类型相关联，从而帮助潜在读者更好地理解他们将在本文稿中找到的内容类型。我们本意是综述，对于标题中的错误我们深表歉意。已修正。

评论3.11 相关工作讨论应扩展，包括其他关于“微服务与安全”的相关综述，例如Ponce等人关于“微服务安全异味”的综述（https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.13303）。感谢建议。该论文在我们撰写初稿时尚未发表，我们正在利用修订过程将其纳入。

评论3.12 作者应引用他们在文献综述中考虑的所有论文，以给予发表这些论文的作者应有的 credit。作者在补充附录中呈现了选定的研究及其分类。如我在上述评论中所指出的，这些信息并非补充性的，而是读者理解哪些论文被考虑以及如何分类以回答作者研究问题的关键。因此，附录中的信息应纳入文稿正文。如前所述，感谢编辑额外页数的特许，我们现在能够列出所有选定的论文并将表格移至正文部分。请注意，表格及为可重复性目的可能有用的额外信息可通过Zenodo获取。https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4774894

评论3.13 - “Alas” - ¿ “Unfortunately” 或 “At the same time”？ - p5/28: “within the” - ¿ “up to the” 已修正。

参考文献 [1] Jacopo Soldani. Grey literature: A safe bridge between academy and industry? ACM SIGSOFT Softw. Eng. Notes, 44(3):11–12, 2019. 8

paper_title: Oral hormone pregnancy tests and the risks of congenital malformations: a systematic review and meta-analysis
paper_abstract:
Background: Oral hormone pregnancy tests (HPTs), such as Primodos, containing ethinylestradiol and high doses of norethisterone, were given to over a million women from 1958 to 1978, when Primodos was withdrawn from the market because of concerns about possible teratogenicity. We aimed to study the association between maternal exposure to oral HPTs and congenital malformations. 
 Methods: We have performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of case-control and cohort studies that included data from pregnant women and were exposed to oral HPTs within the estimated first three months of pregnancy, if compared with a relevant control group. We used random-effects meta-analysis and assessed the quality of each study using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale for non-randomized studies. 
 Results: We found 16 case control studies and 10 prospective cohort studies, together including 71 330 women, of whom 4,209 were exposed to HPTs. Exposure to oral HPTs was associated with a 40% increased risk of all congenital malformations: pooled odds ratio (OR) = 1.40 (95% CI 1.18 to 1.66; P<0.0001; I 2 = 0%). Exposure to HPTs was associated with an increased risk of congenital heart malformations: pooled OR = 1.89 (95% CI 1.32 to 2.72; P = 0.0006; I 2 =0%); nervous system malformations  OR = 2.98 (95% CI 1.32 to 6.76; P = 0.0109 I 2 = 78%); gastrointestinal malformations, OR = 4.50 (95% CI 0.63 to 32.20; P = 0.13; I 2 = 54%); musculoskeletal malformations, OR = 2.24 (95% CI 1.23 to 4.08; P= 0.009; I 2 = 0%); the VACTERL syndrome (Vertebral defects, Anal atresia, Cardiovascular anomalies, Tracheoesophageal fistula, Esophageal atresia, Renal anomalies, and Limb defects), OR = 7.47 (95% CI 2.92 to 19.07; P < 0.0001; I 2 = 0%). 
 Conclusions: This systematic review and meta-analysis shows that use of oral HPTs in pregnancy is associated with increased risks of congenital malformations.
review_content:
I am fully supportive of this article on the effects of hormone pregnancy tests as it stands. I have no substantive criticism of the content or methods.

I am of course interested in why the regulator (MHRA) did not find comparable results but this is not a matter that should be addressed in this article.

There is one extra point that this article may speak to which is that from some time it was thought that teratogens caused signature defects - such as the phocomelia of thalidomide. This may now be a minority position (I'm not sure of this point). The findings here do not support that point of view. I can understand if the authors may think that commenting on this point is a matter for others or for another article; I mention it for consideration.

I have one very minor point about the layout which is that in the column where the numbers of women recruited to various studies is mentioned, the right justification of paragraphs leads to an odd spacing between 28 thousand and 671 - this doesn't apply when the page is resized.
paper_title_zh: 口服激素妊娠试验与先天性畸形风险：系统综述与荟萃分析
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：口服激素妊娠试验（HPTs），如含有炔雌醇和高剂量炔诺酮的Primodos，在1958年至1978年间被超过一百万名女性使用，当时Primodos因可能具有致畸性而从市场上撤回。我们旨在研究母体暴露于口服HPTs与先天性畸形之间的关联。

方法：我们对包括孕妇数据并在怀孕前三个月内暴露于口服HPTs的病例对照研究和队列研究进行了系统综述和荟萃分析，并与相关对照组进行比较。我们使用随机效应荟萃分析，并使用纽卡斯尔-渥太华非随机研究量表评估每项研究的质量。

结果：我们发现了16项病例对照研究和10项前瞻性队列研究，共包括71,330名女性，其中4,209名暴露于HPTs。暴露于口服HPTs与所有先天性畸形风险增加40%相关：合并比值比（OR）= 1.40（95% CI 1.18至1.66；P<0.0001；I²=0%）。暴露于HPTs与先天性心脏畸形风险增加相关：合并OR = 1.89（95% CI 1.32至2.72；P=0.0006；I²=0%）；神经系统畸形OR = 2.98（95% CI 1.32至6.76；P=0.0109；I²=78%）；胃肠道畸形OR = 4.50（95% CI 0.63至32.20；P=0.13；I²=54%）；肌肉骨骼畸形OR = 2.24（95% CI 1.23至4.08；P=0.009；I²=0%）；VACTERL综合征（脊椎缺陷、肛门闭锁、心血管异常、气管食管瘘、食管闭锁、肾脏异常和肢体缺陷），OR = 7.47（95% CI 2.92至19.07；P<0.0001；I²=0%）。

结论：这项系统综述和荟萃分析表明，孕期使用口服HPTs与先天性畸形风险增加相关。
review_content_zh:
我完全支持目前这篇文章关于激素妊娠测试影响的内容。我对文章的内容或方法没有实质性的批评。

当然，我对监管机构（MHRA）为何未得出相似结果感到好奇，但这并不是这篇文章应该讨论的问题。

关于排版，我有一个非常小的意见，即在提到不同研究中招募的女性数量的那一栏中，段落的右对齐导致28千和671之间的间距显得不协调——当页面大小调整时，这个问题不存在。

paper_title: Lots of movement, little progress: A review of reptile home range literature
paper_abstract: Reptiles are the most species-rich terrestrial vertebrate group with a broad diversity of life history traits. Biotelemetry is an essential methodology for studying reptiles as it compensates for several limitations when studying their natural history. We evaluated trends in terrestrial reptile spatial ecology studies focusing upon quantifying home ranges for the past twenty years. We assessed 290 English-language reptile home range studies published from 2000-2019 via a structured literature review investigating publications' study location, taxonomic group, methodology, reporting, and analytical techniques. Substantial biases remain in both location and taxonomic groups in the literature, with nearly half of all studies (45%) originating from the USA. Snakes were most often studied, and crocodiles were least often studied, while testudines tended to have the greatest within study sample sizes. More than half of all studies lacked critical methodological details, limiting the number of studies for inclusion in future meta-analyses (55% of studies lacked information on individual tracking durations, and 51% lacked sufficient information on the number of times researchers recorded positions). Studies continue to rely on outdated methods to quantify space-use (including Minimum Convex Polygons and Kernel Density Estimators), often failing to report subtleties regarding decisions that have substantial impact on home range area estimates. Moving forward researchers can select a suite of appropriate analytical techniques tailored to their research question (dynamic Brownian Bridge Movement Models for within sample interpolation, and autocorrelated Kernel Density Estimators for beyond sample extrapolation). Only 1.4% of all evaluated studies linked to available and usable telemetry data, further hindering scientific consensus. We ultimately implore herpetologists to adopt transparent reporting practices and make liberal use of open data platforms to maximize progress in the field of reptile spatial ecology.

paper_title_zh: 大量移动，少有进展：爬行动物家域文献综述
paper_abstract_zh: 爬行动物是物种最丰富的陆生脊椎动物类群，具有广泛的生命史特征多样性。生物遥测是研究爬行动物的重要方法，因为它弥补了在研究其自然史时的若干局限性。我们评估了过去二十年间陆地爬行动物空间生态学研究的趋势，重点关注家域的量化。通过结构化的文献综述，我们评估了2000-2019年间发表的290篇英文爬行动物家域研究，调查了这些出版物的研究地点、分类群、方法学、报告和分析技术。文献中在研究地点和分类群方面仍存在显著偏倚，近一半的研究（45%）来自美国。蛇类最常被研究，鳄鱼类最少被研究，而龟鳖类往往具有最大的研究内样本量。超过一半的研究缺乏关键的方法学细节，限制了未来元分析中可纳入的研究数量（55%的研究缺乏个体追踪时长的信息，51%缺乏关于研究者记录位置次数的充分信息）。研究继续依赖过时的方法来量化空间利用（包括最小凸多边形和核密度估计），常常未能报告对家域面积估计有重大影响的决策细节。未来，研究人员可以选择一套适合其研究问题的分析技术（如动态布朗桥运动模型用于样本内插值，自相关核密度估计用于样本外推）。在所有评估的研究中，仅有1.4%链接到可用和可用的遥测数据，进一步阻碍了科学共识的形成。我们最终敦促爬行动物学家采用透明的报告实践，并充分利用开放数据平台，以最大化爬行动物空间生态学领域的进展。

paper_title: Efficient Large Language Models: A Survey
paper_abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in important tasks such as natural language understanding and language generation, and thus have the potential to make a substantial impact on our society. Such capabilities, however, come with the considerable resources they demand, highlighting the strong need to develop effective techniques for addressing their efficiency challenges. In this survey, we provide a systematic and comprehensive review of efficient LLMs research. We organize the literature in a taxonomy consisting of three main categories, covering distinct yet interconnected efficient LLMs topics from model-centric, data-centric, and framework-centric perspective, respectively. We have also created a GitHub repository where we organize the papers featured in this survey at https://github.com/AIoT-MLSys-Lab/Efficient-LLMs-Survey. We will actively maintain the repository and incorporate new research as it emerges. We hope our survey can serve as a valuable resource to help researchers and practitioners gain a systematic understanding of efficient LLMs research and inspire them to contribute to this important and exciting field.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This paper presents a very comprehensive survey on the efficiency of LLMs. Different from existing efficient LLMs surveys that typically focus on one specific aspect (e.g. inference efficiency), the concept of efficiency here is broad, covering model-centric efficiency such as model compression, efficient pretraining, efficient fine-tuning, efficient inference, and efficient architecture, data-centric efficiency that includes data selection and prompt engineering, and frameworks that compares different open-source libraries. Each of these subcategories are further classified with many details. I appreciate that the authors constructed such a taxonomy and put different types of efficiency into a single survey.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
### Strengths 1. Efficiency is one of the most important topics in LLMs, and there are many research papers out every week focusing on different types of efficiencies. This survey is very comprehensive to put various efficiencies together. It is a nice read to understand the big picture of these research works. 2. Inside each of the sub-topics such as model compression and efficient fine-tuning, the authors did a good job to further construct the taxonomy, and each subsection in this paper is like a nice separate survey on its own. ### Weaknesses 1. Currently the survey reads more like a bland description of each research work inside each subtopic. However, I think it is important to summarize and compare different lines of research that aim for the same goal to understand the connections among different research lines as well as their pros/cons. For example, in model compression, there are different types of approaches such as quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation. What are the pros/cons of each of these methods? What is the current preferred practice? What is the SOTA for model compression? Why are some of the lines more popular than the others? What is recommended to compress a model and why? Discussing these questions is important for the readers to understand the different tradeoffs and properties from these methods. 2. Another example aligning with the first point is on parameter-efficient fine-tuning. It is not wise to group LoRA separately from the adapters, when LoRA is more like a special case of adapters and LoRA is also often referred to as LoRA adapters. Similar to before, among these many different PEFT methods, what are their connections? Why does LoRA stand out as the most popular one? What are their pros and cons? For example, [1] presents a unified view to connect these different methods – I would like to see this kind of discussion for each subsection of the paper to raise more interesting insights and comparisons, rather than only blandly describing a lot of papers. [1] He et al. Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning. ICLR 2022.

**Requested Changes:**
As mentioned in the weaknesses above, I think more discussions on the connections and pros/cons of different research lines inside each subtopic should be presented to provide more insights and make the paper coherent. This will offer a clearer picture on what is going on in this regime as well. Currently the paper is merely describing each paper under the constructed taxonomy, with few discussions and insights.

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes

**Rebuttal Comments:**
Response to Reviewer npES: > Currently the survey reads more like a bland description of each research work inside each subtopic. However, I think it is important to summarize and compare different lines of research that aim for the same goal to understand the connections among different research lines as well as their pros/cons. For example, in model compression, there are different types of approaches such as quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation. What are the pros/cons of each of these methods? What is the current preferred practice? What is the SOTA for model compression? Why are some of the lines more popular than the others? What is recommended to compress a model and why? Discussing these questions is important for the readers to understand the different tradeoffs and properties from these methods. Thank you for all the constructive suggestions. + We have added definitions, limitations/settings of use, and specific categories of efficiency (parameters, training, inference, serving, data) for each sub-method within their sections, providing readers with insights into the pros/cons of each type of method. + In each section, we have introduced connections among the methods, such as whether they are orthogonal or iterative improvements to other methods. + We organized the methods according to their publication date and compared their performance under the benchmarks mentioned in the paper, contrasting current methods with previous ones. This aids readers in understanding the current state-of-the-art (SOTA) models and the most popular models. **Please refer to the newly added blue text in each subsection.** > Another example aligning with the first point is on parameter-efficient fine-tuning. It is not wise to group LoRA separately from the adapters, when LoRA is more like a special case of adapters and LoRA is also often referred to as LoRA adapters. Similar to before, among these many different PEFT methods, what are their connections? Why does LoRA stand out as the most popular one? What are their pros and cons? For example, [1] presents a unified view to connect these different methods – I would like to see this kind of discussion for each subsection of the paper to raise more interesting insights and comparisons, rather than only blandly describing a lot of papers. The main goal of our survey is to categorize methods as precisely as possible, and people use those names to specifically refer to those specific ways of inserting extra parameters. Therefore, we discuss Adapter-based tuning and LoRA separately and introduce the specific definitions of methods in the first sentence of each subsection to tell the difference.Specifically, Adapters are bottleneck-like trainable modules integrated into LLMs, which first down-project the input feature vector followed by a non-linear layer and then up-project back to the original size. Differently, LoRA is often referred to using the low-rank decomposition strategy to replace the gradient change. And Prefix-Tuning adds a series of trainable vectors, known as prefix tokens, to each layer in an LLM.
paper_title_zh: 高效大型语言模型：综述
paper_abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在自然语言理解、语言生成等重要任务上展现出惊人的能力，因此有可能对我们社会产生重大影响。然而，这些能力伴随着对资源的巨大需求，突显了开发有效技术以解决其效率挑战的强烈需求。在本综述中，我们提供了对高效LLMs研究的系统性和全面性回顾。我们将文献组织在一个分类法中，包括三个主要类别，分别从模型中心、数据中心和框架中心的视角，涵盖不同但相互关联的高效LLMs主题。我们还在GitHub上创建了一个仓库，其中组织了本综述中提到的论文，网址为https://github.com/AIoT-MLSys-Lab/Efficient-LLMs-Survey。我们将积极维护该仓库，并随着新研究的出现而纳入新的内容。我们希望我们的综述能作为一项宝贵的资源，帮助研究人员和实践者系统地了解高效LLMs研究，并激发他们为这个重要而激动人心的领域做出贡献。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文对大型语言模型（LLMs）的效率进行了非常全面的综述。与现有通常专注于某一特定方面（例如推理效率）的高效LLMs综述不同，这里的效率概念更为广泛，涵盖了以模型为中心的效率，如模型压缩、高效预训练、高效微调、高效推理和高效架构；以数据为中心的效率，包括数据选择和提示工程；以及比较不同开源库的框架。每个子类别都进一步细分，并详细阐述。我赞赏作者构建了这样的分类法，并将不同类型的效率纳入同一篇综述中。

**优点与不足：**
### 优点
1. 效率是LLMs中最重要的主题之一，每周都有许多研究论文关注不同类型的效率。这篇综述非常全面，将各种效率整合在一起。它是了解这些研究工作的整体图景的良好读物。
2. 在每个子主题（如模型压缩和高效微调）内部，作者很好地进一步构建了分类法，本文的每个小节都像是一个独立的优质综述。

### 不足
1. 目前这篇综述更像是对每个子主题内每项研究工作的平淡描述。然而，我认为总结和比较旨在实现同一目标的不同研究线，以理解不同研究线之间的联系以及它们的优缺点，是非常重要的。例如，在模型压缩中，有量化、剪枝和知识蒸馏等不同方法。每种方法的优缺点是什么？当前的首选实践是什么？模型压缩的当前最佳水平（SOTA）是什么？为什么某些研究线比其他更受欢迎？推荐压缩模型的方法是什么，为什么？讨论这些问题对于读者理解这些方法的不同权衡和特性非常重要。
2. 与第一点相关的另一个例子是参数高效微调。将LoRA与适配器分开归类是不明智的，因为LoRA更像是一种特殊的适配器，并且LoRA也常被称为LoRA适配器。与之前类似，在这些许多不同的PEFT方法中，它们之间的联系是什么？为什么LoRA脱颖而出成为最受欢迎的方法？它们的优缺点是什么？例如，[1]提出了一个统一视角来连接这些不同方法——我希望看到本文每个小节都有这种讨论，以提出更有趣的见解和比较，而不仅仅是平淡地描述大量论文。[1] He et al. Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning. ICLR 2022.

**请求的修改：**
如上所述不足之处，我认为在每个子主题内应更多地讨论不同研究线之间的联系及其优缺点，以提供更多见解并使论文连贯。这也将为该领域的现状提供更清晰的图景。目前，论文仅描述了在构建的分类法下每篇论文，缺乏讨论和见解。

**声明与证据：**
是

**受众：**
是

**反驳意见：**
对评审者npES的回应：> 目前这篇综述更像是对每个子主题内每项研究工作的平淡描述。然而，我认为总结和比较旨在实现同一目标的不同研究线，以理解不同研究线之间的联系以及它们的优缺点，是非常重要的。例如，在模型压缩中，有量化、剪枝和知识蒸馏等不同方法。每种方法的优缺点是什么？当前的首选实践是什么？模型压缩的当前最佳水平（SOTA）是什么？为什么某些研究线比其他更受欢迎？推荐压缩模型的方法是什么，为什么？讨论这些问题对于读者理解这些方法的不同权衡和特性非常重要。感谢所有建设性的建议。+ 我们在每个子方法的章节中增加了定义、使用限制/设置以及具体效率类别（参数、训练、推理、服务、数据），为读者提供了每种方法优缺点的见解。+ 在每个章节中，我们介绍了方法之间的联系，例如它们是否是其他方法正交或迭代的改进。+ 我们根据论文发表日期组织了方法，并比较了论文中提到的基准下的性能，将当前方法与之前的方法进行对比。这有助于读者理解当前最佳水平（SOTA）模型和最受欢迎的模型。**请参考每个小节中新增的蓝色文本。**> 与第一点相关的另一个例子是参数高效微调。将LoRA与适配器分开归类是不明智的，因为LoRA更像是一种特殊的适配器，并且LoRA也常被称为LoRA适配器。类似地，在这些许多不同的PEFT方法中，它们之间的联系是什么？为什么LoRA脱颖而出成为最受欢迎的方法？它们的优缺点是什么？例如，[1]提出了一个统一视角来连接这些不同方法——我希望看到本文每个小节都有这种讨论，以提出更有趣的见解和比较，而不仅仅是平淡地描述大量论文。我们综述的主要目标是尽可能精确地对方法进行分类，人们使用这些名称来特指那些特定的插入额外参数的方式。因此，我们分别讨论了基于适配器的调优和LoRA，并在每个小节的第一句中介绍了方法的特定定义，以区分差异。具体来说，适配器是集成到LLMs中的瓶颈状可训练模块，首先将输入特征向量降维，然后通过非线性层，再升维回原始大小。不同地，LoRA通常指使用低秩分解策略来替代梯度变化。而Prefix-Tuning则在每个LLM层的开头添加一系列可训练向量，称为前缀标记。

paper_title: COVID-19 in pregnancy: What do we really know?
paper_abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), continues to escalate worldwide and has become a pressing global health concern. This article comprehensively reviews the current knowledge on the impact of COVID-19 over pregnant women and neonates, as well as current recommendations for their management. We also analyse previous evidences from viral respiratory diseases such as SARS, Middle East respiratory syndrome, and influenza that may help to guide clinical practice during the current pandemic. We collected 23 case reports, case series, and case-control studies (18 from China) comprising 174 pregnant women with COVID-19. The majority of mothers showed a clinical presentation of the disease similar to that of non-infected adults. Preliminary evidences point towards a potentially increased risk of pregnancy adverse outcomes in women with COVID-19, with preterm delivery the most frequently observed (16.7%) followed by fetal distress (9.77%). The most commonly reported adverse neonatal outcomes included respiratory symptoms (7.95%) and low birth weight (6.81%). A few studies reported other maternal comorbidities that can influence these outcomes. Mothers with other comorbidities may be at higher risk of infection. Mother-to-child transmission of SARS-CoV-2 appears unlikely, with no study observing intrauterine transmission, and a few cases of neonatal infection reported a few hours after birth. Although the WHO and other health authorities have published interim recommendations for care and management of pregnant women and infants during COVID-19 pandemic, many questions remain open. Pregnant women should be considered in prevention and control efforts, including the development of drugs and vaccines against SARS-CoV-2. Further research is needed to confirm the exact impact of COVID-19 infection during pregnancy. To fully quantify this impact, we urgently need to integrate the current knowledge about viral characteristics, epidemiology, disease immunopathology, and potential therapeutic strategies with data from the clinical practice.
review_content:
This a very interesting review, addressing a relevant topic in the context of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), its impact on pregnancy. Although I congratulate the authors for the efforts, before can be fully acceptable it deserves some improvements, including an update of the review. This review is based on two searches in the literature in two databases. The last review on April 8, 2020. Then, this means, more than four months have passed. For COVID-19 this is a lot. Multiple case reports, studies, and even reviews, and systematic reviews have came out. Then, this needs to be updated, including other additional databases, such as Scopus, and Web of Sciences. The section of Mother-to-Child transmission should be reviewed carefully, as new evidence suggested, that although sporadically, some cases ended in vertical transmission.

Finally, I would suggest to extend more the Conclusions, specially to better discuss the current and future implications of the COVID-19 on pregnancy.
paper_title_zh: 孕期新冠病毒感染：我们真正了解多少？
paper_abstract_zh: 2019冠状病毒病（COVID-19）大流行，由严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2（SARS-CoV-2）引起，持续在全球蔓延，已成为紧迫的全球健康问题。本文全面综述了当前关于COVID-19对孕妇和新生儿影响的知识，以及当前对她们管理的建议。我们还分析了来自严重急性呼吸综合征（SARS）、中东呼吸综合征和流感等病毒性呼吸道疾病的先前证据，这些证据可能有助于指导当前大流行期间的临床实践。我们收集了23篇病例报告、病例系列和病例对照研究（其中18篇来自中国），涉及174名感染COVID-19的孕妇。大多数母亲的临床表现与非感染成人相似。初步证据表明，感染COVID-19的孕妇可能面临妊娠不良结局的风险增加，早产是最常观察到的（16.7%），其次是胎儿窘迫（9.77%）。最常见的围产儿不良结局包括呼吸症状（7.95%）和低出生体重（6.81%）。少数研究报告了其他可能影响这些结局的母体合并症。有其他合并症的母亲可能感染风险更高。SARS-CoV-2的母婴传播似乎不太可能，没有研究观察到宫内传播，少数新生儿感染病例在出生后几小时报告。尽管世界卫生组织和其他卫生机构已发布关于COVID-19大流行期间孕妇和婴儿护理和管理的临时建议，但仍有许多问题悬而未决。孕妇应在预防和控制工作中予以考虑，包括开发针对SARS-CoV-2的药物和疫苗。需要进一步研究以确认COVID-19感染对妊娠的确切影响。为了全面量化这一影响，我们迫切需要将当前关于病毒特性、流行病学、疾病免疫病理学和潜在治疗策略的知识与临床实践数据相结合。
review_content_zh:
这是一篇非常有趣的综述，探讨了2019冠状病毒病（COVID-19）背景下其对妊娠的影响这一相关话题。尽管我祝贺作者们的努力，但在其完全可接受之前，仍需进行一些改进，包括更新综述内容。该综述基于在两个数据库中的两次文献检索，最后一次综述更新于2020年4月8日。这意味着已经过去了四个多月。对于COVID-19而言，这段时间非常长。在此期间，涌现了多篇病例报告、研究，甚至包括综述和系统综述。因此，需要更新综述，并纳入其他附加数据库，如Scopus和Web of Science。母亲至婴儿传播部分应仔细审查，因为有新证据表明，尽管偶发，但有些病例最终发生了垂直传播。

最后，我建议进一步扩展结论部分，特别是更好地讨论COVID-19对妊娠当前及未来的影响。

paper_title: Preliminary evidence for seasonality of Covid-19 due to ultraviolet radiation
paper_abstract: The Covid-19 pandemic has spread across the world during early 2020, with unforeseen consequences. Beyond social measures and biomedical research, it is important to assess the seasonality of the epidemic to inform strategies, with limited available data in the short period of time between the March equinox and the June solstice. While the effect of multiple factors is being investigated, little attention has been paid to ultraviolet (UV) radiation, a key parameter of seasonal forcing. We review the effects of UV radiation, proposing it as a potential element of seasonality, and provide evidence from the current literature and scant, yet revealing, observations. Explicit consideration should be given to UV radiation for the seasonality of Covid-19 at high latitudes and altitudes, based on the SARS and MERS epidemics and coronavirus diseases, and not just the ‘warmer days’ of summer.
review_content:
This paper explores the possible impact of UV exposure on Covid-19. In my view it has a number of weaknesses.
 1. The first paragraph is strange. It presents some arguably minor aspects of Covid-19 and then concludes we need to understand climate factors. This is a non-sequiteur. The paragraph should present a coherent argument for why we need to understand climate impacts on Covid-19.
 2. The second paragraph considers some relevant literature. This is helpful, but not up to date [to today] - notably missing 1 (interest declared).
 3. The reference to deploying artificial UV-C is strange and seems wrong in a paper about seasonality. As described, UV-C from artificial sources could be used to inactivate SARS-CoV-2 in e.g., hospitals, but it cannot influence seasonality of transmission. I suggest this is because it is in a paragraph taken from the pre-print.
 4. Page 4. The paragraph on seabirds is very weak and should be removed. The cited paper found no evidence of coronavirus [or other viruses] in any season in the seabirds; the lack of detection of coronaviruses is not evidence at all of an impact of season.
 5. Page 4. The discussion of SARS/MERS should consider the evidence that they had a seasonal cycle or were affected by climate or UV.
 6. Page 4. The suggestion that the southern hemisphere seems to have escaped the worst (supportive of seasonality etc) has been overtaken by events (e.g., Brasil) and the authors may wish to update the statement. Really, this was the danger from publishing analyses so early in the pandemic. This, and other examples, seem to be cherry picking examples to support their hypothesis.
 7. Figure 1. I have several concerns about this figure. The authors say the figure will be updated but it ends in May 2020. It is very hard to discern patterns in the figure It says in the title "three countries" but I think there are >140. The data are counts – of what? Cases, hospitalisations, deaths? Whichever, it is well known that different countries count these measures in different ways [e.g., UK, death from covid = death by any cause <28 days from a covid+ve test]. Further, many other factors will affect these counts and it is wrong to only look at climate factors.
 8. Figure 2 is very hard to follow. Nevertheless, I note that the right-hand panel makes no attempt to include population density; while in the left hand panel it is mentioned but not actually accounted for. In both cases, population density is strongly associated with altitude, and altitude with UV - so population density MUST be accounted for.
All in all, this is a weak paper. Its arguments are poor, it cherry picks examples, the data analysis is rudimentary and needs to include many other possible explanatory factors in addition to those related to UV.
paper_title_zh: 紫外线辐射导致新冠病毒季节性的初步证据
paper_abstract_zh: 2020年初，新冠疫情在全球蔓延，带来了不可预见的后果。除了社会措施和生物医学研究外，评估疫情的季節性对于制定策略至关重要，尤其是在春分到夏至之间这一短时间内可用的数据有限。尽管正在研究多种因素的影响，但很少关注紫外线（UV）辐射，这一季节性驱动力的关键参数。我们回顾了紫外线辐射的影响，将其作为季节性的潜在因素，并提供了当前文献和虽少但具有揭示性的观察证据。基于SARS和MERS疫情以及冠状病毒疾病的经验，应明确考虑紫外线辐射对高纬度和高海拔地区新冠疫情季节性的影响，而不仅仅是夏季的“温暖日子”。
review_content_zh:
本文探讨了紫外线暴露对新冠病毒肺炎（Covid-19）可能产生的影响。在我看来，它存在一些不足之处。
1. 第一段显得奇怪。它提出了一些有争议的Covid-19的次要方面，然后得出我们需要了解气候因素的结论。这是逻辑不连贯的。该段落应提供一个连贯的论点，说明为什么我们需要了解气候对Covid-19的影响。
2. 第二段考虑了一些相关文献。这很有帮助，但未更新至最新（截至今天）——特别是缺少一篇文献（利益声明）。
3. 提到部署人工紫外线C（UV-C）的部分显得奇怪，且在一篇关于季节性的论文中似乎不恰当。如所述，人工来源的UV-C可用于灭活SARS-CoV-2，例如在医院中，但它不能影响传播的季节性。我建议这是因为该段落来自预印本。
4. 第4页。关于海鸟的段落非常薄弱，应予以删除。所引用的论文在任何季节的海鸟中都未发现冠状病毒（或其他病毒）的证据；未检测到冠状病毒根本不是季节性影响的证据。
5. 第4页。关于SARS/MERS的讨论应考虑它们是否有季节性周期或受气候或紫外线影响的证据。
6. 第4页。关于南半球似乎避免了最严重情况的建议（支持季节性等）已被后续事件（如巴西）所推翻，作者可能需要更新这一说法。实际上，这正是大流行早期发表分析的危险所在。这一点和其他例子似乎是为了支持他们的假设而挑选的。
7. 图1。我对这张图有几个担忧。作者表示图表将更新，但数据截止于2020年5月。图中很难辨别出模式。标题中提到“三个国家”，但我想实际上有超过140个。数据是计数——计的是什么？病例、住院、死亡？无论哪种，众所周知不同国家对这些指标的计数方式不同（例如，英国，新冠死亡是指新冠阳性测试后28天内任何原因的死亡）。此外，许多其他因素也会影响这些计数，仅考虑气候因素是不正确的。
8. 图2很难理解。尽管如此，我注意到右图没有尝试包含人口密度；而左图中虽提及但未实际考虑。在这两种情况下，人口密度与海拔高度密切相关，而海拔与紫外线也相关——因此必须考虑人口密度。
总的来说，这是一篇薄弱的论文。其论点不充分，挑选例证，数据分析基础且需要包括除紫外线相关因素外的许多其他可能的解释因素。

paper_title: Evaluation of cognitive load in team sports: literature review
paper_abstract: In team sports, load management has become one of the most common areas of investigation, given that effective control over load is the key to being able to optimize performance and avoid injuries. Despite the constant evolution and innovation in the latest theories, we can see a clear tendency in load management that focuses on physiological and mechanical aspects and neglects its cognitive character, which generates the variability inherent in the performance of athletes in a changing environment. Indicators of response that inform methods of control over cognitive load can include cognitive, physiological and behavioral indicators. However, limited investigations exist to support the reliability of each indicator regarding cognitive load. For this reason, the objective of this literature review is to present strategies used to manage cognitive load in team sports, as well as the indicators utilized for such a proposition and their relationships in specific contexts.
review_content: Reviewer 2 (Kristy Martin) Thanks for your review and your suggestions. Basic reporting General Comments: The reviewer commends the authors on addressing such an important topic. As is stated in the introduction, cognitive load is known to influence physical performance, yet its existence is rarely, if ever, acknowledged when considering training load in sport. Further, I do not know of any literature which aims to address this issue. That being said, there are several issues which detract from this important work in its current state. One general issue is that the outcomes of your literature search i.e., tools that aim to assess cognitive load and 'indicators' of cognitive load are not discussed until the very end of the introduction and not elaborated on. As this forms the major part of your manuscript I suggest increasing the focus on this. Please see my further specific comments below. Thank you very much for this comment. We respond to all the suggestions below. Your comments make this article better. Specific Comments: Lines 36-37 - It is unclear why change of direction and cognitive requirements are coupled together? Is change of direction not just as much a physical task as the jumps or accelerations mentioned above? We agree. The change of direction is a physical and mechanical task, it should be in the same sentence as the jumps or accelerations. So, we have put it. See line 36-37. Line 37 – I suggest you either provide a reference for the statement ‘cognitive requirements and changes of direction are also identified….’ Or remove the words ‘identified as’ Agreed. We have removed "identified as". Lines 43-55 – I enjoyed this section. This paragraph is well written and speaks to the importance of this topic. Thank you very much for this comment, we really appreciate it. Line 53 – Define is not the correct term here. Something like ‘conclude’ would be more suitable. Thanks. We have changed 'correct' to 'concluded'. Lines 56-57 – Is this how you are defining cognitive load for this review? If so, I suggest making this more explicit in this sentence. Yes, this is for us the definition of cognitive load. We have added 'we consider that the ...' in order to make it more explicit. See line 58-59. Lines 60-62 – I agree with the authors on this point; however, it is unclear how this relates to cognitive load. This concept could be further explained. In order to further explain the relationship between cognitive load and emotional aspects, the phrase 'The regulation of these emotions involves processes through which individuals influence their emotions. These processes require effort, thereby draining cognitive resources (Schmeichel, 2007).' has been added with its respective citation. See lines 61-66. Line 68-70 – This sentence is not clear. Please reword. We have reword the sentence. 'This cognitive demand combined to the effects of the internal and external load, can cause a maladaptation or rejection of the suggested load. This will directly influence whether the athlete is physically and / or mentally prepared for exposure to another training stimulus, known as the readiness to train / compete (Gabbett, 2017).’ See lines 72-75. Line 81 – The term/concept of readiness is only introduced here. I suggest introducing earlier and explaining what you mean by this term. Thank you, we agree with you. We have used the previous sentence change (line 68-70), in order to better describe this term. Lines 86-89 – Reading to this point I was unsure what the aims of the review would be. Can these aims be introduced earlier or the earlier sections lead to the aims more explicitly? Further, it is not clear what is meant by an ‘indicator’. An explanation of this, and/or an example would increase clarity. Thank you very much for your comments. Text has been modified according to it, on lines 47-49, 89-92. Experimental design The methodology section requires more detail, as well as context or rationale, for a number of methodological decisions i.e., Line 93 - Why was the search limited to literature from 1970 onward? Thank you. We pretended to offer concurrent resources to the literature from this point. Line 106 - Can you explain in a little more detail what is meant by 'management of cognitive, mental or psychological load'. Thanks for this comment. To make it better understood we have added the line 114-116. Line 112 - What is considered a 'real sport' Thanks for your comment. This concept is poorly translated. Now it has been written as it should: ‘Individual sports and studies in situations far from sports reality were excluded, as well as analyses in laboratory situations’. See line 119. What was the screening process i.e., did one author screen all articles? Completed as a team? Thank you for your comment. Screening process has been included on lines 121-126 and flowchart. Validity of the findings The findings, although interesting and valid, need more context within the results/discussion. The broad array of studies included, i.e., different sports, different aims of studies etc make it difficult to follow and combine or compare the findings of the different studies. A greater description of the studies referenced is needed in text, not just in tables. Further, the discussion largely describes the tools used to assess cognitive load. This is not particularly beneficial to the reader, rather a discussion of the pro's and con's of such measure might be more useful. The discussion would also benefit from thorough proof reading and editing. Thanks for your comments. In order to make the explanation of the cited articles more extensive, the following lines have been modified: 47-49, 89-92, 133-139, 142-149, 195-199, 308-315, 317-324. Lines 121-123 - As mentioned previously, an explanation of what is meant by an 'indicator' is required. As well as your classifications of indicators. Thank you very much for your comments. Text has been modified according to it, on lines 47-49, 89-92, 133-139. Lines 126-127 - This sentence needs more explanation and context. Thanks. We have further developed this paragraph. See lines 142-149. Line 129 - I don't understand what is meant by 'analysis of indicators of response'. Thanks for your comment. Having made the explanation of indicators and the three types of indicators more extensive, we hope that this sentence does not remain out of context. Line 144 - Is this study a laboratory study? Laboratory studies were part of the exclusion criteria. There appears to be a number of lab studies included i.e., Smith (2016) These two studies by Alarcón et al., 2017; 2018 are not laboratory studies. As you will see in Table 1 the Alarcón et al. 2018 study is in soccer specific situations and the Alarcón et al. 2017 study is in basketball specific situations. The same is true for that of Smith et al., 2016. It is a study that analyzes the effects of mental fatigue in soccer-specific tests. Line 153 - No need for the word scale. The S in VAS is scale. We have deleted the word scale Line 161 - Is bibliography the correct word here? We believe that yes, what is meant is that this indicator has been widely used bibliographically to describe fatigue and lack of energy. Lines 166-173 - This section does not really discuss the VAS, which is the subheading this section falls under. Thank you for your comment, you have made us see that in the text it is not very clear that the VAS indicator of MF i ME is still being talked about. To make it clear, the pertinent modifications have been made. See lines 183-190. Line 177 - Does CSAI stand for anything? You are absolutely right. The meaning of the acronyms is missing. It has been indicated in parentheses. ‘CSAI-2 (Competitive State Anxiety Inventory 2)’. Line 184-188 - This section needs more explanation. E.g., what is meant by somatic and cognitive anxiety. The explanation has been expanded, defining somatic and cognitive anxiety (lines 195-199). ‘Cognitive anxiety refers to the negative feelings that the subject has about his or her performance and the consequences of the outcome. Somatic anxiety, on the other hand, refers to the perception of physiological indicators of anxiety such as muscle tension, increased heart rate, sweating and stomach discomfort’. Line 192 - Spell out the full name for POMS at first use. Agreed. We have spelled POMS in the first use. Line 203 - Change "In a study...". In what study? Apologies for the error, as there is a typo here. The study you are referring to is that of Mashiko et al. (2004). ‘In a study' has been replaced by 'In their study'. Line 237 - Reference for this statement? The correct citation of this statement has been made. Line 244 - This full naming of SIATE needs to occur when this acronym is first used. Agreed. We have full naming SIATE in the first use, as well as VSC. Line 285 - We or other authors? Sorry, this is a typo. The results are from other authors. It has been changed to 'no significant differences have been found in'. See line 302. Lines 294-295 - Physical fatigue could also increase reaction time. Thank you for your comment. We have gone deeper into the subject by citing new articles and expanding the parameters that can affect reaction time. See lines 308-315. Lines 297-301 - Here and elsewhere, these studies need describing. This information holds no value without greater explanation or context. Thank you for your comment. The studies have been more detailed. See lines 317-324 The conclusion brings in a lot of new information. A conclusion typically summarises the information stated previously. I would also suggest having the practical applications section, prior to the conclusion. Thanks for your comment. We have placed this order following the style of the narrative reviews published in PeerJ.
paper_title_zh: 团队运动中认知负荷评估：文献综述
paper_abstract_zh: 在团队运动中，负荷管理已成为最常见的调查领域之一，因为有效的负荷控制是优化表现和避免伤病的关键。尽管最新理论不断演变和创新，但我们仍可看到负荷管理中存在一种明显倾向，即专注于生理和机械方面，而忽视了其认知特性，这导致了运动员在变化环境中表现出的内在变异性。用于告知认知负荷控制方法的响应指标可以包括认知、生理和行为指标。然而，支持每个指标在认知负荷方面的可靠性的研究有限。因此，本文献综述的目的是介绍团队运动中用于管理认知负荷的策略，以及用于此类命题的指标及其在特定情境中的关系。
review_content_zh: 审稿人2（Kristy Martin）感谢您的审阅和建议。基本报告总体评论：审稿人称赞作者们探讨了如此重要的话题。正如引言中所说，认知负荷已知会影响身体表现，然而在考虑运动训练负荷时，其存在几乎从未被承认。此外，我不知道有任何文献旨在解决这一问题。话虽如此，当前状态下有几处问题削弱了这项重要工作。一个普遍的问题是，您文献检索的结果，即旨在评估认知负荷的工具和认知负荷的“指标”，直到引言的最后才被讨论，且未详细阐述。由于这构成了您手稿的主要部分，我建议增加对此的关注。请参阅以下我的具体评论。非常感谢这一评论。我们在下方回应了所有建议。您的评论使这篇文章变得更好。具体评论：第36-37行——不清楚为什么变向和认知要求被放在一起？变向不也和上文提到的跳跃或加速一样是体力任务吗？我们同意。变向是一个物理和机械任务，它应该和跳跃或加速放在同一句中。所以我们已经修改了。见第36-37行。第37行——我建议您要么为“认知要求和变向也被识别……”这句话提供参考文献，要么删除“被识别为”这几个字。同意。我们已经删除了“被识别为”。第43-55行——我喜欢这一部分。这段写得很好，说明了这个话题的重要性。非常感谢这一评论，我们非常感激。第53行——“定义”在这里不是正确的术语。像“得出结论”这样的词会更合适。谢谢。我们已经将“正确”改为“得出结论”。第56-57行——这是您为本次综述定义的认知负荷吗？如果是，我建议在这句话中更明确地表达。是的，这对我们来说是认知负荷的定义。我们添加了“我们认为……”以使其更明确。见第58-59行。第60-62行——我同意作者在这一点的看法；然而，不清楚这与认知负荷有何关系。这一概念可以进一步解释。为了进一步解释认知负荷与情感方面的关系，添加了“这些情绪的调节涉及个体影响其情绪的过程。这些过程需要努力，从而消耗认知资源（Schmeichel, 2007）”这句话及其相应的引用。见第61-66行。第68-70行——这句话不清楚。请重写。我们已经重写了这句话。“这种认知需求结合内部和外部负荷的影响，可能导致对建议负荷的适应不良或排斥。” 这将直接影响运动员在身体和/或心理上是否准备好接受另一个训练刺激，即训练/比赛准备度（Gabbett，2017）。见第72-75行。第81行——准备度的术语/概念仅在此处引入。建议提前引入并解释该术语的含义。谢谢，我们同意您的观点。我们使用了前一句的修改（第68-70行），以便更好地描述这一术语。第86-89行——读到此处，我不确定综述的目标是什么。这些目标能否提前引入，或者前文部分能否更明确地引出目标？此外，“指标”一词的含义不明确。对此进行解释，和/或提供一个例子将增加清晰度。非常感谢您的评论。文本已根据您的意见进行了修改，见第47-49行、89-92行。实验设计 方法部分需要更多细节，以及一些方法决策的背景或理由，例如：第93行——为什么文献搜索仅限于1970年以后的文献？谢谢。我们旨在从这一点提供并行的资源。第106行——能否更详细地解释“认知、心理或心理负荷的管理”是什么意思？感谢这一评论。为了更好地理解，我们添加了第114-116行。第112行——什么是“真实运动”？感谢您的评论。这一概念翻译不当。现在已更正为：“个人运动和远离运动现实的研究被排除，以及在实验室情况下的分析”。见第119行。筛选过程是怎样的，例如：是一位作者筛选所有文章，还是团队共同完成？感谢您的评论。筛选过程已包含在第121-126行和流程图中。研究结果的有效性 研究结果虽然有趣且有效，但在结果/讨论部分需要更多背景信息。所包含的广泛研究，例如：不同运动、不同研究目标等，使得难以跟踪、综合或比较不同研究的结果。文本中需要对引用的研究进行更详细的描述，而不仅仅是在表格中。此外，讨论部分主要描述了用于评估认知负荷的工具。这对读者并不特别有益，反而讨论这类测量的优缺点可能更有用。讨论部分也将受益于彻底的校对和编辑。感谢您的评论。为了更广泛地解释所引用的文章，以下行已修改：47-49、89-92、133-139、142-149、195-199、308-315、317-324。第121-123行——如前所述，需要解释“指标”的含义以及您对指标的分类。非常感谢您的评论。 文本已根据其进行修改，见第47-49行、第89-92行、第133-139行。第126-127行——这句话需要更多的解释和上下文。谢谢。我们已经进一步发展了这一段落。见第142-149行。第129行——我不明白“响应指标分析”是什么意思。谢谢你的评论。在更广泛地解释了指标和三种类型的指标后，我们希望这句话不再脱离上下文。第144行——这项研究是实验室研究吗？实验室研究是排除标准之一。似乎包含了一些实验室研究，例如Smith（2016）。Alarcón等人2017年和2018年的这两项研究不是实验室研究。正如你在表1中所看到的，Alarcón等人2018年的研究是在足球特定情境中进行的，而Alarcón等人2017年的研究是在篮球特定情境中进行的。Smith等人2016年的研究也是如此。这是一项分析心理疲劳在足球特定测试中影响的研究。第153行——不需要“量表”这个词。VAS中的S就是量表。我们已经删除了“量表”这个词。第161行——“参考文献”这个词在这里正确吗？我们相信是的，意思是这个指标在文献中广泛用于描述疲劳和缺乏能量。第166-173行——这一部分实际上并没有讨论VAS，而这部分内容属于VAS的子标题。谢谢你的评论，你让我们看到文本中并不清楚仍在讨论VAS指标。为了明确这一点，已做了相关修改。见第183-190行。第177行——CSAI代表什么？你完全正确。缺少了缩写的含义。已在括号中注明‘CSAI-2（竞技状态焦虑量表2）’。第184-188行——这一部分需要更多解释。例如，什么是躯体焦虑和认知焦虑。已扩展解释，定义了躯体焦虑和认知焦虑（第195-199行）。‘认知焦虑指主体对其表现及结果后果的负面感受。而躯体焦虑则指对焦虑的生理指标如肌肉紧张、心率加快、出汗和胃部不适的感知’。第192行——首次使用时拼写POMS的全称。同意。我们已在首次使用时拼写了POMS。第203行——更改“在一项研究中...”。在什么研究中？为错误道歉，这里有打字错误。你所指的研究是Mashiko等人（2004）的研究。‘在一项研究中’已替换为‘在他们的研究中’。第237行——这一陈述的参考文献？已正确引用这一陈述。第244行——首次使用SIATE这一缩写时需要全称。同意。我们已在首次使用时全称SIATE，以及VSC。第285行——是我们还是其他作者？抱歉，这是打字错误。 这些结果是来自其他作者的。已更改为“未发现显著差异”。见第302行。第294-295行——身体疲劳也可能增加反应时间。感谢您的评论。我们通过引用新文章并扩展可能影响反应时间的参数，更深入地探讨了这一主题。见第308-315行。第297-301行——在这里和其他地方，这些研究需要描述。如果没有更详细的解释或背景，这些信息毫无价值。感谢您的评论。研究已更加详细。见第317-324行。结论引入了大量新信息。结论通常是对之前陈述的信息进行总结。我也建议在结论之前设置实际应用部分。感谢您的评论。我们按照PeerJ上发表的叙事综述的风格安排了这一顺序。

paper_title: Technological tools for the measurement of sensory characteristics in food: A review
paper_abstract: The use of technological tools, in the food industry, has allowed a quick and reliable identification and measurement of the sensory characteristics of food matrices is of great importance, since they emulate the functioning of the five senses (smell, taste, sight, touch, and hearing). Therefore, industry and academia have been conducting research focused on developing and using these instruments which is evidenced in various studies that have been reported in the scientific literature. In this review, several of these technological tools are documented, such as the e-nose, e-tongue, colorimeter, artificial vision systems, and instruments that allow texture measurement (texture analyzer, electromyography, others). These allow us to carry out processes of analysis, review, and evaluation of food to determine essential characteristics such as quality, composition, maturity, authenticity, and origin. The determination of these characteristics allows the standardization of food matrices, achieving the improvement of existing foods and encouraging the development of new products that satisfy the sensory experiences of the consumer, driving growth in the food sector. However, the tools discussed have some limitations such as acquisition cost, calibration and maintenance cost, and in some cases, they are designed to work with a specific food matrix.
review_content:
The manuscript "Technological Tools for Sensory Analysis in the Food Industry" provides an overview of various technological tools used in the food industry to measure and analyze sensory characteristics of food products. The paper covers electronic nose, electronic tongue, artificial vision systems, texture analyzers, electromyographic analysis, and acoustic analysis.

This present manuscript provides a valuable overview of technological tools used for sensory analysis in the food industry. It offers practical insights into how these tools can be applied to assess various sensory attributes of food products. However, it would benefit from a more critical evaluation of the limitations and challenges associated with these tools and a discussion of recent advancements in the field. Additionally, a deeper exploration of data analysis methods would enhance the paper's utility for researchers and practitioners in the food industry.

This article does not demonstrate an innovative character. There are several reviews already published in this area. This manuscript should draw attention to real innovations and aspects that have not yet been addressed in the literature.

Below I detail some positive aspects of the review, but also some points that must be improved so that this manuscript can be accepted.

The paper provides a comprehensive overview of various technological tools used in sensory analysis in the food industry. It covers a wide range of devices and techniques, including e-nose, e-tongue, artificial vision systems, texture analyzers, electromyographic analysis, and acoustic analysis. This comprehensive coverage is valuable for readers interested in understanding the diversity of tools available for sensory analysis.

This manuscript is well-structured, with each section dedicated to a specific technological tool. This organization makes it easy for readers to navigate and find information on each tool separately. Additionally, the internal structure and applications of each tool are described in detail, providing a clear understanding of their operation and potential uses.

The authors emphasize the practical applications of these technological tools in the food industry. It highlights how these tools can be used to assess various sensory characteristics such as flavor, texture, and appearance. The practical examples and applications mentioned in the paper demonstrate the real-world utility of these tools for quality control and product development.

However, the authors should provide a wealth of information on the various tools, it lacks critical evaluation and discussion of their limitations and challenges. A review should not only highlight the strengths but also address potential weaknesses and constraints associated with the use of these tools. For instance, the paper does not discuss the cost, maintenance requirements, and calibration challenges that may arise when implementing these tools in food production settings. The manuscript does not discuss recent advancements and developments in the field of sensory analysis technology. Given the rapid pace of technological innovation, it would be beneficial to include information on any emerging tools or techniques that have been developed since the paper's publication.

Finally, the authors briefly mention some data analysis methods used in conjunction with these tools, such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and machine learning classifiers. However, it would be helpful to provide more in-depth discussions on data analysis techniques and how they are applied to interpret the results obtained from these tools.
paper_title_zh: 食品感官特性测量的技术工具：综述
paper_abstract_zh: 在食品工业中，使用技术工具已实现对食品基质感官特征的快速且可靠的识别和测量，这一点至关重要，因为它们模拟了五种感官（嗅觉、味觉、视觉、触觉和听觉）的功能。因此，工业界和学术界一直在进行专注于开发和利用这些仪器的研究，这在科学文献中报道的诸多研究中得到了证实。在这篇综述中，记录了多种此类技术工具，例如电子鼻、电子舌、色度计、人工视觉系统以及允许进行质地测量的仪器（质地分析仪、肌电图仪等）。这些工具使我们能够对食品进行分析、审查和评估，以确定其关键特征，如质量、成分、成熟度、真实性和来源。确定这些特征有助于食品基质的标准化，实现现有食品的改进，并鼓励开发满足消费者感官体验的新产品，从而推动食品行业的增长。然而，所讨论的工具存在一些局限性，如购置成本、校准和维护成本，以及在某些情况下，它们被设计为仅适用于特定的食品基质。
review_content_zh:
《食品工业中感官分析的技术工具》手稿概述了食品工业中用于测量和分析食品产品感官特性的各种技术工具。该论文涵盖了电子鼻、电子舌、人工视觉系统、质地分析仪、肌电图分析和声学分析。

本文提供了食品工业中用于感官分析的技术工具的有价值概述。它提供了关于如何将这些工具应用于评估食品产品各种感官属性的实用见解。然而，如果能更批判性地评估这些工具的局限性和挑战，并讨论该领域的最新进展，将更有益。此外，深入探讨数据分析方法将增强该论文对食品工业研究人员和从业者的实用性。

本文未展示创新性。该领域已发表多篇综述。本文应关注真正的创新和文献中尚未涉及的方面。

以下我详细列出该综述的一些积极方面，以及为使本文得以接受而必须改进的一些要点。

该论文全面概述了食品工业中感官分析使用的各种技术工具。涵盖了广泛的设备和技术，包括电子鼻、电子舌、人工视觉系统、质地分析仪、肌电图分析和声学分析。这种全面的覆盖对于有兴趣了解感官分析工具多样性的读者非常有价值。

本文结构良好，每个部分专门介绍一种特定的技术工具。这种组织方式使读者易于导航并分别查找每种工具的信息。此外，每种工具的内部结构和应用都进行了详细描述，清晰地展示了其操作和潜在用途。

作者强调了这些技术工具在食品工业中的实际应用。突出了如何使用这些工具评估各种感官特性，如风味、质地和外观。文中提到的实际示例和应用展示了这些工具在质量控制和产品开发中的现实效用。

然而，尽管作者提供了关于各种工具的大量信息，但缺乏对其局限性和挑战的批判性评估和讨论。综述不仅应突出优势，还应探讨使用这些工具可能带来的潜在弱点和约束。例如，论文未讨论在食品生产环境中实施这些工具可能产生的成本、维护需求和校准挑战。本文未讨论感官分析技术领域的最新进展和发展。鉴于技术创新的快速步伐，包括本文发表以来开发的任何新兴工具或技术将是有益的。

最后，作者简要提及了一些与这些工具结合使用的数据分析方法，如主成分分析（PCA）和机器学习分类器。然而，提供更深入的数据分析技术讨论以及如何应用它们来解释这些工具获得的结果将是有帮助的。

paper_title: Does evidence support the high expectations placed in precision medicine? A bibliographic review
paper_abstract:
Background : Precision medicine is the Holy Grail of interventions that are tailored to a patient’s individual characteristics. However, conventional clinical trials are designed to find differences in averages, and interpreting these differences depends on untestable assumptions. Although only an ideal, a constant effect of treatment would facilitate individual management. A direct consequence of a constant effect is that the variance of the outcome measure would be the same in the treated and control arms. We reviewed the literature to explore the similarity of these variances as a foundation for examining whether and how often precision medicine is definitively required. 
 Methods : We reviewed parallel clinical trials with numerical primary endpoints published in 2004, 2007, 2010 and 2013. We collected the baseline and final standard deviations of the main outcome measure. We assessed homoscedasticity by comparing the variance of the primary endpoint between arms through the outcome variance ratio (treated to control group). 
 Results : The review provided 208 articles with enough information to conduct the analysis. One out of five studies (n = 40, 19.2%) had statistically different variances between groups, implying a non-constant-effect. The adjusted point estimate of the mean outcome variance ratio (treated to control group) is 0.89 (95% CI 0.81 to 0.97). 
 Conclusions : The mean variance ratio is significantly lower than 1 and the lower variance was found more often in the intervention group than in the control group, suggesting it is more usual for treated patients to be stable. This observed reduction in variance might also imply that there could be a subgroup of less ill patients who derive no benefit from treatment. This would require further study as to whether the treatment effect outweighs the side effects as well as the economic costs. We have shown that there are ways to analyze the apparently unobservable constant effect.
review_content:
This paper makes an important point and goes some way to tempering the high expectations placed on precision medicine.

Have the authors shown that the comparison of variances is a useful but not definitive tool for assessing whether or not the assumption of a constant effect holds? I think they have.

Would more data be useful? I think it would. The paper could be misinterpreted as an attack on precision medicine. This is unfair. In this version, the authors have tempered their conclusions in an appropriate manner. The study is based on just 208 of the eligible studies. It seems likely that studies permitting the analysis are a select subset of the studies available. And, given the uncertainties surrounding estimates of variance components, it seems not unreasonable to assume that not all studies were equally likely to have detected differences in outcome variance. However, the authors have defined a method and a process permitting evidence in support of precision medicine to be discussed rationally.
paper_title_zh: "证据是否支持对精准医疗的高期望？——文献综述"
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：精准医学是针对患者个体特征量身定制的干预措施的“圣杯”。然而，传统的临床试验旨在发现平均差异，而这些差异的解释依赖于无法验证的假设。尽管只是一个理想状态，但治疗效果的恒定将有助于个体管理。恒定效果的直接后果是，治疗组和对照组的结局测量方差相同。我们回顾了文献，探讨这些方差的相似性，作为检验精准医学是否以及多常被明确需要的基石。

方法：我们回顾了2004年、2007年、2010年和2013年发表的具有数值主要终点的平行临床试验。我们收集了主要结局指标的基线和最终标准差。通过比较治疗组与对照组主要终点方差的结果方差比（治疗组与对照组），评估同方差性。

结果：回顾提供了208篇包含足够信息进行分析的文章。五分之一的研究（n = 40，19.2%）在组间存在统计学上不同的方差，意味着效果非恒定。调整后的平均结局方差比（治疗组与对照组）的点估计为0.89（95% CI 0.81至0.97）。

结论：平均方差比显著低于1，且干预组比对照组更常出现较低方差，表明治疗患者的稳定性更为常见。观察到的方差减少也可能意味着存在一个病情较轻的患者亚组，他们从治疗中未获得益处。这需要进一步研究，以确定治疗效果是否超过副作用和经济成本。我们已经证明，有方法可以分析看似不可观察的恒定效果。
review_content_zh:
本文提出了一个重要观点，并在一定程度上缓和了对精准医疗的高期望。

作者是否已经证明，方差比较是评估恒定效应假设是否成立的有用但非决定性工具？我认为他们已经证明了。

更多的数据会有用吗？我认为会有用。该论文可能被误解为对精准医疗的攻击。这是不公平的。在这个版本中，作者适当地缓和了他们的结论。该研究仅基于208项符合条件的研究。似乎允许分析的研究是可用研究的一个精选子集。而且，鉴于方差分量估计的不确定性，假设并非所有研究都同样可能检测到结果方差差异似乎并非不合理。然而，作者已经定义了一种方法和过程，允许理性地讨论支持精准医疗的证据。

reasons: The study is based on just 208 of the eligible studies.
This paper makes an important point and goes some way to tempering the high expectations placed on precision medicine.
Have the authors shown that the comparison of variances is a useful but not definitive tool for assessing whether or not the assumption of a constant effect holds?
I think they have.
However, the authors have defined a method and a process permitting evidence in support of precision medicine to be discussed rationally.
Would more data be useful? I think it would.

And, given the uncertainties surrounding estimates of variance components, it seems not unreasonable to assume that not all studies were equally likely to have detected differences in outcome variance.

paper_title: Why do proteins aggregate? “Intrinsically insoluble proteins” and “dark mediators” revealed by studies on “insoluble proteins” solubilized in pure water
paper_abstract: In 2008, I reviewed and proposed a model for our discovery in 2005 that unrefoldable and insoluble proteins could in fact be solubilized in unsalted water. Since then, this discovery has offered us and other groups a powerful tool to characterize insoluble proteins, and we have further addressed several fundamental and disease-relevant issues associated with this discovery. Here I review these results, which are conceptualized into several novel scenarios. 1) Unlike 'misfolded proteins', which still retain the capacity to fold into well-defined structures but are misled to 'off-pathway' aggregation, unrefoldable and insoluble proteins completely lack this ability and will unavoidably aggregate in vivo with ~150 mM ions, thus designated as 'intrinsically insoluble proteins (IIPs)' here. IIPs may largely account for the 'wastefully synthesized' DRiPs identified in human cells. 2) The fact that IIPs including membrane proteins are all soluble in unsalted water, but get aggregated upon being exposed to ions, logically suggests that ions existing in the background play a central role in mediating protein aggregation, thus acting as 'dark mediators'. Our study with 14 salts confirms that IIPs lack the capacity to fold into any well-defined structures. We uncover that salts modulate protein dynamics and anions bind proteins with high selectivity and affinity, which is surprisingly masked by pre-existing ions. Accordingly, I modified my previous model. 3) Insoluble proteins interact with lipids to different degrees. Remarkably, an ALS-causing P56S mutation transforms the β-sandwich MSP domain into a helical integral membrane protein. Consequently, the number of membrane-interacting proteins might be much larger than currently recognized. To attack biological membranes may represent a common mechanism by which aggregated proteins initiate human diseases. 4) Our discovery also implies a solution to the 'chicken-and-egg paradox' for the origin of primitive membranes embedded with integral membrane proteins, if proteins originally emerged in unsalted prebiotic media.
review_content: This is a very lengthy review on the contributions of dissolved ions to the behavior (aggregation, membrane interaction) of proteins. It is rather long and rambling (and seems somewhat repetitive) and may be construed to some extent as “propaganda” for the author’s opinion in this case. There also does seem to be quite a lot of primary data, ie, data appearing in this review that have not received peer review in other journals. However, on balance, the review is interesting, and should spark dialogue if not controversy in the scientific community.
paper_title_zh: 为什么蛋白质会聚集？“内在不溶性蛋白质”和“暗中介物”通过研究在纯水中溶解的“不溶性蛋白质”得以揭示
paper_abstract_zh: 2008年，我回顾并提出了一个模型，解释了我们在2005年的发现，即不可复性和不溶性蛋白质实际上可以在无盐水中溶解。自那时起，这一发现为我们和其他研究组提供了一种强大的工具来表征不溶性蛋白质，并且我们进一步解决了与这一发现相关的几个基本和疾病相关的问题。在此，我回顾了这些结果，并将其概念化为几个新的情景。1）与“错误折叠蛋白质”不同，后者仍保留折叠成明确定义结构的能力，但被误导至“偏离途径”的聚集，不可复性和不溶性蛋白质完全缺乏这种能力，并且在体内不可避免地与约150 mM的离子聚集，因此在此被指定为“内在不溶性蛋白质（IIPs）”。IIPs可能在很大程度上解释了在人类细胞中识别的“浪费合成的”DRiPs。2）包括膜蛋白在内的IIPs在无盐水中均可溶，但在暴露于离子时会发生聚集，这逻辑上表明背景中存在的离子在介导蛋白质聚集方面起着核心作用，从而充当“暗中介者”。我们对14种盐的研究证实，IIPs缺乏折叠成任何明确定义结构的能力。我们发现盐调节蛋白质动态，并且阴离子以高选择性和亲和力结合蛋白质，这一现象被预先存在的离子掩盖。因此，我修改了我之前的模型。3）不溶性蛋白质与脂质的相互作用程度不同。值得注意的是，一个导致ALS的P56S突变将β-三明治MSP结构域转变为螺旋型整合膜蛋白。因此，与膜相互作用的蛋白质数量可能比目前认识到的要多得多。攻击生物膜可能是聚集蛋白质引发人类疾病的共同机制。4）我们的发现还暗示了解决“先有鸡还是先有蛋悖论”的方案，即原始膜与整合膜蛋白的起源，如果蛋白质最初出现在无盐的前生物介质中。
review_content_zh: 这是一篇关于溶解离子对蛋白质行为（聚集、膜相互作用）贡献的非常冗长的综述。文章相当长且杂乱（并且似乎有些重复），在某种程度上可能被视为作者观点的“宣传”。此外，确实似乎有大量原始数据，即在此综述中出现但未在其他期刊经过同行评审的数据。然而，总体而言，这篇综述是有趣的，即使不在科学界引起争议，也应当引发讨论。

It is rather long and rambling (and seems somewhat repetitive) and may be construed to some extent as “propaganda” for the author’s opinion in this case.

paper_title: The role of salivary contents and modern technologies in the remineralization of dental enamel: a narrative review
paper_abstract: Human enamel once formed cannot be biologically repaired or replaced. Saliva has a significant role in remineralization of dental enamel. It not only has a buffering capacity to neutralize the oral cavity’s low pH generated after acidic encounters, but also acts as a carrier of essential ions, such as fluoride, calcium and phosphate, which have a positive role in enamel’s remineralization. This review discusses how salivary contents, like proteins and enzymes, have a natural role in enamel’s mineralization. In addition, the presence of ions, such as fluoride, calcium and phosphate, in saliva further enhances its capability to remineralize the demineralized enamel surface. The review further examines modern innovative technologies, based on biomimetic regeneration systems, including dentin phosphoproteins, aspartate-serine-serine, recombinant porcine amelogenin, leucine-rich amelogenin peptide and nano-hydroxyapatite, that promote enamel remineralization. Fluoride boosters like calcium phosphates, polyphosphates, and certain natural products can also play an important role in enamel remineralization.
review_content:
It is a well-written article. The role of salivary contents are comprehensively explained. I would like to suggest the following suggestions:
 1. The inclusion criteria of the articles is a bit confusing. How the research started is well-written but later it is a bit confusing how 500 relevant articles were selected. It would be nice to know how these 500 articles were selected.
 2. Some flow charts, for the selection of the articles for research can be helpful.
 3. Similarly, if there could be a chart, diagram or table before the conclusion, it would help in learning about the article summary.
paper_title_zh: 唾液成分与现代技术在牙釉质再矿化中的作用：叙述性综述
paper_abstract_zh: 人类牙釉质一旦形成，便无法进行生物修复或替换。唾液在牙釉质的再矿化过程中起着重要作用。它不仅具有缓冲能力，可以中和口腔在接触酸性物质后产生的低pH值，还作为必需离子的载体，如氟离子、钙离子和磷酸盐离子，这些离子在牙釉质的再矿化中具有积极作用。本文综述了唾液中的成分，如蛋白质和酶，在牙釉质矿化中的天然作用。此外，唾液中存在的氟离子、钙离子和磷酸盐离子进一步增强了其再矿化脱矿牙釉质表面的能力。本文还探讨了基于仿生再生系统的现代创新技术，包括牙本质磷酸蛋白、天冬氨酸-丝氨酸-丝氨酸、重组猪釉原蛋白、富含亮氨酸的釉原蛋白肽和纳米羟基磷灰石，这些技术能够促进牙釉质的再矿化。氟增强剂如磷酸钙、多磷酸盐以及某些天然产品在牙釉质再矿化中也发挥着重要作用。

paper_title: Mislabeled examples detection viewed as probing machine learning models: concepts, survey and extensive benchmark
paper_abstract: Mislabeled examples are ubiquitous in real-world machine learning datasets, advocating the development of techniques for automatic detection. We show that most mislabeled detection methods can be viewed as probing trained machine learning models using a few core principles. We formalize a modular framework that encompasses these methods, parameterized by only 4 building blocks, as well as a Python library that demonstrates that these principles can actually be implemented. The focus is on classifier-agnostic concepts, with an emphasis on adapting methods developed for deep learning models to non-deep classifiers for tabular data. We benchmark existing methods on (artificial) Completely At Random (NCAR) as well as (realistic) Not At Random (NNAR) labeling noise from a variety of tasks with imperfect labeling rules. This benchmark provides new insights as well as limitations of existing methods in this setup.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This paper considers the problem of detecting mislabeled data and proposes a general framework composed of four modular components that can integrate various existing techniques. The main contribution is a Python library that precisely implements these principles and benchmarks existing methods against both random and non-random label noise across a series of datasets with automated labeling rules. The experiments are conducted fairly to me, and the key findings offer valuable insights for advancing research in this area.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
Strengths: 1. This paper proposes a general framework for noisy label detection that can integrate various existing techniques. The Python implementation provides valuable support for research in this field. 2. The empirical studies are thorough, usding various benchmark datasets, and the findings are convincing. Weaknesses: 1. The proposed framework follows a basic procedure for noisy label detection. While the empirical findings are valuable, the theoretical contribution is somewhat limited. Additionally, the ensemble module is primarily an engineering solution rather than a novel theoretical advancement. 2. The experiments are primarily conducted on benchmark datasets with artificially generated label noise. The performance of the proposed method with different modules remains unclear on real-world noisy labeled datasets, such as the Animal10N dataset [1]. [1] Song, H., Kim, M., and Lee, J., "SELFIE: Refurbishing Unclean Samples for Robust Deep Learning," In Proc. 36th Int'l Conf. on Machine Learning (ICML), Long Beach, California, June 2019

**Requested Changes:**
It is recommended to test the proposed framework on real-world datasets with noisy labels, such as the Animal10N dataset, to strengthen the applicability of this work in practical scenarios.

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes
paper_title_zh: 将错标样本检测视为探测机器学习模型：概念、综述及广泛基准测试
paper_abstract_zh: 错标样本在现实世界的机器学习数据集中普遍存在，这促使了自动检测技术的发展。我们表明，大多数错标检测方法可以被视为利用少数核心原理对训练好的机器学习模型进行探测。我们形式化了一个模块化框架，该框架包含这些方法，仅由4个构建模块参数化，并开发了一个Python库，展示了这些原理实际上是可以实现的。重点在于分类器无关的概念，特别强调将针对深度学习模型开发的方法适配到非深度分类器，用于表格数据。我们在（人工的）完全随机（NCAR）以及（现实的）非随机（NNAR）标签噪声的各种任务上对现有方法进行了基准测试，这些任务具有不完美的标签规则。该基准测试提供了对现有方法的新见解以及在此设置中的局限性。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文探讨了检测错误标记数据的问题，并提出了一个由四个模块化组件组成的通用框架，该框架可以整合各种现有技术。主要贡献是一个精确实现这些原则的Python库，并对现有方法在一系列具有自动标记规则的数据集上进行了随机和非随机标签噪声的基准测试。在我看来，实验进行得公平，关键发现为推进该领域的研究提供了宝贵的见解。

**优点和缺点：**
优点：1. 本文提出了一个用于噪声标签检测的通用框架，可以整合各种现有技术。Python实现为该领域的研究提供了宝贵支持。2. 实证研究全面，使用了各种基准数据集，发现具有说服力。
缺点：1. 所提出的框架遵循噪声标签检测的基本程序。尽管实证发现有价值，但理论贡献相对有限。此外，集成模块主要是一个工程解决方案，而非新颖的理论进展。2. 实验主要在具有人工生成标签噪声的基准数据集上进行。在不同模块下，所提出方法在真实世界噪声标记数据集（如Animal10N数据集[1]）上的性能仍不清楚。[1] Song, H., Kim, M., and Lee, J., "SELFIE: Refurbishing Unclean Samples for Robust Deep Learning," In Proc. 36th Int'l Conf. on Machine Learning (ICML), Long Beach, California, June 2019

**建议的修改：**
建议在具有噪声标签的真实世界数据集（如Animal10N数据集）上测试所提出的框架，以加强该工作在实际场景中的适用性。

**声明和证据：**
是

**受众：**
是
